970	=== how-captions-work
971	---
972	title: "Captions are text clips"
973	description: "How captions behave in Frame Job: ordinary text clips on a track of their own, burned into the picture, with the same few rules however they were made."
974	---
975	
976	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
977	
978	Every caption in Frame Job is an ordinary text clip on a track of its own. That one fact explains most of how captions behave: where they show up, how you change them, and what happens to them in an export.
979	
980	<AtAGlance
981	  menu={['File ▸ Import Captions…', 'File ▸ Generate Captions…', 'File ▸ Export Captions…']}
982	  where="Inspector ▸ Clip tab ▸ Text"
983	  tools={['import_captions', 'transcribe', 'export_captions', 'render_frame', 'export']}
984	/>
985	
986	## Get captions in and out
987	
988	Three commands sit next to each other in the **File** menu. None of them has a keyboard shortcut.
989	
990	| Command | What it does |
991	| --- | --- |
992	| [**File ▸ Import Captions…**](/captions/import-captions/) | Reads a SubRip (`.srt`) file onto a new caption track. |
993	| [**File ▸ Generate Captions…**](/captions/generate-captions/) | Transcribes the speech in your clips onto a new caption track. |
994	| [**File ▸ Export Captions…**](/captions/export-captions/) | Writes one track out as SubRip (`.srt`) or WebVTT (`.vtt`). |
995	
996	## Captions are ordinary text clips
997	
998	However a caption gets onto the timeline, it lands the same way: one text clip per caption, on a new track at the front of the stack, so it draws over everything else. An imported caption and a generated one are the same kind of thing afterwards.
999	
1000	So the tools you already use work on them:
1001	
1002	- Drag a caption to retime it.
1003	- Trim its edges, split it or delete it.
1004	- Select a run of captions and restyle them together in the Clip tab, under **Text**.
1005	
1006	[Edit captions](/captions/edit-captions/) covers what's particular to them, such as changing the words on a word caption.
1007	
1008	## Captions burn in with no extra step
1009	
1010	Captions are part of the picture, so the preview, an exported movie and a frame an agent renders all show them. There's nothing to switch on.
1011	
1012	That also means an export always carries them burned in. They aren't a soft-subtitle track that a viewer can turn on and off. If you need that, write a separate subtitle file with [**File ▸ Export Captions…**](/captions/export-captions/).
1013	
1014	## Two kinds of caption: subtitles and word captions
1015	
1016	When you generate captions, the **Style** row chooses the kind.
1017	
1018	| Kind | What you get |
1019	| --- | --- |
1020	| [Subtitles](/captions/subtitles/) | Classic two-line captions. |
1021	| [Word captions](/captions/word-caption-styles/) | Large captions in one of five styles, where the word being said stands out. |
1022	
1023	Speech is recognised [on this Mac](/captions/on-device-transcription/), with nothing uploaded, or [by AssemblyAI](/captions/assemblyai-transcription/) in the cloud, on your own key. Either engine can make either kind.
1024	
1025	An imported file always comes in as plain text in the **Caption** preset, the look subtitles use.
1026	
1027	## Caption track names
1028	
1029	The first caption track is called **Captions**, then **Captions 2**, **Captions 3** and so on, taking the next free number, so you can tell separate runs apart in the track headers.
1030	
1031	The name does some work. **Replace** in [Generate Captions](/captions/restyle-captions/), [**Re-lay Captions for This Canvas**](/captions/re-lay-captions/) and [captions following a speed change](/speed/captions-and-speed/) only touch a track called **Captions** or **Captions** and a number, and only when it holds nothing but text clips. [Rename a track](/timeline/manage-tracks/) to anything else and all three leave it alone.
1032	
1033	## A caption track is never guessed
1034	
1035	Nothing in a project marks a track as the caption track. A name alone doesn't make one, and you can rename a track whenever you like. So a command that writes a caption file shows you the choice instead of assuming.
1036	
1037	Any track can be exported when it has at least one clip, every clip on it is a text clip, and at least one of those clips has text. A track of titles qualifies as well.
1038	
1039	[**File ▸ Export Captions…**](/captions/export-captions/) lists every such track in its **Track** pop-up, front-most first, with the front-most selected. With only one to choose from, the pop-up is greyed. With none, the menu item is greyed.
1040	
1041	An agent has no pop-up to look at. When a project has several such tracks and the agent doesn't name one, `export_captions` won't pick for it, and it replies with the list. With none, it says there are no captions to write.
1042	
1043	## Frame grid and no overlaps
1044	
1045	These rules apply to every caption that's imported or generated.
1046	
1047	- **Times land on frames.** Every caption's start and end snap to the nearest frame of the project, so a caption can come out up to a frame shorter or longer than its source says. A caption that would snap to no length at all gets one frame.
1048	- **Captions on one track never overlap.** When a caption starts before the previous one ends, the earlier one is cut back to meet it, and the run reports how many were shortened.
1049	- **A caption needs at least one frame.** One that would be left shorter than that is skipped and reported.
1050	
1051	## Captions inside a nest
1052	
1053	The caption commands work on the timeline you have open. With a [nest open](/editing/inside-a-nest/):
1054	
1055	- **Import Captions…** and **Generate Captions…** put the new track at the front of the nest.
1056	- **Export Captions…** lists that nest's tracks.
1057	
1058	To caption the main timeline, close the nest first.
1059

1069	=== import-captions
1070	---
1071	title: "Import captions"
1072	description: "Bring a SubRip (.srt) caption file onto the timeline as text clips, and see what Frame Job copes with, removes and reports along the way."
1073	---
1074	
1075	import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
1076	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
1077	
1078	Import Captions reads a SubRip (`.srt`) file onto a new caption track, one text clip per caption, as a single undo step. Use it when someone has already written the captions.
1079	
1080	<AtAGlance menu="File ▸ Import Captions…" tools="import_captions" />
1081	
1082	## Import captions
1083	
1084	<Steps>
1085	
1086	1. Choose **File ▸ Import Captions…**. It has no keyboard shortcut, and it's available whenever the project window has no sheet open.
1087	
1088	2. Pick the file. The open panel reads "Choose a SubRip (.srt) caption file." It accepts `.srt` and any plain-text file, so a SubRip file saved as `.txt` imports too.
1089	
1090	</Steps>
1091	
1092	Each caption becomes one text clip in the [**Caption** preset](/text-and-shapes/text-presets/), on a new track at the front called **Captions**, or the next free number. Undo removes the lot in one step, **Import Captions**. With a [nest](/editing/inside-a-nest/) open, the track goes at the front of the nest.
1093	
1094	A clean import shows no message. If there's anything to tell you, an alert appears when it finishes. See [Malformed entries are reported](#malformed-entries-are-reported).
1095	
1096	## File variations it copes with
1097	
1098	Real SubRip files vary, and Frame Job copes with these variations rather than turning the file away:
1099	
1100	- A UTF-8 byte-order mark.
1101	- Windows (CRLF) or old Mac (bare CR) line endings.
1102	- A missing index line above the timing line.
1103	- A comma or a dot before the milliseconds.
1104	- The `MM:SS` and `SS` shorthands, and up to nine digits after the seconds.
1105	- Position settings after the end time, which are ignored.
1106	- Text in UTF-8, or in UTF-16 with a byte-order mark.
1107	
1108	## What happens to the text
1109	
1110	A text clip holds one plain string, so formatting that can't be kept is removed rather than shown as angle brackets on the canvas.
1111	
1112	| In the file | What happens |
1113	| --- | --- |
1114	| `<i>`, `<b>`, `<u>`, `<font …>` and their closing tags | Removed, along with anything else shaped like a tag: a `<` followed by a letter, or by `/` and a letter, up to the next `>`. |
1115	| `{\an8}`-style overrides | Removed: a `{\` up to the next `}`. |
1116	| `&` `<` `>` `"` `'` `'` ` ` | Decoded to the character they stand for. |
1117	| Text that only looks like a tag, such as `<<` or `a < b` | Stays as text. |
1118	
1119	The file's own line breaks are kept, and long lines also wrap inside the caption box, which is 80% of the canvas width.
1120	
1121	## What happens to the timing
1122	
1123	Every time snaps to the project's frame grid. A caption that starts before the previous one ends cuts the earlier one back to meet it. A caption left shorter than one frame is skipped. [Frame grid and no overlaps](/captions/how-captions-work/#frame-grid-and-no-overlaps) has the rules.
1124	
1125	## Malformed entries are reported
1126	
1127	Frame Job skips an entry it can't read, carries on with the rest, and tells you. Nothing is dropped silently.
1128	
1129	When the import finishes with something to report, an alert headed "Imported 42 captions from “interview.srt”." says how many captions were shortened to fit and lists what was skipped by line number. It shows the first eight, then "…and N more."
1130	
1131	| The alert says | What's wrong with the entry |
1132	| --- | --- |
1133	| no “-->” timing line in this entry | The block has no timing line. |
1134	| “…” is not a HH:MM:SS,mmm time | A time can't be read. A time past 1,000,000 seconds, about 277 hours, counts as unreadable. |
1135	| two “-->” in one timing line | The timing line has more than one arrow. |
1136	| 2 lines before the timing line | More than an index line sits above the timing line. |
1137	| ends at or before it starts | The end time isn't after the start time. |
1138	| no caption text | The entry has timing but no words, or nothing left once markup is removed. |
1139	| starts less than a frame before the next caption | Shortening it to fit would leave it under one frame. |
1140	
1141	On a canvas taller than wide, the alert also says when captions wrap to more than two lines. See [Subtitles](/captions/subtitles/).
1142	
1143	## When a file can't be read
1144	
1145	If not one caption in a file can be read, Frame Job imports nothing and the project doesn't change.
1146	
1147	| The message says | What it means |
1148	| --- | --- |
1149	| No captions could be read from “name.srt”. | Every entry failed. The message gives the first three reasons. |
1150	| “name.srt” could not be read as text. | The file couldn't be opened. |
1151	| “name.srt” holds 5000 captions, more than this project has room for: 900 more clips would fit, out of 4096. | The file would take the project past its 4,096-clip limit. |
1152	
1153	## Good to know
1154	
1155	A caption file comes in through this command, not as media.
1156	
1157	Import reads SubRip only. Frame Job can [export WebVTT](/captions/export-captions/), but it has no way to read a `.vtt` file as WebVTT, so convert one to SubRip first.
1158	
1159	Save a caption file as UTF-8 before you import it. A file in an older encoding such as Windows-1252 or Latin-1 is fine with no accented letters in it, but with them the import usually stops with “No captions could be read”. If one does import, its accented letters may come out wrong.
1160	
1161	## With an agent
1162	
1163	`import_captions` can put the captions on a track that already exists, which the menu can't. Captions that would overlap something on that track are dropped, so leaving it to make a new track is the safer choice. It reports what landed and each malformed entry by line. See [Tools: captions and transcripts](/mcp/tools-captions/).
1164	
1165	## Related

1	=== on-device-transcription
2	---
3	title: "Transcribe on this Mac"
4	description: Turn the speech in your clips into captions with your Mac's own speech engine, with no key, no upload and no length limit, and install the languages you need.
5	---
6	
7	import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
8	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
9	import Shot from '@components/Shot.astro';
10	
11	**On this Mac** is the free engine for [Generate Captions](/captions/generate-captions/). It recognises speech with the engine built into your Mac, so it costs nothing, needs no key, and your audio never leaves the machine.
12	
13	<AtAGlance
14	  menu="File ▸ Generate Captions…"
15	  where="Generate Captions sheet ▸ Engine: ▸ On this Mac"
16	  tools={['transcribe', 'get_transcript']}
17	  needs="The language's speech model, installed on this Mac. No key, and nothing is uploaded."
18	/>
19	
20	## Transcribe on this Mac
21	
22	<Steps>
23	
24	1. Choose **File ▸ Generate Captions…**.
25	
26	2. Set **Engine:** to **On this Mac**. The sheet remembers the engine you chose last.
27	
28	3. Check **Language:**. If it reads "— not installed", [download the language](#download-a-speech-language) first.
29	
30	4. Choose **Generate**.
31	
32	</Steps>
33	
34	<Shot
35	  name="15-generate-captions-sheet.sheet"
36	  alt="The Generate Captions sheet with Language set to English (United States), Engine set to On this Mac, From set to Whole timeline and Style set to Subtitles. The paragraph at the top says the words are recognised on this Mac and nothing is uploaded, and the summary reads 2 clips, 00:00:10.200 of audio."
37	/>
38	
39	The sheet says what it's about to do: "The words are recognised ON THIS MAC and land as ordinary text clips on a track of their own, so they show in the preview and burn into an export with no further step. Nothing is uploaded."
40	
41	Frame Job extracts the part of the media each clip plays, and recognises that. There's no length limit, and macOS shows no permission prompt. The engine reads an extracted audio file and never touches the microphone.
42	
43	[Generate Captions](/captions/generate-captions/) covers the rest of the sheet: which clips to caption, the style and the progress card. The other engine is [AssemblyAI](/captions/assemblyai-transcription/), which runs in the cloud on your own key.
44	
45	## Choose a language
46	
47	**Language:** lists every language this Mac's speech engine supports, by name, so the list differs from Mac to Mac. It opens on your Mac's own language, or the nearest one on the list.
48	
49	A language whose speech model isn't on this Mac reads "— not installed". **Generate** stays greyed until the chosen language is installed.
50	
51	If the engine names no language at all, the pop-up reads **No on-device language** and the note under the summary says "This Mac's speech engine named no language with an on-device speech model. Reopen this sheet to ask it again." Setting **Engine:** to **AssemblyAI** still works in that state.
52	
53	## Download a speech language
54	
55	Speech models are installed per Mac, not per project, and this sheet is the only place Frame Job installs one.
56	
57	<Steps>
58	
59	1. Choose a language marked "— not installed". A **Download** button appears under **Language:**.
60	
61	2. Choose **Download**.
62	
63	3. Wait for the row to finish. It shows a bar and "Downloading *language*…".
64	
65	</Steps>
66	
67	When the download finishes, the language is installed and selected, and **Generate** comes on.
68	
69	The bar moves without a figure until the download reports its size. Only then does the row add a percentage, such as "Downloading French… 40%". It never shows a size.
70	
71	While the download runs:
72	
73	- **Language:** and **Engine:** are locked, and **Generate** stays greyed.
74	- **Download** becomes **Cancel**, which is greyed until the download has started reporting. Choosing it stops the download with no message.
75	- The **Cancel** at the bottom of the sheet closes the sheet and leaves the download running. You lose the bar and the way to stop it.
76	
77	If the download fails, the note reads "The download did not finish:" and gives the reason. The **Download** button is back, so you can try again.
78	
79	## Every run recognises the audio again
80	
81	Nothing is kept between runs for captions made on this Mac. Each run, [restyling](/captions/restyle-captions/) included, recognises the audio from the start. That's free, but it takes the time again.
82	
83	The sheet's preview never shows on-device words either. It shows the first words of a cached [AssemblyAI](/captions/assemblyai-transcription/#reuse-a-transcript) transcript if the clip has one, and "This is how it looks" if not.
84	
85	The [Transcript tab](/captions/transcript-words/) does keep the words it recognises on this Mac, but those are separate, and captions never use them.
86	
87	## The pause note
88	
89	With **On this Mac** chosen and a [word style](/captions/word-caption-styles/) picked, a note under the look boxes reads "On-device words rarely carry a pause; this shows mostly with AssemblyAI." It shows whether or not **Dim in pauses** is ticked.
90	
91	The on-device engine starts each word early, so the word after a pause starts inside the silence, and few gaps are left for [Dim in pauses](/captions/word-caption-looks/) to act on. The look still works, but you'll see it rarely.
92	
93	## With an agent
94	
95	`transcribe` uses this engine by default, whatever the sheet last chose.
96	
97	An agent can't install a language, and `transcribe` never downloads one. A language tag that speech recognition doesn't know stops the call with "check the tag's spelling" and the tags it does know. A tag it knows with no model on this Mac stops the call with "A person has to install it", the steps in this sheet, and the languages that are ready. Nothing changes in either case. `get_transcript` works to the same rules. See [Tools: captions and transcripts](/mcp/tools-captions/).
98

106	=== re-lay-captions
107	---
108	title: Re-lay captions for a canvas
109	description: Page word captions again after a canvas size change, keeping every word you corrected, and find out why a track was left as it was.
110	---
111	
112	import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
113	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
114	
115	[Word captions](/captions/word-caption-styles/#word-caption-pages) are split into pages that fit the canvas they were made on, so a narrower canvas can leave them too wide. Re-lay Captions splits them into pages again for the new width, from the words they already hold.
116	
117	<AtAGlance menu="File ▸ Re-lay Captions for This Canvas" tools="relay_captions" />
118	
119	## Re-lay Captions for This Canvas
120	
121	<Steps>
122	
123	1. [Change the canvas size](/projects/canvas-size/) on the Document tab.
124	
125	2. Choose **File ▸ Re-lay Captions for This Canvas**. It has no keyboard shortcut and no options.
126	
127	3. If a sheet appears, read which tracks were [kept as placed](#tracks-kept-as-placed) and why.
128	
129	</Steps>
130	
131	Frame Job looks at every track named **Captions** or **Captions N** that holds only text clips. A track whose pages are all in one of the five [word styles](/captions/word-caption-styles/), with the same [looks](/captions/word-caption-looks/), is paged again from the words its pages hold. Nothing is transcribed again, so nothing is uploaded or billed.
132	
133	The whole re-lay is one undo step, **Re-lay Captions**.
134	
135	## What a re-lay keeps
136	
137	Every correction you typed is kept, because the new pages are made from the words on the old ones.
138	
139	Each page is paged again inside its own clip, and the new pages take the old track's place:
140	
141	- A page you split, trimmed or moved keeps its words where they are.
142	- Pages are never merged across clips. A re-lay can split a page that's too wide for the new canvas, but a wider canvas won't join short pages together.
143	- Words cut off by a trim stay cut off.
144	- The new pages go on a track with the same name, in the same place in the track stack, hidden and locked if the old one was.
145	
146	The new pages are drawn fresh from the style, so any other change you made to a page goes. That includes a colour, an outline, a size, a position, or an unticked **UPPERCASE**.
147	
148	## Tracks kept as placed
149	
150	A track that can't be re-laid stays exactly as it was. A sheet after the edit names each one and why, under a first line that reads "Re-laid 2 caption tracks for this canvas." or "No caption track was re-laid."
151	
152	Each track gets a line like this:
153	
154	> Caption track "Captions 2" is kept as placed: it holds a page with no word timings.
155	
156	| The reason | What it means |
157	| --- | --- |
158	| it is a matte track | The track is a [matte track](/canvas/matte-tracks/). |
159	| it holds a page with no word timings | It's a [Subtitles](/captions/subtitles/) or imported track, or a page lost its timing because you [changed its number of words](/captions/edit-captions/). |
160	| it holds a page none of whose words starts inside it | A trim or split left a page with no word that begins on it. |
161	| it holds a page in a style Frame Job does not make | You changed a page's font, or an agent changed its word style. |
162	| its pages are in more than one style | Pages on the track differ in style or looks, for example after you moved some from another track. |
163	| *N* captions is more than this project has room for | The new pages would take the project past its limit of 4,096 clips. The sentence says how many more would fit. |
164	
165	No sheet appears when every track was re-laid.
166	
167	To re-wrap a Subtitles track, or a track that lost its timing, generate it again on the new canvas. See [Restyle a caption track](/captions/restyle-captions/).
168	
169	## When it is available, and inside a nest
170	
171	The item is greyed out when:
172	
173	- there's no caption track it can re-lay
174	- a sheet is open
175	- a recording is running
176	
177	So if every caption track is ruled out by a reason in the table above, other than the project's clip limit, the item is greyed out and no sheet tells you why.
178	
179	Inside a [nest](/editing/nests/), it works on the nest's tracks at the nest's size.
180	
181	**File ▸ Make Vertical Version…** does the same for the vertical copy. See [What Make Vertical changes](/framing/vertical-what-changes/).
182	
183	## Good to know
184	
185	- A track with any other name isn't looked at, and the sheet doesn't mention it. Neither is a track that holds a clip other than text.
186	- The item doesn't check whether the canvas changed. Choosing it on the same canvas pages the track again, which still drops the hand changes listed in [What a re-lay keeps](#what-a-re-lay-keeps). Undo brings them back.
187	
188	## With an agent
189	
190	`relay_captions` does the same in the timeline or nest that's open, usually after `set_canvas` changes the size. It takes no arguments, and its result lists the tracks it re-laid and each kept track with its reason. When nothing can be re-laid, the call fails with those reasons, so an agent can tell you why the menu item is greyed out. See [Tools: captions and transcripts](/mcp/tools-captions/).

199	=== restyle-captions
200	---
201	title: Restyle a caption track
202	description: Switch a caption track to another word style or look by generating it again, or change the font and backdrop of a run of captions in the inspector.
203	---
204	
205	import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
206	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
207	
208	There are two ways to restyle captions, depending on what you want to change. A word style and its looks are set when the captions are generated, so changing those means generating again. Font, outline and backdrop are ordinary text settings, which you can change on a run of captions in the inspector.
209	
210	<AtAGlance
211	  menu="File ▸ Generate Captions…"
212	  where={['The Generate Captions sheet ▸ Replace:', 'Clip tab ▸ Text']}
213	  tools={['transcribe', 'set_text']}
214	/>
215	
216	## Restyle by generating again
217	
218	<Steps>
219	
220	1. Choose **File ▸ Generate Captions…** and set **From:** to the same clips.
221	
222	2. Set **Style:** to the new word style and tick any [looks](/captions/word-caption-looks/).
223	
224	3. Tick **Replace: existing captions**. The line under it names each track it will remove, with its caption count, for example "Replaces “Captions” (12 captions)."
225	
226	4. Choose **Generate**.
227	
228	</Steps>
229	
230	The old tracks are removed and the new one takes their place at the front of the stack, all in one undo step, **Generate Captions**. The new track takes the first free name, so a lone **Captions** track is replaced by another called **Captions**.
231	
232	What it costs depends on the engine:
233	
234	- **AssemblyAI:** the cached transcript is reused whatever style you ask for, so nothing is uploaded and nothing is billed. That holds while the language, **Speakers:** and **Vocabulary:** match the transcript and **Transcribe again:** stays unticked. See [Transcribe with AssemblyAI](/captions/assemblyai-transcription/).
235	- **On this Mac:** the audio is recognised again. It's free, but it takes the time again.
236	
237	:::caution
238	New pages are made from the transcript, not from the old track. Words you corrected, pages you split or trimmed, and anything you restyled by hand go with the old track. To page a track again and keep your corrections, use [Re-lay Captions](/captions/re-lay-captions/) instead.
239	:::
240	
241	## Which tracks Replace may remove
242	
243	**Replace:** is available only for a word style, and only when there's a track it may replace. It's greyed out with Subtitles chosen. When it isn't available, it's unticked and the line under it is hidden.
244	
245	A track qualifies when:
246	
247	- it's named **Captions** or **Captions N**, such as **Captions 2**. A track you renamed doesn't qualify.
248	- it holds at least one clip, and only text clips.
249	- every one of those clips overlaps a clip being transcribed.
250	
251	The last rule is about the whole track. If even one caption on it sits outside what **From:** covers, the track is left alone and **Replace:** won't list it. Choosing a wider **From:** can bring it in.
252	
253	The old track's style doesn't matter, so **Replace:** also swaps out a Subtitles track or an [imported](/captions/import-captions/) one that meets these rules.
254	
255	## Change a run of captions together
256	
257	To change the font, outline or backdrop and leave the word style alone, select the captions and use the inspector.
258	
259	<Steps>
260	
261	1. [Select the captions](/timeline/selecting-clips/) on the timeline.
262	
263	2. Open the **Clip** tab and its **Text** sub-tab.
264	
265	3. Change what you need under [**Font**, **Style**](/text-and-shapes/text-style/), [**Outline**, **Backdrop**](/text-and-shapes/text-outline-and-backdrop/) or [**Box**](/text-and-shapes/text-box/).
266	
267	</Steps>
268	
269	Each page keeps its own words and word timing. Its word style stays too: the highlight colour, the pop and the pill only change by generating again, or through an agent. See [Word colours](/captions/word-caption-looks/#word-colours).
270	
271	:::note
272	A change of typeface on a word caption page, which a text preset also makes, means Re-lay Captions no longer recognises its track and [keeps it as placed](/captions/re-lay-captions/#tracks-kept-as-placed).
273	:::
274	
275	## Good to know
276	
277	- **Replace:** always opens unticked. The sheet doesn't remember it.
278	- A hidden or locked caption track is replaced like any other, and the new track is visible and unlocked.
279	- If you cancel a run, nothing is placed and the old tracks stay.
280	- If one file can't be transcribed, the captions from the other files are still placed and the old tracks still go, so the captions over that file's clips are lost. Undo brings them back.
281	- To go from a word style back to Subtitles, generate the Subtitles track, then [remove the old one](/timeline/manage-tracks/). **Replace:** isn't available for that.
282	- With a [nest](/editing/nests/) open, the sheet works on that nest's tracks.
283	
284	## With an agent
285	
286	`transcribe` restyles the same way with `replace`, as long as it asks for a word style and places the captions. An agent can also change a placed page's word style directly with `set_text`, which keeps your corrected words. See [Word colours](/captions/word-caption-looks/#with-an-agent).
287

295	=== shorten-pauses
296	---
297	title: "Shorten a pause"
298	description: Spot long pauses in the Transcript tab and tighten them, keeping 0.2 s at each end and closing the gap on every unlocked track.
299	---
300	
301	import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
302	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
303	
304	The Transcript tab marks each long pause in the speech. Click one and delete it to tighten the pause without taking any words, as one undo step.
305	
306	<AtAGlance
307	  menu={['Edit ▸ Delete', 'Edit ▸ Ripple Delete']}
308	  keys={['⌫', '⌦', '⌘⌫']}
309	  where="Inspector ▸ Transcript"
310	  tools={['get_timeline_transcript', 'ripple_delete_ranges', 'set_range']}
311	  needs="Words in the Transcript tab, and the voice model, which runs on your Mac with no key and no upload."
312	/>
313	
314	## Pauses in the transcript
315	
316	Where the speech stops for more than a second between two words of one clip, the transcript shows the pause's length in grey after the word before it, such as `[2.4 s]`.
317	
318	The length is what the voice model hears as silence between that word and the next. The model is the one [Remove Silences](/cleanup/remove-silences/) uses. It runs when the project opens the file, so a file's pauses appear once it has finished. They appear for words from an [AssemblyAI transcript](/captions/assemblyai-transcription/) as well as words read on this Mac.
319	
320	That second is measured as the clip plays on the timeline, so a clip's speed changes what counts. A 0.8 s silence in a clip slowed to half speed plays for 1.6 s, and shows as a pause.
321	
322	## Select a pause
323	
324	Click the pause. It's selected on its own, the part that would go becomes the timeline's [in/out range](/timeline/in-out-range/), and the playhead moves to the start of that cut. To hear what would go, turn on [Loop](/timeline/loop/).
325	
326	<kbd>⎋</kbd> clears the selection and the range. Dragging, <kbd>⇧</kbd> and <kbd>⌘A</kbd> select words only, so a pause is always selected by clicking it.
327	
328	## Delete the pause
329	
330	<Steps>
331	
332	1. Choose **View ▸ Transcript** (<kbd>⌃⌘T</kbd>) to open the Transcript tab.
333	
334	2. Click the pause, the grey length in the text.
335	
336	3. Press <kbd>⌫</kbd>.
337	
338	</Steps>
339	
340	The pause is shortened, keeping 0.2 s at each end, and the gap closes on every unlocked track, as one undo step named **Delete Pause**. A `[2.4 s]` pause loses about 2 s and leaves about 0.4 s. The range clears and the playhead lands where the cut was.
341	
342	<kbd>⌦</kbd>, <kbd>⌘⌫</kbd>, **Edit ▸ Delete** and **Edit ▸ Ripple Delete** do the same, as long as the transcript text has the keyboard.
343	
344	The cut lands on whole frames and never takes the start of a word.
345	
346	The tab won't cut a pause when a locked track has words inside the cut, or when the cut would pass the limit of 4,096 clips. It beeps and shows the same [reason](/captions/delete-words/#when-the-tab-wont-cut) it gives for words, at the foot of the inspector.
347	
348	## When a pause isn't shown
349	
350	The tab shows a pause only when it can cut it cleanly. There's no pause marked:
351	
352	- between two clips, including the two halves of a clip you've split
353	- when either word next to it is [faint](/captions/delete-words/#words-that-cant-be-cut): inside a nest, under a transition or on a locked track
354	- when a word on another track, one the tab shows, reaches into the part that would go, because the cut would take that word
355	- when a clip whose words haven't been read yet starts inside the cut
356	- when keeping 0.2 s at each end would leave nothing to cut
357	
358	## With an agent
359	
360	`get_timeline_transcript` reads the same pauses, each with the range the tab would cut it by, and one `ripple_delete_ranges` call shortens one. `set_range` can shade that range first. An agent can pass several in that call, which makes them one undo step. See [Tools: captions and transcripts](/mcp/tools-captions/).
361	
362	## Related

367	- [Remove Silences](/cleanup/remove-silences/)

369	=== subtitles
370	---
371	title: Subtitles
372	description: Turn speech into classic two-line captions, give each speaker a colour, and see how the Caption preset sizes and places them on any canvas.
373	---
374	
375	import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
376	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
377	import Shot from '@components/Shot.astro';
378	
379	The Subtitles style turns speech into classic two-line cues, the kind you'd see on a film or a broadcast. Each cue is a text clip in the **Caption** preset.
380	
381	<AtAGlance
382	  menu="File ▸ Generate Captions…"
383	  where="The Generate Captions sheet ▸ Style: ▸ Subtitles"
384	  tools="transcribe"
385	  needs="Speaker colours need AssemblyAI."
386	/>
387	
388	<Shot
389	  name="15-generate-captions-sheet.sheet"
390	  alt="The Generate Captions sheet with Style set to Subtitles. The three look checkboxes and Replace are greyed out, and the preview shows “This is how it looks” in small white text on a dark backdrop."
391	/>
392	
393	## Make subtitles
394	
395	<Steps>
396	
397	1. Choose **File ▸ Generate Captions…**.
398	
399	2. Set **Language:**, **Engine:** and **From:**. [Generate Captions](/captions/generate-captions/) explains each one.
400	
401	3. Set **Style:** to **Subtitles**. The sheet opens on the last style you chose, and on Subtitles the first time.
402	
403	4. Choose **Generate**.
404	
405	</Steps>
406	
407	The cues land on a new track at the front of the stack, called **Captions**, or **Captions 2** and so on if that name is taken. The whole run is one undo step, **Generate Captions**.
408	
409	## The Subtitles style
410	
411	Frame Job builds each cue from the recognised words by these rules:
412	
413	| Rule | Limit |
414	| --- | --- |
415	| Lines in a cue | At most 2 |
416	| Characters on a line | At most 42 |
417	| Time on screen | At most 6 seconds, up to the end of the cue's last word |
418	| Gap between cues | At least one frame |
419	| Speakers in a cue | One. A change of speaker always starts a new cue. |
420	
421	A cue starts on its first word and ends with its last, so it doesn't stay up through a long silence. A word too long for a line is left whole, never hyphenated, and wraps inside the caption box.
422	
423	## Speaker colours
424	
425	Each speaker's cues can take their own colour, so a viewer can tell who's talking.
426	
427	<Steps>
428	
429	1. Set **Engine:** to **AssemblyAI**. The **Speakers:** row is hidden with **On this Mac**, and a new AssemblyAI transcription needs [your key](/captions/assemblyai-key/).
430	
431	2. Tick **Speakers:**, which reads "split by speaker, coloured in Subtitles".
432	
433	3. Set **Style:** to **Subtitles** and choose **Generate**.
434	
435	</Steps>
436	
437	Speakers take their colours in the order they first appear in the run: white, yellow, cyan, green, then round again. The fifth speaker is white like the first. The colours are a fixed table with no setting. To change one afterwards, select those cues and set the colour under **Text** in the [Clip tab](/text-and-shapes/text-style/).
438	
439	Speakers are told apart within each media file, so the first speaker in one file and the first speaker in another count as two people and take two colours.
440	
441	Speaker colours only apply to the Subtitles style. In a [word caption style](/captions/word-caption-styles/), a change of speaker starts a new page and the colours stay as the style draws them.
442	
443	## The Caption preset
444	
445	Every cue is drawn in the **Caption** [text preset](/text-and-shapes/text-presets/), whether it was generated or [imported from a SubRip file](/captions/import-captions/).
446	
447	| Setting | Value |
448	| --- | --- |
449	| Typeface | Source Sans 3 Regular |
450	| Size | 3.5% of the canvas's shorter side |
451	| Alignment | Centred |
452	| Colour | White, unless a speaker colour applies |
453	| Backdrop | Black at 60%, with 12 px of padding and 8 px corners |
454	| Wraps at | 80% of the canvas width |
455	| Position on a wide or square canvas | The box is centred 38% of the frame height below the middle |
456	| Position on a canvas taller than wide | The box is centred a quarter of the frame height below the middle |
457	
458	On a 1920 × 1080 canvas that's 38 px text that wraps at 1,536 px. On a 1080 × 1920 canvas it's the same 38 px text, wrapping at 864 px. A canvas taller than wide, such as 9:16 or 4:5, also puts the box higher in the frame.
459	
460	A narrow canvas can wrap a cue past two lines, because the wrap happens inside the box after the cue is built. On a canvas taller than wide, Frame Job counts these and tells you once the captions are placed:
461	
462	> 3 captions wrap to more than two lines on this canvas.
463	
464	After generating, this appears on the sheet, which stays open with **Close**. After importing, it's an alert. The captions are placed either way.
465	
466	## Good to know
467	
468	- An imported SubRip file keeps its own line breaks and timing. The rules in [The Subtitles style](#the-subtitles-style) only apply to generated cues.
469	- **Replace:** is greyed out with Subtitles chosen. To swap a word caption track for Subtitles, generate the new track, then [remove the old one](/timeline/manage-tracks/).
470	- [Re-lay Captions for This Canvas](/captions/re-lay-captions/) keeps a Subtitles track as placed. To re-wrap one for a new canvas, generate it again on that canvas.
471	- A cue has no word timing, so the [looks](/captions/word-caption-looks/) don't apply. All three boxes are greyed out with Subtitles chosen.
472	- Subtitles are text in the picture, not a track a player can switch off. To ship a separate file, use [Export Captions…](/captions/export-captions/).
473	
474	## With an agent
475	
476	`transcribe` makes Subtitles (`style: subtitles`) unless it asks for another style, whatever the sheet last chose. See [Tools: captions and transcripts](/mcp/tools-captions/).
477	
478	## Related
479	
480	- [Captions are text clips](/captions/how-captions-work/)
481	- [Generate Captions](/captions/generate-captions/)
482	- [Word caption styles](/captions/word-caption-styles/)
483	- [Edit captions](/captions/edit-captions/)
484	- [Export captions](/captions/export-captions/)
485	=== transcript-keys
486	---
487	title: "Transcript keys"
488	description: Every key the Transcript tab's text takes, for moving by word or line, selecting, clearing and deleting, and what the rest of the keyboard does there.
489	---
490	
491	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
492	
493	While the transcript text has the keyboard, the arrows move through the words instead of the frames, and the delete keys cut words. Every other key works as it does on the timeline.
494	
495	<AtAGlance menu="View ▸ Transcript" keys="⌃⌘T" where="Inspector ▸ Transcript, with the text active" />
496	
497	To give the text the keyboard, choose **View ▸ Transcript** (<kbd>⌃⌘T</kbd>) or click in the text. Clicking **Transcript** in the inspector's tab strip shows the tab but doesn't give the text the keyboard.
498	
499	| Key | What it does |
500	| --- | --- |
501	| <kbd>←</kbd> <kbd>→</kbd> | Select the previous or next word and move the playhead to it |
502	| <kbd>↑</kbd> <kbd>↓</kbd> | Select the nearest word on the line above or below and move the playhead to it |
503	| <kbd>⇧</kbd> with an arrow | Extend the selection without moving the playhead |
504	| <kbd>⌘A</kbd> | Select every word |
505	| <kbd>⎋</kbd> | Clear the selected words or pause |
506	| <kbd>⌫</kbd> <kbd>⌦</kbd> | Delete the selected words and close the gap, or shorten the selected pause |
507	
508	## Move word by word
509	
510	<kbd>←</kbd> and <kbd>→</kbd> select the previous or next word and move the playhead to it. If the video is playing, it keeps playing from there.
511	
512	They move from the end of the selection you last moved. With a [pause](/captions/shorten-pauses/) selected, they move from the word before it. With nothing selected, they move from the highlighted word, the last one to start at or before the playhead, and if there isn't one, <kbd>→</kbd> selects the first word and <kbd>←</kbd> the last. At the first and last word they stay put.
513	
514	## Move line by line
515	
516	<kbd>↑</kbd> and <kbd>↓</kbd> select the nearest word on the line above or below, as the text is laid out, and move the playhead to it. They skip the timecode lines, and beep at the first and last line.
517	
518	## Extend the selection
519	
520	<kbd>⇧</kbd> with any arrow moves one end of the selection and leaves the playhead where it is. The other end stays where you started, so going back the other way shrinks the selection. <kbd>⇧</kbd>-click does the same with the mouse.
521	
522	The tab may [widen the selection](/captions/delete-words/#the-selection-becomes-the-range) further, over any word the cut would cut into.
523	
524	## Select every word
525	
526	<kbd>⌘A</kbd> selects every word, and **Edit ▸ Select All** does the same while the text has the keyboard. It selects words only, so a selected pause is dropped.
527	
528	## Clear the selection
529	
530	<kbd>⎋</kbd> clears the selected words or pause, along with the range they set. With nothing selected, <kbd>⎋</kbd> does what it does in the rest of the window, which is deselect a selected [action](/motion/actions/).
531	
532	## Delete
533	
534	With words selected, <kbd>⌫</kbd> or <kbd>⌦</kbd> [deletes them and closes the gap](/captions/delete-words/). With a pause selected, either one [shortens it](/captions/shorten-pauses/). <kbd>⌘⌫</kbd> does the same.
535	
536	With nothing selected in the text, <kbd>⌫</kbd> and <kbd>⌘⌫</kbd> do what they do on the timeline, so they act on the [selected clips or the range](/editing/delete-clips/).
537	
538	## Timeline keys keep working
539	
540	Any key this page doesn't list works as it does on the timeline, so you can play and mark without leaving the text. These are the common ones:
541	
542	| Key | What it does |
543	| --- | --- |
544	| <kbd>Space</kbd> | Play and pause |
545	| <kbd>J</kbd> <kbd>K</kbd> <kbd>L</kbd> | Shuttle back, pause, shuttle forward |
546	| <kbd>I</kbd> <kbd>O</kbd> | Set the in and out points at the playhead |
547	| <kbd>M</kbd> | Add a marker |
548	
549	[Keyboard shortcuts](/reference/keyboard-shortcuts/) has the rest.
550	
551	## Related
552	
553	- [Cut by deleting words](/captions/delete-words/)
554	- [Shorten a pause](/captions/shorten-pauses/)

558	---
559	title: "The Transcript tab"
560	description: "Read everything said in your project as text in the inspector, and choose which track and language the words come from."
561	---
562	
563	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
564	import Shot from '@components/Shot.astro';
565	
566	The Transcript tab shows what's said in your project as text you can read and click. It's the whole timeline as words, in the order you'd hear them, through every trim, speed change and nest. The spoken word [lights up](/captions/follow-the-transcript/) as the playhead passes it, and you can [cut by deleting words](/captions/delete-words/).
567	
568	<AtAGlance
569	  menu="View ▸ Transcript"
570	  keys="⌃⌘T"
571	  where="Inspector ▸ Transcript, between Document and the Assistant"
572	  tools={['get_timeline_transcript', 'get_transcript']}
573	  needs="A speech model on this Mac, or an AssemblyAI transcript of the file. No key is needed to read."
574	/>
575	
576	<Shot
577	  name="11c-transcript-tab.inspector"
578	  alt="The inspector's Transcript tab, with the Words from and Language pop-ups at the top and the timeline's words below them in paragraphs, each led by its timecode."
579	/>
580	
581	## Open the Transcript
582	
583	Choose **View ▸ Transcript** or press <kbd>⌃⌘T</kbd>. The inspector opens if it was hidden, the tab shows, and the text takes the keyboard, so the [transcript keys](/captions/transcript-keys/) work at once. It isn't a toggle: choosing it again leaves the tab showing.
584	
585	You can also click **Transcript** in the inspector's tab strip. That shows the tab without giving the text the keyboard, until you click in it.
586	
587	The first time you look, the tab may need to read your files, which means transcribing them on this Mac. See [Where the transcript's words come from](/captions/transcript-words/).
588	
589	## Every word you would hear
590	
591	The tab lists every word you'd hear if the timeline played, in order. That takes in clips on every track, and clips inside nests where they play.
592	
593	It leaves out what you wouldn't hear: muted tracks, clips [soloed out](/audio/mute-and-solo/), clips turned down to silence and clips with their audio switched off.
594	
595	With a [nest](/editing/nests/) open (<kbd>⌘↓</kbd>), the tab shows only what's inside it.
596	
597	## Paragraphs and timecodes
598	
599	The words come in paragraphs, each with its timecode above it. A new paragraph starts when:
600	
601	- the words move to another track
602	- the speaker changes, which only a transcript from AssemblyAI can tell
603	- there are 1.5 seconds or more between two clips' words on one track
604	- the speaker pauses for 1.5 seconds or more inside a clip
605	
606	A change of speaker starts a paragraph, and the tab doesn't print a speaker's name.
607	
608	Some words show faint, and a pause over a second can show as a grey length such as "[2.4 s]". Those are about cutting. See [Cut by deleting words](/captions/delete-words/) and [Shorten a pause](/captions/shorten-pauses/).
609	
610	## The bar
611	
612	A bar sits above the text and stays put while the text scrolls. It holds the two pop-ups, then short notes on what the tab is doing and anything it couldn't read.
613	
614	**Words from** and **Language** belong to the window. They stay while it's open, whichever tab you look at, and they aren't saved with the project.
615	
616	### Words from
617	
618	**Words from** chooses whose words to show: **All tracks**, the default, or one track by name. With one track chosen, the tab shows only the words on it, and reads only the files with a clip on it. If that track goes away, the tab goes back to **All tracks**.
619	
620	### Language
621	
622	**Language** chooses the language files are read in on this Mac.
623	
624	**Automatic** is your Mac's language, shown in brackets as a code such as `en-US`. If you have no speech model for it, Automatic uses another form of the same language, or failing that the first language you have. Below it is every language your Mac has a speech model for. The pop-up is disabled when there are none.
625	
626	Choosing a language reads the files again in that language. The earlier reading is kept too, so switching back is immediate. A file with an AssemblyAI transcript keeps showing that transcript whichever you choose.
627	
628	### Read and Stop
629	
630	While a file is being read on this Mac, a note shows its progress, with **Stop** beside it:
631	
632	> Reading “interview.mov” on this Mac… 40 % (1 of 2)
633	
634	**Stop** leaves the rest of the files unread, and the note changes:
635	
636	> Stopped. 2 files not read on this Mac.
637	
638	**Read** carries on from there, and so does coming back to the tab after looking at another one. Editing the timeline or changing **Words from** or **Language** doesn't start it again.
639	
640	A file you stop part-way isn't kept, so it's read from its start next time. **Stop** ends only the tab's own reading: if an agent is waiting for the same file's words at that moment, its reading goes on.
641	
642	## Clips with no words
643	
644	A clip that can't give any words is listed under the pop-ups with the reason, such as "clip 12 — its audio is switched off". A clip inside a nest reads "clip 12 in nest Intro — …".
645	
646	| The note says | What to do |
647	| --- | --- |
648	| its audio is switched off | Turn the clip's audio on. |
649	| its media has no audio track | Nothing. The file has no sound to read. |
650	| its media file is missing | [Relink the file](/projects/relink-media/). |
651	| it plays in reverse, so its speech cannot be transcribed | Turn off [Reverse](/speed/reverse/) to read it. |
652	
653	The first three clips are listed. "…and 4 more clips with no words." stands for the rest, and holding the pointer over it lists them.
654	
655	## The same speech on two tracks
656	
657	When two clips carry the same speech, such as a camera's sound and a separate microphone, a note names the pair:
658	
659	> Clips 3 and 7 carry the same speech. Mute one, or switch its audio off, to read it once.
660	
661	Both stay in the text until you do. The note appears for clips of different files that overlap for at least 5 seconds, when at least 60% of the words of the clip with fewer words in that overlap also appear in the other, in the same order.
662	
663	## Good to know
664	
665	- Nothing you do in the tab's bar changes the project, and the words aren't part of your edit.
666	- The tab has no search.
667	
668	## With an agent
669	
670	Agents read the same words with `get_timeline_transcript`. It returns the same notes as `notes` and the clips with no words as `no_words`, and its `tracks` and `language` do what **Words from** and **Language** do. See [`get_timeline_transcript`](/mcp/tools-captions/#get_timeline_transcript).
671

679	=== transcript-words
680	---
681	title: "Where the transcript's words come from"
682	description: "How the Transcript tab gets its words, from an AssemblyAI transcript or by reading on this Mac, and what it keeps so the next look is immediate."
683	---
684	
685	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
686	
687	The [Transcript tab](/captions/transcript-tab/) needs no setting up. It uses a transcript you already have, or transcribes the file on this Mac the first time you look, which the tab calls reading it. Either way it sends nothing anywhere.
688	
689	<AtAGlance
690	  where="Inspector ▸ Transcript"
691	  tools={['get_timeline_transcript', 'get_transcript']}
692	  needs="A speech model on this Mac, for any file with no AssemblyAI transcript."
693	/>
694	
695	## AssemblyAI first, otherwise this Mac
696	
697	For each file, the tab takes the first of these it finds:
698	
699	1. **An AssemblyAI transcript.** You have one if you've used [**File ▸ Generate Captions…** with AssemblyAI](/captions/assemblyai-transcription/) or [**Remove Filler Words**](/cleanup/remove-filler-words/) on the file. Using it needs no key.
700	2. **A reading on this Mac.** Otherwise the tab transcribes the file the first time you look, in your Mac's language unless you [choose another](/captions/transcript-tab/#language).
701	
702	Reading on this Mac is quick: about 0.7 seconds a minute of speech on an M2 Max, so an hour takes well under a minute. Playback keeps running while it reads.
703	
704	The tab never makes a network request, whichever source it uses.
705	
706	## One file at a time, playhead first
707	
708	Files are read one at a time, starting with the one under the playhead. Each file's words appear as soon as it's done, without waiting for the rest.
709	
710	If you switch to another tab, the reading stops, and it picks up when you come back. To stop it yourself, use [**Stop**](/captions/transcript-tab/#read-and-stop).
711	
712	## Kept per file and language
713	
714	What this Mac heard is kept in the project's [cache](/reference/framejob-package/#cache), one reading for each file and language, so the next look is immediate.
715	
716	Each file is read whole, once. Trimming a clip, adding another clip of the same file or changing its speed doesn't read it again.
717	
718	A reading is used only while the file and the macOS version are the same. If either changes, or you choose another language, the file is read again.
719	
720	These readings are only for the transcript. [Captions](/captions/generate-captions/) and [Remove Filler Words](/cleanup/remove-filler-words/) never use them.
721	
722	## When no speech model is installed
723	
724	If your Mac has no speech model, the tab says:
725	
726	> This Mac has no speech model installed. Choose File ▸ Generate Captions…, pick a language and press Download.
727	
728	Do that, then come back to the tab. A file with an AssemblyAI transcript shows its words in the meantime.
729	
730	A file this Mac can't read is named in the same place, and the tab carries on with the others. It tries that file again when you next come back to the tab.
731	
732	## Ramped clips and following edits
733	
734	Words are placed through a clip's speed, including a [ramp](/speed/speed-ramps/), so a word's time matches what plays on the timeline.
735	
736	Editing the timeline updates the text right away, and the words you were reading stay where they were. During a drag, the text updates when you let go.
737	
738	## With an agent
739	
740	An agent reads these words with `get_timeline_transcript`, or one clip's with `get_transcript`. When it reads a file on this Mac, the tab's **Stop** leaves that reading running. The Assistant's own **Stop** ends it, unless the tab is reading that file too, and nothing is saved from a stopped reading. See [Tools: captions and transcripts](/mcp/tools-captions/).
741	
742	## Related
743

748	=== what-can-be-transcribed
749	---
750	title: "What can be transcribed"
751	description: "Which clips Generate Captions can read, why a clip gets left out of a run, and the limits on how much one run can do."
752	---
753	
754	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
755	
756	Generate Captions can only read clips that play recorded sound. Before a run starts, Frame Job works out which clips those are. Use this page when a clip gets left out, or when a long project stops a run.
757	
758	<AtAGlance menu="File ▸ Generate Captions…" tools="transcribe" />
759	
760	## Which clips can be transcribed
761	
762	A clip can be transcribed when all of these are true:
763	
764	- It plays a movie or sound file that has an audio track.
765	- It plays forwards.
766	- Its audio is on.
767	- Its file is present.
768	
769	**File ▸ Generate Captions…** is greyed out when no clip on the open timeline plays sound from a media file, forwards, with its audio on.
770	
771	## Why a clip is skipped
772	
773	A clip that can't be read isn't part of the run. In the [Generate Captions](/captions/generate-captions/) sheet it doesn't count towards the summary line, so if the sheet says 2 clips and you expected 3, the third is here. The sheet doesn't list these clips one by one. If it leaves nothing at all, it reads "Nothing to transcribe".
774	
775	An agent that names the clips it wants gets the reason back for each one, in these words:
776	
777	| Reason | What it means | What to do |
778	| --- | --- | --- |
779	| its source is not a media file, so it has no speech | It's a text, shape, still, image, graphic, adjustment or nest clip. | For a nest, [open it](/editing/inside-a-nest/) and caption inside it. |
780	| it plays in reverse, so its speech cannot be transcribed | The words would come out backwards. | Only a clip playing forwards can be read. See [Reverse a clip](/speed/reverse/). |
781	| its media has no audio track | The file has no sound. | Nothing to transcribe here. |
782	| its audio is switched off | For example, the picture half of a clip after [Detach Audio](/audio/detach-and-attach/). | After Detach Audio, the audio-only clip below it holds the sound and is read instead. **Clip ▸ Attach Audio** joins the two again. |
783	| its media file is missing | Frame Job can't find the file. | [Relink it](/projects/relink-media/). |
784	| its speed ramps, and no speed map was read for it | Frame Job couldn't work out where the ramp puts the words, so it won't guess. | Remove the [ramp](/speed/speed-ramps/) if you need this clip captioned. |
785	| its speed or length is degenerate | The clip has no usable speed or no length. | Add the clip to the timeline again. |
786	
787	A clip that's read but holds no words shows up afterwards, in the [run report](/captions/generate-captions/#the-run-report), as "no speech was recognised in it".
788	
789	## Retimed clips land correctly
790	
791	On a sped-up, slowed or speed-ramped clip, each word lands where it's heard on the timeline, not where it sits in the file. Transcribing a ramped clip places each word where the ramp plays it.
792	
793	Captions keep following afterwards. Change the speed later and they move with the speech. See [Captions follow a speed change](/speed/captions-and-speed/).
794	
795	## The 10-hour and 4,096-clip limits
796	
797	**AssemblyAI takes at most 10 hours per file.** What counts is the length of the whole file, not the part your clip uses, because the whole file is what's sent. Frame Job won't extract or send a longer file, and its clips are listed in the [run report](/captions/generate-captions/#the-run-report) with "“name” is longer than AssemblyAI's 10-hour limit for one file." The other files in the run carry on.
798	
799	**On this Mac there's no limit on length.** There is a limit on time: each clip gets four times the length of its audio, and at least two minutes. A clip still going after that is stopped and reported with "Transcribing “name” took too long and was stopped."
800	
801	**A project holds at most 4,096 clips.** When a run's captions wouldn't fit, none of them are placed and the project doesn't change. The card says "5000 captions is more than this project has room for: 900 more clips would fit, out of 4096." Frame Job can only count captions once the words are in, so this comes at the end of the run. With **Replace** ticked, the clips on the tracks it would remove don't count against you.
802	
803	Every caption or page is one clip, so word styles usually use more clips than **Subtitles**, and **One Word** uses one clip for every word. [Limits](/reference/limits/) lists the rest of the project's limits.
804

811	=== word-caption-looks
812	---
813	title: Looks for word captions
814	description: Add a sliding pill, a left-to-right word fill or a dim in pauses to word captions, and find out what you can change about their colours.
815	---
816	
817	import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
818	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
819	
820	Looks add movement to a [word style](/captions/word-caption-styles/)'s pages: a pill that slides between words, a word that fills as it's said, and a page that dims when nobody's talking.
821	
822	<AtAGlance
823	  menu="File ▸ Generate Captions…"
824	  where="The Generate Captions sheet, under Style:"
825	  tools={['transcribe', 'set_text']}
826	/>
827	
828	## Three looks for word captions
829	
830	<Steps>
831	
832	1. Choose **File ▸ Generate Captions…**, and set **Language:**, **Engine:** and **From:** as [Generate Captions](/captions/generate-captions/) explains.
833	
834	2. Set **Style:** to a [word style](/captions/word-caption-styles/).
835	
836	3. Tick the looks you want under the **Style:** pop-up.
837	
838	4. Choose **Generate**.
839	
840	</Steps>
841	
842	Each look works with some styles and not others:
843	
844	| Look | Highlight | Pill | Karaoke | Build | One Word |
845	| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
846	| **Slide the pill** | | Yes | | | |
847	| **Fill words as spoken** | Yes | | Yes | Yes | |
848	| **Dim in pauses** | Yes | Yes | Yes | Yes | Yes |
849	
850	A box that doesn't apply to the chosen style is greyed out and does nothing, but it keeps its tick for when you switch back. With **Subtitles** chosen, all three are greyed out.
851	
852	Each box is off until you tick it, and the sheet remembers each one between runs.
853	
854	A look changes how a word is drawn, never a letter or the size of the page. Ticking one doesn't change where pages break.
855	
856	Looks are set when the captions are generated, like the style. To change them on a placed track, [generate again with Replace](/captions/restyle-captions/#restyle-by-generating-again).
857	
858	## Slide the pill
859	
860	The pill slides from the previous word to the one being said, instead of jumping. The slide takes 0.2 s, or less when the next word starts sooner, so the pill has always arrived before it has to leave. The first word on a page has nothing to slide from, so the pill starts there.
861	
862	This works with **Pill**, the only style that has one.
863	
864	## Fill words as spoken
865	
866	The word being said fills from left to right as it's spoken. The fill runs from the word's start to its end, and takes 0.6 s at most, so a long word finishes filling before it's finished being said.
867	
868	| Style | The part already said | The rest of the word |
869	| --- | --- | --- |
870	| **Highlight** | Yellow | White |
871	| **Karaoke** | Yellow | White at 55% opacity |
872	| **Build** | Yellow | Not drawn yet |
873	
874	**Pill** and **One Word** can't use this look, because their spoken word is the same colour on both sides of the fill.
875	
876	## Dim in pauses
877	
878	The page fades to half opacity during a pause of 0.25 s or more, then comes back before the next word. Each fade takes 0.1 s, and the words and the pill fade together. It works with all five word styles.
879	
880	The page also dims at either end of a caption, when the wait there is 0.25 s or more:
881	
882	- before the first word. The page opens dim, with no fade.
883	- after the last word, until the caption ends.
884	
885	A pause of 0.25 s also [ends a page](/captions/word-caption-styles/#where-a-page-breaks), so on a generated track you'll mostly see the dim at the end of a page, after its last word.
886	
887	With **On this Mac** chosen and a word style selected, a note under the boxes reads "On-device words rarely carry a pause; this shows mostly with AssemblyAI."
888	
889	The sheet's [preview](/captions/word-caption-styles/#the-sheets-two-frame-preview) doesn't show this look.
890	
891	## Word colours
892	
893	The inspector has no section for a page's word colours, pop size or pill. Nothing in the Clip tab changes the yellow, the violet or how far the word pops.
894	
895	To change them, generate again with a [different style](/captions/restyle-captions/#restyle-by-generating-again), or [have an agent do it](#with-an-agent).
896	
897	The **Color** row under **Text ▸ Style** still works on the words drawn in the text's own colour. That's the white words in **Highlight** and **Build**, and every word in **Pill** and **One Word**. It leaves the yellow alone, and it changes nothing in **Karaoke**, which sets all its own colours.
898	
899	## With an agent
900	
901	An agent can do two things here that the sheet can't.
902	
903	It can change a placed page's word style with `set_text`. That covers highlighting or building word by word, the colours of the spoken word and of the words before and after it, a pop from 100% to 150%, the pill's colour, padding and corners, whether the pill slides, whether the word fills, and how far the page dims, from none to fully invisible. The sheet's dim is always half. A page changed this way is no longer one of the styles Frame Job makes, so [Re-lay Captions](/captions/re-lay-captions/#tracks-kept-as-placed) keeps its track as placed. See [Tools: text, shapes and clip names](/mcp/tools-clip-properties/).
904	
905	It can also ask for looks with `transcribe`, through `slide`, `fill` and `dim`, but each one is off unless it asks, never what the sheet last chose. Frame Job won't add a look to a style it wouldn't show on, or to captions it isn't placing. When it gives any of the three and the captions are placed, the result lists the looks that were on. See [Tools: captions and transcripts](/mcp/tools-captions/).
906	
907	## Related
908	
909	- [Generate Captions](/captions/generate-captions/)
910	- [Word caption styles](/captions/word-caption-styles/)

913	=== word-caption-styles
914	---
915	title: Word caption styles
916	description: Make the large word-by-word captions used in shorts and reels, choose how the spoken word is marked, and see how pages are filled for your canvas.
917	---
918	
919	import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
920	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
921	
922	The five word styles make the large captions used in shorts and reels, where each word is marked as it's said. For classic two-line cues, use [Subtitles](/captions/subtitles/) instead.
923	
924	<AtAGlance
925	  menu="File ▸ Generate Captions…"
926	  where="The Generate Captions sheet ▸ Style:"
927	  tools="transcribe"
928	/>
929	
930	## Make word captions
931	
932	<Steps>
933	
934	1. Choose **File ▸ Generate Captions…**.
935	
936	2. Set **Language:**, **Engine:** and **From:**. [Generate Captions](/captions/generate-captions/) explains each one.
937	
938	3. Set **Style:** to **Highlight**, **Pill**, **Karaoke**, **Build** or **One Word**. The sheet remembers your choice for next time.
939	
940	4. Tick any [looks](/captions/word-caption-looks/) you want, and check the [preview](#the-sheets-two-frame-preview).
941	
942	5. Choose **Generate**.
943	
944	</Steps>
945	
946	## Word caption pages
947	
948	A word style doesn't make cues. Each clip holds a **page** of words, with each word's timing, and the word being spoken is drawn the way the style says. A page is still an ordinary [text clip](/captions/how-captions-work/), so you can drag, trim and split it.
949	
950	All five styles are white with the spoken word marked. Words are marked by their timing only, so there's no keyword emphasis and no emoji.
951	
952	The text is 7.5% of the canvas's shorter side, or 12% for One Word. That means a vertical and a horizontal canvas get the same text height: on both 1080 × 1920 and 1920 × 1080 it's 81 px, or 130 px for One Word. Where a style pops the spoken word, the pop takes 0.12 s.
953	
954	## The five styles
955	
956	### Highlight
957	
958	The spoken word turns yellow and pops to 112%, and the other words stay white.
959	
960	Montserrat Black with a black outline, in capitals. The box is centred a quarter of the frame height below the middle.
961	
962	### Pill
963	
964	The spoken word sits on a violet pill, and doesn't change size. [Slide the pill](/captions/word-caption-looks/#slide-the-pill) makes the pill travel between words instead of jumping.
965	
966	Montserrat ExtraBold, in capitals. The box is centred a quarter of the frame height below the middle.
967	
968	### Karaoke
969	
970	Words turn yellow as they're said and stay yellow. Words still to come are white at 55% opacity.
971	
972	Montserrat ExtraBold, as written. Karaoke can use up to two lines, and it's the only style that wraps a page of several words. The box is centred 28% of the frame height below the middle.
973	
974	### Build
975	
976	Words appear one by one. The newest is yellow and pops to 115%, and the ones before it are white.
977	
978	Anton with a black outline, in capitals. The box is centred a quarter of the frame height below the middle.
979	
980	### One Word
981	
982	One large word at a time, white, popping to 120%. Every page holds one word.
983	
984	Bebas Neue with a black outline, in capitals. The box is centred 18% of the frame height below the middle.
985	
986	## Bundled typefaces
987	
988	Montserrat Black, Montserrat ExtraBold, Anton and Bebas Neue ship inside the app under the SIL Open Font License, so there's nothing to install.
989	
990	## Pages are filled to their measured width
991	
992	A page holds as many words as fit, not a set number. Frame Job measures each page in its style's typeface, size, case and outline on your canvas, and fills it up to 86% of the canvas width, on one line. Karaoke can use two lines, and One Word always holds one word.
993	
994	So the same speech makes shorter pages on a 9:16 canvas than on a 16:9 one. On a 1080 × 1920 canvas a page can be about 929 px wide. If you change the canvas size later, [Re-lay Captions for This Canvas](/captions/re-lay-captions/) pages them again.
995	
996	When a page ends because the width ran out, Frame Job can move its last word onto the next page if the two then come closer in width. That stops a sentence ending on one word alone.
997	
998	## Where a page breaks
999	
1000	A page ends early at any of these:
1001	
1002	- a pause of 0.25 s or more between two words
1003	- a word ending in `.` `?` `!` or `…`
1004	- 3 seconds on screen, up to the end of the page's last word
1005	- a change of speaker, when [**Speakers:**](/captions/assemblyai-transcription/) is ticked
1006	
1007	When the width runs out within two words of a comma, semicolon or colon, the break moves back to that mark. It only does this when the page is already at least half full and the words that move still fit on the next page.
1008	
1009	On-device words rarely carry a pause, so pages from **On this Mac** break at pauses less often than pages from AssemblyAI.
1010	
1011	## A word too wide for the frame
1012	
1013	A word too wide for a page gets a page of its own and shrinks in 5% steps, down to 80% of the style's size, until it fits. If it's still too wide at 80%, it stays at that size and wraps.
1014	
1015	## How long a page stays up
1016	
1017	A page stays up 0.5 s after its last word, and the row is empty until the next page. If the next page starts sooner than that, the page runs right up to it, so the row doesn't blink between pages.
1018	
1019	Pages never run past the end of the clip they came from.
1020	
1021	## The sheet's two-frame preview
1022	
1023	The preview under the looks shows a sample page, drawn the way the canvas draws it and paged for this canvas's proportions. It shows you how the style looks, not how big it will be, because each frame is scaled to fit the strip.
1024	
1025	| What you see | What it means |
1026	| --- | --- |
1027	| Two frames | A word style, with the first word active in the top frame and the second word in the bottom one. A page of one word shows that word in both. |
1028	| One frame | Subtitles. |
1029	| The sample words | The first words of the first clip's cached AssemblyAI transcript when there is one, otherwise "This is how it looks". |
1030	| A half-filled word | **Fill words as spoken** is ticked. |
1031	| A pill between two words | **Slide the pill** is ticked. It shows in the second frame. |
1032	
1033	**Dim in pauses** isn't previewed.
1034	
1035	## Good to know
1036	
1037	- A style is set when the captions are generated, and you can't switch it on a placed track. To change it, see [Restyle a caption track](/captions/restyle-captions/).
1038	- The capitals are applied when a page is drawn, so the words stay as written in the **Content** box and in an [exported caption file](/captions/export-captions/). To show a page as written, untick **UPPERCASE**. See [Edit captions](/captions/edit-captions/).
1039	- [Text reveals](/text-and-shapes/text-reveal/) don't apply to a timed page.
1040	- The [Subtitles](/captions/subtitles/) style is the first choice in the **Style:** pop-up, and it works differently: two-line cues with no word timing.
1041	
1042	## With an agent
1043	
1044	`transcribe` makes word captions when it asks for a word style: `highlight`, `pill`, `karaoke`, `build` or `one_word`. It never uses the style the sheet last chose. See [Tools: captions and transcripts](/mcp/tools-captions/).
