29	## `transcribe`
30	
31	Turns the speech in clips into captions, on this Mac or with AssemblyAI, and places them as text clips on a new track of their own at the front. It does what [**File ▸ Generate Captions…**](/captions/generate-captions/) does.
32	
33	The new clips are [ordinary text clips](/captions/how-captions-work/), so they draw in the preview, in `render_frame` and in an export, and they can be retimed with `move_clip` or restyled with `set_text`.
34	
35	**Arguments**
36	
37	| Argument | Type | Required | What it does |
38	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
39	| `clips` | array of integers | No | Transcribe only these clips, at least one. Left out, every clip with recorded sound in the timeline or nest that's open. |
40	| `engine` | string | No | `apple` (the default) on this Mac, or `assemblyai` in the cloud. See [Transcribe engines](#transcribe-engines). |
41	| `language` | string | No | A language tag, such as `en-US`. On this Mac it defaults to the Mac's own language. With AssemblyAI it defaults to `auto`, which detects the language. |
42	| `style` | string | No | `subtitles` (the default), `highlight`, `pill`, `karaoke`, `build` or `one_word`. See [Caption styles and paging](#caption-styles-and-paging). |
43	| `place` | boolean | No | True (the default) places the cues as one undo step. False answers the cues and changes nothing. See [Check a transcript before placing it](#check-a-transcript-before-placing-it). |
44	| `replace` | boolean | No | With a word style, removes earlier caption tracks in the same undo step. See [Restyle captions](#restyle-captions). |
45	| `slide` | boolean | No | The pill slides between words. See [Caption looks](#caption-looks). |
46	| `fill` | boolean | No | The spoken word fills from left to right. See [Caption looks](#caption-looks). |
47	| `dim` | boolean | No | The page fades in a pause. See [Caption looks](#caption-looks). |
48	| `speakers` | boolean | No | AssemblyAI only. Ask who says what. Default false. See [Speakers and vocabulary](#speakers-and-vocabulary). |
49	| `vocabulary` | array of strings | No | AssemblyAI only. Words and phrases to expect. See [Speakers and vocabulary](#speakers-and-vocabulary). |
50	| `refresh` | boolean | No | AssemblyAI only. Ignore the kept transcript and upload again. Default false. |
51	| `project` | string | No | The path of the open project to act on, as `get_project` reports it. The frontmost project when left out. |
52	
53	Only a clip playing a movie or sound file can be transcribed, and not one played in reverse, whose words would come out backwards. A clip you name that can't be is listed under `skipped`. See [What can be transcribed](/captions/what-can-be-transcribed/).
54	
55	**What it answers**
56	
57	| Key | What it holds |
58	| --- | --- |
59	| `cues` | The cues, placed or not, each with `start`, `end` and `text`. With a word style each also has `words`, a list of `start`, `end` and `text` in timeline ticks, and `size` where a lone word shrank. |
60	| `engine`, `language` | The engine that ran and the language it used. |
61	| `clips_read` | The clips words came from. |
62	| `placed` | Whether the cues were placed. |
63	| `captions` | How many text clips were placed. |
64	| `track_name` | The name of the new track. |
65	| `trimmed` | How many cues were shortened to meet the next one, when any were. |
66	| `replaced` | The ids of the tracks removed, whenever `replace` was given. |
67	| `looks` | The looks that were on, whenever `slide`, `fill` or `dim` was given. |
68	| `skipped` | Each clip that gave no captions and why, when there are any. |
69	
70	A placed run also has the ids of what it created and the `project` summary. Subtitles cues are at most two lines of 42 characters and at most 6 s, with a frame between them.
71	
72	An AssemblyAI run adds these:
73	
74	| Key | What it holds |
75	| --- | --- |
76	| `uploaded` | The media files sent. |
77	| `cached` | The media files answered from the transcript kept in the project, with no request. |
78	| `audio_seconds` | The seconds of audio billed. |
79	| `speech_model_used` | Each uploaded file's `media` and `model`. |
80	| `language_detected` | With `language` left out or `auto`, each uploaded file's `media`, `code` and, when AssemblyAI gave one, `confidence`. |
81	| `endpoint` | The host the run's requests went to. Absent when no key is set. |
82	| `note` | Anything else worth saying: a cut vocabulary, a fallback model, a delete AssemblyAI hasn't confirmed, or a transcript that couldn't be kept for reuse. |
83	
84	**When it refuses**
85	
86	Nothing changes and nothing is uploaded when:
87	
88	- A clip id names nothing, or `clips` is empty.
89	- Nothing has recorded sound. The answer reads "Nothing in this timeline has recorded sound to transcribe…", or, for clips you named, "None of those clips can be transcribed" with the reason for each.
90	- `style` or `engine` isn't one of its spellings. The answer names them all.
91	- `speakers`, `vocabulary` or `refresh` is given with engine `apple`. Giving one at all is enough, even as false.
92	- `replace` is given with `subtitles` or with `place: false`. Giving it at all is enough, even as false.
93	- `slide`, `fill` or `dim` is true with a style it doesn't show on, or with `place: false`.
94	- The `language` tag is misspelt, for engine `apple`. The answer lists the tags speech recognition knows, 24 at most.
95	- The language is real but its speech model isn't on this Mac, for engine `apple`. The answer lists the languages ready here, 24 at most. This is a separate answer from a misspelling, because a person has to fix it: they open **File ▸ Generate Captions…**, choose the language and press **Download**. The tool never downloads a model. See [Download a speech language](/captions/on-device-transcription/#download-a-speech-language).
96	- No AssemblyAI key is set and a file needs uploading: "No AssemblyAI API key is set. Set one in Frame Job ▸ Settings… ▸ Transcription."
97	- The project has nowhere to keep its transcripts, which is rare: "This document has nowhere to keep its transcript cache, so it cannot be transcribed with AssemblyAI. Save it first."
98	
99	Once a run starts, a clip that fails is listed under `skipped` and the others are still placed. That includes a clip whose file is over AssemblyAI's 10-hour limit, and a clip where no speech was heard. The exception is a key AssemblyAI refuses, which ends the run with nothing placed, because every later file would fail the same way. If no cues come out of the whole run, nothing is placed and the answer says why, for example "No speech was recognised in the audio that was transcribed."
100	
101	If an AssemblyAI run fails after it has spent money, the answer says so: "AssemblyAI had already been billed for 1 media file (N audio seconds) before this failed." [When a file fails](/captions/assemblyai-transcription/#when-a-file-fails) lists the reasons you can see.
102	
103	### Transcribe engines
104	
105	**`apple`** is the default. Speech recognition runs on this Mac and nothing leaves it. It needs no permission and has no length limit. Each run recognises the audio again, because this engine keeps nothing for `transcribe` to reuse, and `refresh` doesn't apply.
106	
107	Speech models are installed per Mac, from the **Download** row in **File ▸ Generate Captions…**. `language` matches a tag such as `en-US`, a language's display name, or a bare code such as `en`, which takes the first matching language on this Mac.
108	
109	**`assemblyai`** sends the audio of every media file behind the clips you named to AssemblyAI, a cloud service that bills for it. It sends the whole file, not only the parts in use. The transcript is deleted from AssemblyAI once the words have been read back. See [What goes to AssemblyAI](/captions/assemblyai-privacy/).
110	
111	:::caution
112	Don't choose `assemblyai` for somebody else's recording without their say-so. Audio leaves the Mac and the owner of the key pays for it.
113	:::
114	
115	- **The engine is never remembered.** Left out, it's `apple`, whatever the Generate Captions sheet last chose. An agent that wants the cloud says so on every call.
116	- **Each file is kept.** One transcript per media file is kept in the project package, so a second run over the same files with the same settings makes no request and lists them under `cached`. See [Reuse a transcript](/captions/assemblyai-transcription/#reuse-a-transcript).
117	- **`refresh`** ignores what's kept and uploads again, and the file is billed again.
118	- **The key.** A new transcription needs your AssemblyAI key. A run whose every file already has a current transcript needs no key and makes no network request, unless `refresh` is true. If AssemblyAI hasn't confirmed deleting a transcript and no key is set, `note` says so, and a later run with a key for the same account and region tries the deletion again.
119	- **`language`.** `auto`, the default, detects the language and the answer reports it. Any other code goes to AssemblyAI unchecked, and one it doesn't support comes back as AssemblyAI's own sentence after the upload.
120	- **The region.** It's a choice in [Settings](/captions/assemblyai-key/), and no argument sets it. `endpoint` tells you where a run's requests went.
121	
122	The built-in Assistant can't use this engine. A call with `engine: "assemblyai"` is withheld from it, and it points you to **File ▸ Generate Captions…**, which shows what's uploaded and what it costs. See [What it won't do and what it asks first](/assistant/what-it-will-not-do/).
123	
124	### Speakers and vocabulary
125	
126	Both need `engine: "assemblyai"`. The sheet's rows are described on [Transcribe with AssemblyAI](/captions/assemblyai-transcription/#split-the-words-by-speaker).
127	
128	`speakers: true` asks AssemblyAI who says what, and a change of speaker then starts a new cue. With `subtitles`, each speaker's cues take their own colour: white, yellow, cyan, then green in order of first appearance, then round again. A speaker is a label within one media file, so one person in two files can come back as two speakers.
129	
130	`vocabulary` tells AssemblyAI the words and phrases to expect, such as product names, people and identifiers. Terms are trimmed, repeats are dropped keeping the first spelling, and the list stops at 1,000 terms. `note` says so when it was cut.
131	
132	### Check a transcript before placing it
133	
134	`place: false` answers the cues and changes nothing, with no edit and no undo step. Use it to read a transcript before committing to it.
135	
136	You can't combine it with `replace` or with a look set to true, because nothing is placed. To place the captions, call again without `place`. With AssemblyAI the second call reuses the kept transcript and uploads nothing.
137	
138	### Caption styles and paging
139	
140	`style` chooses how the words look. It's the same choice as **Style** in the sheet, and the default is never what the sheet last chose. See [Word caption styles](/captions/word-caption-styles/).
141	
142	| `style` | What it makes |
143	| --- | --- |
144	| `subtitles` | Two-line cues in the Caption preset. The default. |
145	| `highlight` | Montserrat Black, upper case, the word being said in yellow with a pop. |
146	| `pill` | Montserrat ExtraBold, upper case, the word being said on a violet pill. |
147	| `karaoke` | Montserrat ExtraBold as written, up to two lines, words turning yellow. |
148	| `build` | Anton, upper case, words appearing one by one. |
149	| `one_word` | Bebas Neue, one large word at a time. |
150	
151	Every style but `subtitles` is a word style, and makes pages rather than cues. A page is the group of words on screen at one time. Each page holds its words' timings, so the word being said is drawn as the style says.
152	
153	A page is filled to the width it will measure on this canvas in that style, at most 0.86 of the canvas width, not to a word count. It sits on one line, or up to two with `karaoke`. A page also closes at:
154	
155	- a change of speaker
156	- a gap of 0.25 s or more
157	- a word ending in `.`, `?`, `!` or `…`
158	- 3 s on screen
159	
160	A lone word too wide for the canvas shrinks, down to 80 % of the style's size, before it wraps. Pages stay inside their own clip. A page meets the next one where the gap is under 0.25 s, and otherwise holds for 0.5 s after its last word.
161	
162	### Caption looks
163	
164	`slide`, `fill` and `dim` add a look to a word style's pages, as the sheet's three boxes do. Each is false unless given, and never what the sheet last chose. See [Looks for word captions](/captions/word-caption-looks/).
165	
166	| Argument | The sheet's box | What it does | Works with |
167	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
168	| `slide` | **Slide the pill** | The pill slides from the word before to the word being said, over 0.2 s or sooner, instead of jumping. | `pill` |
169	| `fill` | **Fill words as spoken** | The word being said fills from left to right as it's spoken, taking 0.6 s at most. | `highlight`, `karaoke`, `build` |
170	| `dim` | **Dim in pauses** | The page fades to half its opacity in a pause of 0.25 s or more. | All five word styles |
171	
172	True with any other style, or with `place: false`, where it would show nothing, is refused and the answer names the argument. False is always accepted. Words from engine `apple` rarely carry a pause that long, so `dim` shows mostly with `assemblyai`.
173	
174	Whenever one of the three was given, a placed run lists under `looks` the ones that were on.
175	
176	### Restyle captions
177	
178	To change a word style, run `transcribe` again with `replace: true`. See [Restyle a caption track](/captions/restyle-captions/).
179	
180	`replace` removes, in the same undo step, every track this command could have made over these clips: a track named **Captions** or **Captions N** that holds only text clips, each of which overlaps a clip being transcribed. The answer lists those tracks under `replaced`.
181	
182	It needs a word style and `place` true. A style is only a display choice, so with AssemblyAI a kept transcript is reused whatever style you ask for, and restyling uploads nothing. Engine `apple` recognises the audio again.
183	
184	## `import_captions`
185	
186	Reads a SubRip (`.srt`) file and lays it out as text clips, one for each cue, on a new track of its own. It does what [**File ▸ Import Captions…**](/captions/import-captions/) does, and that page has what the reader copes with.
187	
188	They're ordinary text clips in the Caption preset, so they burn in on export with no further step. Times snap to the frame grid, and a cue that overlapped the next one is shortened to meet it.
189	
190	**Arguments**
191	
192	| Argument | Type | Required | What it does |
193	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
194	| `path` | string | Yes | The absolute or `~` path to the `.srt` file. |
195	| `track` | integer | No | Put the captions on this existing track instead of a new one, which the menu can't do. Cues that would overlap something there are dropped, so it's safer to leave this out. |
196	| `project` | string | No | The path of the open project to act on, as `get_project` reports it. The frontmost project when left out. |
197	
198	**What it answers**
199	
200	| Key | What it holds |
201	| --- | --- |
202	| `cues` | How many cues survived. |
203	| `captions` | How many text clips were made. It's smaller than `cues` when a track you named turned some away. |
204	| `track_name` | The new track's name. Absent when you named a track. |
205	| `trimmed` | How many cues were shortened, when any were. |
206	| `skipped` | Every entry it couldn't read or place, with its line number, when there are any. |
207	
208	It also has the ids of what it created and the `project` summary. It's one undo step, **Import Captions**.
209	
210	**When it refuses**
211	
212	Nothing changes when there's no file at `path` ("No file at …"), when `track` names no track, when the file can't be read as text, when not one cue in it can be read, when a track you named takes none of the cues, or when it would take the project past its limit of 4,096 clips. [When a file can't be read](/captions/import-captions/#when-a-file-cant-be-read) has the sentences.
213	
214	## `export_captions`
215	
216	Writes one text track out as a subtitle file, one cue for each text clip, at the time it sits at and in the order they play. It does what [**File ▸ Export Captions…**](/captions/export-captions/) does. It edits nothing and makes no undo step.
217	
218	**Arguments**
219	
220	| Argument | Type | Required | What it does |
221	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
222	| `path` | string | Yes | Where to write, for example `~/Movies/talk.srt`. The folder must exist. A trailing `.srt` or `.vtt` is replaced by the format's own. Any other extension stays as part of the name, so `chart.png` becomes `chart.png.srt`. |
223	| `format` | string | No | `srt` (SubRip) or `vtt` (WebVTT). By default the path's own extension when it's one of those, otherwise `srt`. A format you name wins over the path's extension. |
224	| `track` | integer | No | The track to write. Leave it out when exactly one track holds only text clips. |
225	| `project` | string | No | The path of the open project to act on, as `get_project` reports it. The frontmost project when left out. |
226	
227	**What it answers**
228	
229	`path` (the file really written, which can differ from what you asked for), `format`, `track`, `track_name`, `cues` (how many were written) and the `project` summary.
230	
231	**When it refuses**
232	
233	The track is never guessed, because writing the wrong track and reporting success is worse than asking. Nothing is written when:
234	
235	- No track holds only text clips.
236	- Several do and `track` is left out. The answer lists each candidate by id and name, front-most first. Call again with `track`.
237	- `track` names no track, holds a clip that isn't text, or has no caption text on it.
238	- The folder doesn't exist, or the file can't be written.
239	
240	The built-in Assistant asks you before it runs this tool, because it writes a file.
241	
242	**Round trips.** Exported and brought back with `import_captions`, every cue returns to the tick it was written from, at every ordinary frame rate. The file itself may not match one you first imported. See [Frame-exact round trips](/captions/export-captions/#frame-exact-round-trips).
243	
244	## `relay_captions`
245	
246	Pages word captions again for the current canvas, from the words their pages hold, so every correction is kept. It does what [**File ▸ Re-lay Captions for This Canvas**](/captions/re-lay-captions/) does, and it's the step to take after `set_canvas`.
247	
248	It looks at every track named **Captions** or **Captions N** holding only text clips, in the timeline or in the open nest at the nest's size. A track whose pages are all in one of the five word styles, with its looks, is paged again and put back at the same place in the stack, with the same name, hidden and locked as before. It's one undo step, **Re-lay Captions**.
249	
250	**Arguments**
251	
252	| Argument | Type | Required | What it does |
253	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
254	| `project` | string | No | The path of the open project to act on, as `get_project` reports it. The frontmost project when left out. |
255	
256	**What it answers**
257	
258	| Key | What it holds |
259	| --- | --- |
260	| `relaid` | Each track paged again: `track` (the new track), `replaced` (the old one), `name`, `style` and `pages`. |
261	| `kept` | Each track left as placed: `track`, `name` and `reason`. |
262	
263	It also has the ids of what it created and the `project` summary.
264	
265	A track is kept when it's a matte track, holds a page with no word timings (Subtitles pages included), holds a page none of whose words starts inside it, holds a page in a style Frame Job doesn't make, has pages in more than one style, or wouldn't fit the project's clip limit. [Tracks kept as placed](/captions/re-lay-captions/#tracks-kept-as-placed) explains each reason.
266	
267	**When it refuses**
268	
269	With nothing it can re-lay, nothing changes and the answer begins "relay_captions found no caption track it can re-lay:", followed by each kept track and its reason, or "there is no track named Captions holding only text clips".
270	
271	## `get_transcript`
272	
273	Reads one clip's spoken words with their times on the timeline, ready for `ripple_delete_ranges`. Use it when you care about one clip. To work across the timeline, or to cut exactly where the Transcript tab would, use [`get_timeline_transcript`](#get_timeline_transcript). The Assistant uses this tool to [cut a false start](/cleanup/false-starts/). No menu item shows these words clip by clip. The nearest view is the [Transcript tab](/captions/transcript-tab/). The tool edits nothing, makes no undo step and never uploads anything.
274	
275	**Arguments**
276	
277	| Argument | Type | Required | What it does |
278	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
279	| `clip` | integer | Yes | The clip whose words to read, in its own timeline position and speed. |
280	| `language` | string | No | A language tag, such as `en-US`, for this Mac's recogniser only. By default this Mac's own language. A kept AssemblyAI transcript answers in its own language. |
281	| `from` | integer | No | Where on the timeline to start, in ticks, snapped to frames. The clip's start by default. See [The from and to window](#the-from-and-to-window). |
282	| `to` | integer | No | Where on the timeline to stop, in ticks, snapped to frames. The clip's end by default. Must be after `from`. |
283	| `project` | string | No | The path of the open project to act on, as `get_project` reports it. The frontmost project when left out. |
284	
285	**What it answers**
286	
287	| Key | What it holds |
288	| --- | --- |
289	| `words` | The words sorted by start, each with `text`, `start`, `end` and `filler`, and `speaker` where the transcript labelled it. |
290	| `count` | How many words came back. |
291	| `engine` | `assemblyai` for a kept transcript, or `apple` for this Mac's recogniser. |
292	| `language` | The language of the words, when known. |
293	| `fillers_reported` | Whether the transcript was made with filler words. See [Fillers in a transcript](#fillers-in-a-transcript). |
294	| `cached` | With engine `apple`, whether the answer came from what was already heard. |
295	| `clip`, `media` | The clip and its media file. |
296	| `from`, `to` | The window read, when one was given. |
297	| `note` | Anything to know: no words were heard, fillers may be missing, or word starts haven't been moved yet. |
298	| `project` | The project summary. |
299	
300	**When it refuses**
301	
302	- The clip doesn't exist, or it has no words to read: "Clip 3 has no words to read: its audio is switched off." The reason can also be that it isn't a media file, plays in reverse, has no audio track, or that its file is missing.
303	- The window is empty, or outside the clip.
304	- The `language` tag is misspelt. The answer lists the tags speech recognition knows, 24 at most.
305	- There's no kept transcript and the language's speech model isn't installed. The tool never downloads one. A person installs it from **File ▸ Generate Captions…**.
306	- A read fails, or is stopped, and the answer gives the recogniser's sentence.
307	
308	### Where the words come from
309	
310	The words come from the file's current AssemblyAI transcript, kept in the project, when it has one. That transcript comes from an earlier AssemblyAI run, such as [`transcribe`](#transcribe) or the sheet. Otherwise this Mac's own speech recogniser runs over the clip, which takes seconds per minute of speech. Reading never uses the network and needs no key.
311	
312	- **Where a word starts.** An on-device word's start is moved to where its sound begins, using the file's voice detection and waveform. The recogniser's own start is often early, inside the pause before the word. Until voice detection has finished with the file, starts are the recogniser's and `note` says so, so ask again once it has. AssemblyAI words and every word's end are as transcribed.
313	- **Saved for next time.** What the recogniser heard is saved in the project for each media file and language. A later request inside a stretch it has heard comes back at once, even from another clip of the same file at another speed, and `cached` says so. It's used only while the media file and the macOS version are unchanged.
314	- **Speed.** Words are placed through the clip's speed, including a speed ramp, so their times match what plays on the timeline.
315	- **Language.** On-device recognition uses this Mac's language unless `language` names another.
316	- **Stopping.** The Assistant's **Stop** ends a long on-device read, and nothing is saved from a stopped read.
317	
318	### Fillers in a transcript
319	
320	`filler` is true for um, uh, hmm, mhm, uh-huh, ah, huh, hm, m, er and erm, in any case and with punctuation at their edges trimmed.
321	
322	`fillers_reported` says whether the transcript was made with filler words at all. It's false for every on-device read, and for a kept transcript made without them. A filler can then be in the audio and missing from `words`, and `note` says so. See [Transcripts for filler words](/cleanup/filler-transcripts/).
323	
324	### The from and to window
325	
326	`from` and `to` are timeline times, and they return only the words that overlap that part of the timeline. A word crossing an edge comes back whole, with its own times.
327	
328	Either end can be given alone. A missing `from` is the clip's start and a missing `to` is its end. The window is held inside the clip, and the answer gives it back as `from` and `to`. An empty window, or one wholly outside the clip, is refused.
329	
330	With a window, the on-device recogniser hears only that part and 2 s either side. That's faster, but a windowed read can differ slightly from a read of the whole clip.
331	
332	## `get_timeline_transcript`
333	
334	Reads every word heard on the timeline, or inside the open nest, in timeline order, with nested clips included. Each word carries the range the [Transcript tab](/captions/transcript-tab/) would cut it by. It edits nothing, makes no undo step, never makes a network request and needs no key.
335	
336	**Arguments**
337	
338	| Argument | Type | Required | What it does |
339	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
340	| `from` | integer | No | Where on the timeline to start, in ticks, snapped to frames. The timeline's start by default. A word across this edge comes back whole. |
341	| `to` | integer | No | Where on the timeline to stop, in ticks, snapped to frames. The timeline's end by default. Must be after `from`. |
342	| `tracks` | array of integers | No | Only the words playing on these timeline tracks. Every track by default. |
343	| `language` | string | No | A language tag, such as `en-US`, for this Mac's recogniser only. By default this Mac's own language. Each language is kept apart, and a kept AssemblyAI transcript answers in its own language. |
344	| `project` | string | No | The path of the open project to act on, as `get_project` reports it. The frontmost project when left out. |
345	
346	**What it answers**
347	
348	| Key | What it holds |
349	| --- | --- |
350	| `words` | Each word, ordered by start, then end, then the front track first. Its keys are below. |
351	| `count` | How many words are on this page. |
352	| `pauses` | Each pause. See [Cut words and pauses](#cut-words-and-pauses). |
353	| `media` | Each file read, with `media`, `engine`, `language` and `fillers_reported`. |
354	| `no_words` | Clips that can't be read, each with `clip`, `nest_path`, `tag` and `reason`. |
355	| `notes` | Sentences to read: the same speech twice, words not transcribed with fillers, or word starts not moved yet. |
356	| `from`, `to` | The window read, when one was given. |
357	| `truncated`, `next_from` | Present when there's more. See [Paging](#paging). |
358	| `project` | The project summary. |
359	
360	Each word has these keys:
361	
362	| Key | What it holds |
363	| --- | --- |
364	| `text`, `start`, `end` | The word and its timeline times. |
365	| `clip`, `track`, `media` | The clip it comes from, the timeline track it plays on and its media file. A nested word's track is its nest clip's. |
366	| `engine` | `assemblyai` or `apple`. |
367	| `filler` | True for a [filler word](#fillers-in-a-transcript). |
368	| `speaker` | The speaker, when the transcript labelled one. |
369	| `editable`, `why` | Whether cutting it is safe, and why not when it isn't. |
370	| `id` | The word's identity across edits. |
371	| `cut_start`, `cut_end` | The range the Transcript tab cuts this word by. |
372	
373	**When it refuses**
374	
375	- `to` isn't after `from`, or the window is wholly outside the timeline.
376	- A `tracks` id names no track.
377	- The `language` tag is misspelt.
378	- A file needs this Mac's recogniser and the language's speech model isn't installed. The tool never downloads one.
379	- A read fails, or is stopped, and the answer gives the recogniser's sentence.
380	
381	### Heard words and editable words
382	
383	Words come from every clip that plays speech from a media file, clips inside nests included. A clip that's muted, soloed out or at volume 0 isn't heard and gives no words.
384	
385	A clip whose words can't be read is listed under `no_words` with the reason instead: its audio switched off, played in reverse, or its file missing, for example.
386	
387	`editable` is false, with a sentence in `why`, for a word:
388	
389	- inside a nest. Open the nest with `set_scope` and read again to cut words inside it. A person opens one with **Clip ▸ Open Nest**, <kbd>⌘↓</kbd>.
390	- under a transition, where a cut would leave one clip's tail under its neighbour.
391	- on a locked track, where a cut would leave the word in place and move everything after it.
392	
393	`id` names a word across edits elsewhere on the timeline. It has four parts:
394	
395	| Part | What it is |
396	| --- | --- |
397	| `nest_path` | The nest clips the word plays through. |
398	| `media` | Its media file. |
399	| `source` | Its start in the media's own time, in ticks, as the recogniser put it. |
400	| `k` | How many earlier words have the same three, which is 0 unless one piece of the file plays twice. |
401	
402	### Read once per file
403	
404	Each file without a current AssemblyAI transcript is read whole by this Mac's recogniser the first time it's needed, at about 0.7 s per minute of speech on an M2 Max. The words are saved in the project, so a later call answers at once.
405	
406	Trimming a clip, adding another clip of the same file, or reading again later doesn't read the file again. The saved words are used while the file and the macOS version stay the same. The Assistant's **Stop** ends a read, and nothing is saved from a stopped read. The Transcript tab's own **Stop** leaves an agent's read running. See [Where the transcript's words come from](/captions/transcript-words/).
407	
408	An on-device word's start is moved to its sound as in [`get_transcript`](#where-the-words-come-from), and `notes` names any file still waiting for voice detection.
409	
410	### Duplicate speech
411	
412	When two clips of different files carry the same speech at the same time, such as a camera's sound and a separate microphone, `notes` names the pair and both sets of words stay in `words`. Mute one, or switch its audio off, to read the speech once.
413	
414	### Paging
415	
416	At most 2,000 words come back in one answer. When there's more, `truncated` is true and `next_from` says where to call again. Pass it as `from`.
417	
418	A word overlapping that point can come back again on the next page, with the same `id`, so match words by `id`. A pause is listed on the page that holds the word before it.
419	
420	### Cut words and pauses
421	
422	`cut_start` and `cut_end` are the range the Transcript tab cuts a word by when it alone is deleted, snapped to frames. The range runs from where the word's sound starts to where the next word's sound starts, at most 1 s past the word's end, widened over any other track's word it would cut into. See [Where a word cut falls](/captions/delete-words/#where-a-word-cut-falls).
423	
424	To cut a run of words:
425	
426	<Steps>
427	
428	1. Call `get_timeline_transcript` and find the words.
429	
430	2. Check that each word in the run has `editable` true.
431	
432	3. Call [`ripple_delete_ranges`](/mcp/tools-cut-and-delete/#ripple_delete_ranges) once, with one range in `ranges`, from the first word's `cut_start` to the last word's `cut_end`.
433	
434	4. Read the transcript again before the next cut, because everything after a cut moves. The ids still name the same words.
435	
436	</Steps>
437	
438	Each row of `pauses` is a silence over 1 s between two words of one clip, read from voice detection:
439	
440	| Key | What it holds |
441	| --- | --- |
442	| `start`, `end` | Where the silence runs. |
443	| `cut_start`, `cut_end` | What the Transcript tab cuts when the pause is deleted, with 0.2 s kept at each end, snapped to frames. |
444	| `clip`, `track`, `media` | Where it is. |
445	| `follows`, `precedes` | The ids of the words before and after it. |
446	
447	To shorten a pause, call `ripple_delete_ranges` with `[[cut_start, cut_end]]` as `ranges`. Not every silence is listed. See [When a pause isn't shown](/captions/shorten-pauses/#when-a-pause-isnt-shown).

459	title: "Tools: clean-up"
460	description: "The agent tools that find silences and filler words as ranges, make a filler transcript, and cut what they found."
461	---
462	
463	These tools find what [Remove Silences](/cleanup/remove-silences/) and [Remove Filler Words](/cleanup/remove-filler-words/) would cut. The two `detect_` tools change nothing, so you can read and adjust their ranges before making the cut.
464	
465	Neither `detect_` tool takes `scope`. They work in whatever nest `set_scope` has open. See [Editing inside a nest](/mcp/nests/).
466	
467	## Cut what the tools found
468	
469	Pass the `ranges` from `detect_silence` or `detect_fillers` to [`ripple_delete_ranges`](/mcp/tools-cut-and-delete/#ripple_delete_ranges). That's what **Remove** does in each sheet, and it makes the whole cut one undo step.
470	
471	```json
472	{ "ranges": [[1200000, 1500000], [3000000, 3240000]] }
473	```
474	
475	For filler words, look at `needs_transcript` in the `detect_fillers` answer first. Any media named there needs [`transcribe_for_fillers`](#transcribe_for_fillers) before its fillers can be found, so make the transcript and call `detect_fillers` again.
476	
477	An agent isn't held to the ranges it was given: it can drop some or change them first. `ripple_delete_ranges` takes `scope` like any edit, so it can reach a nest without opening it. See [How a clean-up cut works](/cleanup/how-cleanup-cuts-work/).
478	
479	## `detect_silence`
480	
481	Finds the quiet stretches of the timeline and reports them, changing nothing. It's what **Clip ▸ Remove Silences…** shows you before you choose **Remove**, see [Remove Silences](/cleanup/remove-silences/).
482	
483	The voice model runs on your Mac, with no key and no upload.
484	
485	| Argument | Type | Required | What it does |
486	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
487	| `clips` | array of integers | No | Analyse only these clips, like the sheet's **Selected clips**. At least one. Default: the current selection when it holds anything with sound, otherwise every audible clip. |
488	| `mode` | string | No | `voice` judges by the voice model, falling back to level over a clip that holds no voice. `level` judges by level alone. Default: `voice`. |
489	| `voice_confidence` | number | No | Voice mode only. The model's probability, 0.1 to 0.9, at or above which a moment counts as speech. Default: 0.5. The sheet doesn't offer this. |
490	| `threshold_db` | number | No | Quieter than this counts as silence, in dBFS in the mix, at or below 0. Default: −40. |
491	| `min_length` | integer | No | The shortest quiet run worth cutting, in ticks. Default: 300,000 (0.5 s). |
492	| `padding` | integer | No | How much to leave at each end of a run, in ticks. Default: 60,000 (0.1 s). |
493	| `project` | string | No | Path of the open project to act on. Default: the frontmost one. |
494	
495	`min_length` and `padding` run exactly as sent. Only the finished ranges go on the frame grid, and they snap inward, which can leave a frame of room tone rather than clip the next word. Each takes 0 to 9,000,000,000,000,000.
496	
497	Quiet is measured in the mix, so a clip's volume, fades, ducking, mute and another track's solo all count. In either mode, a moment the mix alone turns down to `threshold_db` or below is quiet.
498	
499	A moment none of the measured clips covers isn't a candidate, because a hole in the timeline isn't dead air. A nest clip is a wall: no range reaches into one.
500	
501	**Answers:**
502	
503	| Key | What it says |
504	| --- | --- |
505	| `ranges`, `count`, `removes` | The spans as `[from, to]` pairs in ticks, how many, and how many ticks they remove. |
506	| `scope`, `clips` | `selected` or `audible`, and the clips that ran. This `scope` is about clips, not nests. |
507	| `mode`, `threshold_db`, `min_length`, `padding`, `voice_confidence` | What actually ran. |
508	| `judged_by_level`, `judged_by_level_clips` | The media and the clips judged by level because they hold no voice. |
509	| `proposed_by_mix_clips` | Each clip a range is proposed inside only because the mix turns it down while its analysis is still running. |
510	| `pending_peaks` | Media still being analysed, for either the waveform or speech. Call again shortly. |
511	| `voice_pending` | Media whose speech is still being analysed. |
512	| `protected_nests` | Each nest clip a quiet run of at least `min_length` crossed. There may be dead air inside. |
513	| `note` | Sentences on any of the above. |
514	| `project` | The [project summary](/mcp/what-a-call-answers/). |
515	
516	`proposed_by_mix_clips`, `pending_peaks`, `voice_pending`, `protected_nests` and `note` appear only when they have something to report. To look inside a protected nest, open it with `set_scope` and call again.
517	
518	**Refuses:**
519	
520	- `voice_confidence` in level mode, or outside its range.
521	- `mode: "voice"` when the voice model can't be used. Leave `mode` out instead and it falls back to level with a note.
522	- A `threshold_db` above 0.
523	- A `min_length` or `padding` that's negative or too long.
524	
525	See [What counts as silent](/cleanup/voice-or-level/).
526	
527	## `detect_fillers`
528	
529	Finds the filler words in the timeline's speech and reports them as ranges, changing nothing. It's what **Clip ▸ Remove Filler Words…** shows you before you choose **Remove**, see [Remove Filler Words](/cleanup/remove-filler-words/).
530	
531	The fillers it knows are ah, er, erm, hm, hmm, huh, m, mhm, uh, uh-huh and um.
532	
533	| Argument | Type | Required | What it does |
534	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
535	| `clips` | array of integers | No | Read only these clips. At least one. Default: the current selection when it holds a clip with speech from a media file, otherwise every clip. |
536	| `project` | string | No | Path of the open project to act on. Default: the frontmost one. |
537	
538	It reads only a saved AssemblyAI transcript that asked for filler words, and never uses the network, so it needs no key. Making that transcript does, see [`transcribe_for_fillers`](#transcribe_for_fillers).
539	
540	Each run of fillers is widened outward to a 32 ms grid, never into the words beside it, then its edges snap inward to the frame grid.
541	
542	**Answers:**
543	
544	| Key | What it says |
545	| --- | --- |
546	| `ranges`, `count`, `removes` | The merged spans as `[from, to]` pairs in ticks, how many, and how many ticks they remove. |
547	| `fillers` | Each kept run, with its `clip`, `words` and `range`. |
548	| `dropped` | Each run left in, with its `clip`, `words` and `reason`. |
549	| `needs_transcript` | Media with no such transcript. [`transcribe_for_fillers`](#transcribe_for_fillers) makes one. |
550	| `locked` | Clips on a locked track, which weren't read, because `ripple_delete_ranges` neither cuts nor moves a locked track. |
551	| `scope`, `clips` | `selected` or `all`, and the clips that ran. |
552	| `skipped` | When you named `clips`, each one it couldn't read, with the reason. |
553	| `note` | Sentences on any of the above. |
554	| `project` | The project summary. |
555	
556	A filler is dropped whole when:
557	
558	- it's too short once it's on both grids
559	- it overlaps a word of another clip on any unlocked track, because the cut reaches every unlocked track, not only the clips it read
560	- it crosses a nest clip
561	- it crosses a transition
562	
563	## `transcribe_for_fillers`
564	
565	Re-transcribes one media file with AssemblyAI so its filler words can be found. It's the **Transcribe** button beside a file in **Clip ▸ Remove Filler Words…**, see [Filler transcripts](/cleanup/filler-transcripts/).
566	
567	:::caution
568	This is a paid upload to AssemblyAI, even over a transcript that's current for captions. It needs your AssemblyAI key, and the built-in Assistant can't use this tool.
569	:::
570	
571	| Argument | Type | Required | What it does |
572	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
573	| `media` | integer | Yes | The media to transcribe, one of `detect_fillers`' `needs_transcript`. |
574	| `project` | string | No | Path of the open project to act on. Default: the frontmost one. |
575	
576	It keeps the media's previous request (its language, speaker labels and vocabulary) and adds filler words. A media with no previous request gets language detection, no speakers and no vocabulary.
577	
578	It writes only the media's transcript cache: no caption is placed and no undo step is made.
579	
580	A media that already has a transcript made with filler words makes no request and needs no key. It answers `ready: true` and an empty `uploaded`.
581	
582	**Answers:**
583	
584	| Key | What it says |
585	| --- | --- |
586	| `ready` | Whether `detect_fillers` can now read the media. |
587	| `media` | The media id. |
588	| `uploaded`, `cached` | The media uploaded, and the media answered from the cache. |
589	| `audio_seconds` | The seconds of audio billed. |
590	| `engine`, `language` | `assemblyai`, and the language code or `auto`. |
591	| `note` | Present when there's something to say. |
592	| `project` | The project summary. |
593	
594	**Refuses:**
595	
596	- A document with nowhere to keep its transcript cache. Save it first.
597	- A media no clip plays from its file.
598	- With no key, where it would upload: "No AssemblyAI API key is set. Set one in Frame Job ▸ Settings… ▸ Transcription."

626	## `get_media_analysis`
627	
628	Reads an analysis of one media file, or of the part of it one clip plays. No menu item shows these results as numbers. **View ▸ Show Subjects** [draws](/framing/show-subjects/) the selected clip's faces and subjects at the playhead, from what's already been found, and never starts an analysis itself.
629	
630	| `kind` | What it finds |
631	| --- | --- |
632	| [`shots`](#kind-shots) | The hard cuts. |
633	| [`masks`](#kind-masks) | Where a person is, as runs of frames. |
634	| [`faces`](#kind-faces) | Every face, 10 times a second, with its tilt and how open the mouth is. |
635	| [`subjects`](#kind-subjects) | People and the regions the eye is drawn to, 10 times a second. |
636	| [`sound_events`](#kind-sound_events) | How likely laughter, applause, cheering, a crowd, music and speech are, every 0.75 s. |
637	
638	**Arguments**
639	
640	| Argument | Type | Required | What it does |
641	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
642	| `kind` | string | Yes | What to find: `shots`, `masks`, `faces`, `sound_events` or `subjects`. |
643	| `media` | integer | One of `media` and `clip` | The media file to analyse. |
644	| `clip` | integer | One of `media` and `clip` | A media clip. Its file is analysed over the part the clip plays. |
645	| `from` | integer | No | Where to start, in the file's own time played forwards, in ticks, not snapped. The file's start, or the start of the part the clip plays, by default. |
646	| `to` | integer | No | Where to stop, not included, in the file's own time. The file's end, or the end of the part the clip plays, by default. Must be after `from`. |
647	| `project` | string | No | The path of the open project to act on, as `get_project` reports it. The frontmost project when left out. |
648	
649	`from` and `to` are file times, not timeline times. They're held inside the file, and with `clip` they're held inside the part the clip plays.
650	
651	**What it answers**
652	
653	Every kind answers these, as well as its own keys below:
654	
655	| Key | What it holds |
656	| --- | --- |
657	| `kind`, `media` | What was asked for and the file it was read from. |
658	| `clip` | The clip, when you named one. |
659	| `from`, `to` | The window that was read. |
660	| `size` | The media's upright picture size, as width and height. |
661	| `cached` | True when the answer came from the cache alone. |
662	| `stamp` | What the cache was made with. |
663	| `run` | Present only when this call ran the analysis: `queued_at`, `started_at` and `ended_at`, in seconds of the app's uptime. |
664	| `project` | The project summary. |
665	
666	With `clip`, each cut, sample or window also has `clip_time`, in ticks from the clip's start in its playing direction, through its speed, ramp and reversal, and `timeline`, the clip's start plus `clip_time`.
667	
668	**When it refuses**
669	
670	- You named both `media` and `clip`, or neither.
671	- `kind` isn't one of the five. The answer lists them.
672	- A media or clip id names nothing, or the clip isn't a media clip, so it has no media to analyse.
673	- A picture kind is asked of a file with no moving picture, which includes a still image: "Media 4 has no moving picture, so it has no shots to find."
674	- `sound_events` is asked of a file with no sound, or of a clip that plays in reverse, whose sound runs backwards.
675	- The file is missing. `relink_media` points it at the file.
676	- `to` isn't after `from` once both are held inside the file or the clip.
677	- The analysis fails, or the Assistant's **Stop** ends it.
678	- The kept results can't be read. The answer says which cache files to remove so they're made again.
679	
680	### Long analyses and big answers
681	
682	A call waits at most 60 s. After that it stops and says how much of the window was covered, for example "The faces analysis of media 2 covered 41.0 s of the window's 120.0 s in the 60 s a call waits; what it covered is kept — call again to continue." What was covered is kept, so another call carries on from there.
683	
684	An answer over 512 KiB of cuts, runs, samples or windows is refused, and the sentence names the largest `to` that fits. So read a long file in `from` and `to` windows. Here's how much fits in one answer:
685	
686	| Kind | One row | One answer holds |
687	| --- | --- | --- |
688	| `faces` | About 176 bytes with one face, 221 with `clip` | About 296 s of samples, 236 s with `clip`, and less with more faces in frame. Read about 2 minutes at a time. |
689	| `subjects` | About 177 bytes with one person and one salient box, 222 with `clip` | About 294 s of samples, 235 s with `clip` |
690	| `sound_events` | About 130 bytes | About an hour of windows |
691	
692	### `kind: shots`
693	
694	Finds the hard cuts. It answers `count` and `cuts`, sorted by time. Each cut has `frame`, the file's frame index, and `source`, its time in the file.
695	
696	- A cut inside a gradual dissolve isn't reported.
697	- A single flash frame isn't a cut.
698	- A dissolve between flat-coloured pictures, such as slides or title cards, can show as one cut.
699	
700	[`split_at_shots`](/mcp/tools-cut-and-delete/#split_at_shots) cuts clips at these moments. See [Split at Shot Changes](/editing/split-at-shot-changes/).
701	
702	### `kind: masks`
703	
704	Finds a person's outline in every frame and answers where a person is, never the masks themselves.
705	
706	| Key | What it holds |
707	| --- | --- |
708	| `mask_size` | The masks' own width and height. |
709	| `frames` | How many frames in the window have been analysed. |
710	| `subject_found` | Whether any frame holds a person. |
711	| `count` | How many runs there are. |
712	| `runs` | Each run of consecutive frames that agree, with `from`, `to`, `subject_found` and `frames`, in the file's own time. |
713	
714	A frame holds a person when at least 0.5 % of its mask is above half strength. `runs` have no `clip_time` or `timeline`, even with `clip`.
715	
716	[Remove Background](/effects/remove-background/) draws these masks. A still picture's masks aren't this tool's. Use [`analyze_cutout`](#analyze_cutout) for those.
717	
718	### `kind: faces`
719	
720	Finds every face at 10 samples a second of the file's own time. It answers `rate`, `count` and `samples`.
721	
722	| Sample key | What it holds |
723	| --- | --- |
724	| `source` | The sample's instant in the file. |
725	| `frame` | The time of the frame it read, the first at or after `source` within one sample, or null. |
726	| `faces` | Each face in the sample. |
727	
728	| Face key | What it holds |
729	| --- | --- |
730	| `box` | `[x, y, w, h]`, from 0 to 1 of the upright picture, measured from its top-left corner. |
731	| `confidence` | How sure the detection is. |
732	| `roll`, `yaw` | How far the face is tilted and turned, in radians. |
733	| `mouth_gap` | The inner lips' height, over the face box's height. |
734	| `mouth_width` | The outer lips' width, over the face box's height. |
735	
736	`mouth_gap` over `mouth_width` is how open the mouth is. Values are rounded to 4 decimals, and are null where no value was found.
737	
738	Faces are ordered from left to right and carry no identity or name. To follow one, follow its box from sample to sample.
739	
740	### `kind: subjects`
741	
742	Finds people and the regions the eye is drawn to, at 10 samples a second. Every sample instant is also a `faces` sample. It answers `rate`, `count` and `samples`.
743	
744	Each sample has `source` and `frame`, as `faces` does, then `people` and `salient`. Both are lists of `box` and `confidence`, with boxes measured as faces' are and ordered from left to right, with no identity. A person box covers the head and shoulders. See [Subjects in the picture](/framing/what-is-found/).
745	
746	### `kind: sound_events`
747	
748	Listens to the file's first sound track with Apple's Sound Analysis, in windows of 1.5 s that start every 0.75 s, and says how sure it is of six kinds of sound: laughter, applause, cheering, crowd, music and speech. It needs a file with sound, and an audio file works.
749	
750	| Key | What it holds |
751	| --- | --- |
752	| `window`, `hop` | The window's length and the step between windows, in ticks: 900,000 and 450,000. |
753	| `groups` | Each kind of sound, with `name`, `labels`, `first_class` and `threshold`. `labels` are the classifier's own labels behind that kind, and its confidence is the highest of theirs. |
754	| `count` | How many windows came back. |
755	| `windows` | Each window, with `source`, its start in the file, and a confidence from 0 to 1 for each of the six kinds. |
756	
757	Confidences are rounded to 4 decimals, and are null where a window runs past the end of the sound.
758	
759	:::note
760	Treat these as hints, never as a finding on their own. None of the six has been checked against labelled recordings, so `first_class` is false and `threshold` is null for all of them.
761	:::
762	
763	## `analyze_cutout`
764	
765	Reports where Remove Background stands for cut-out clips and makes their masks now. It's the agent's version of **Status** and [**Analyze Now**](/effects/remove-background/#analyze-now) in the Clip tab's **Picture ▸ Background** section.
766	
767	A cut-out clip is one with Remove Background on, through **Clip ▸ Remove Background**, the section's checkbox, or `cutout` in [`set_video`](/mcp/tools-set-video/). A clip's masks are made as soon as that's set, so an agent needs this tool only to wait for them or to read how they went. A still picture counts, and its one frame is made from the picture itself.
768	
769	A call asks for every frame the clips play and runs again an analysis that failed or was stopped. Frames already analysed are never analysed again. It then waits up to `wait` seconds for every clip to settle, which means reaching any state but `analyzing`. Running out of time isn't an error. The answer gives the state so far, and you call again to keep waiting. The Assistant's **Stop** ends the wait.
770	
771	**Arguments**
772	
773	| Argument | Type | Required | What it does |
774	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
775	| `clips` | array of integers | No | The cut-out clips to answer for. Left out, every cut-out clip in the timeline or nest that's open, in timeline order. |
776	| `wait` | number | No | How many seconds to wait for every clip to settle, from 0 to 60. Left out, it's 0, which answers now. |
777	| `project` | string | No | The path of the open project to act on, as `get_project` reports it. The frontmost project when left out. |
778	
779	**What it answers**
780	
781	`clips`, a row for each clip, and the `project` summary. Each row has these keys:
782	
783	| Key | What it holds |
784	| --- | --- |
785	| `clip`, `media` | The clip and its media file. |
786	| `state` | Where it stands. See the next table. |
787	| `progress` | From 0 to 1. |
788	| `quality` | The clip's cutout quality, `standard` or `best`. |
789	| `frames` | How many frames of the file the clip plays, which is 1 for a picture. |
790	| `covered` | How many of those are analysed. |
791	| `ready` | Whether `covered` equals `frames`. |
792	| `subject_found` | Whether a subject was found. |
793	| `centroid` | `x` and `y`, the subject's mean centre over those frames, in the media's upright pixels from the top left with y going down. Null unless the state is `ready`. The app doesn't show this figure. |
794	| `error` | With `failed`, the sentence saying why. |
795	
796	| `state` | What it means | The app's **Status** |
797	| --- | --- | --- |
798	| `analyzing` | The masks are being made. | **Analyzing N %** |
799	| `ready` | Every frame is analysed, and a person, or a picture's foreground subject, was found. | **Ready** |
800	| `no_person` | Every frame is analysed and no person is in the clip, so it draws whole. | **No person found** |
801	| `no_subject` | A picture with subject `foreground` has no subject, so it draws whole. | **No subject found** |
802	| `failed` | The masks couldn't be made. | **Failed:** and the reason |
803	| `no_picture` | The clip plays no frame of its file. | **No picture to analyze** |
804	
805	**When it refuses**
806	
807	Nothing is done when:
808	
809	- `wait` is outside 0 to 60: "wait must be from 0 to 60 seconds."
810	- A clip id names nothing, or `clips` is empty.
811	- A clip you named has no Remove Background: "Clip 3 has no Remove Background; set_video `{cutout: {}}` turns it on."
812	- With `clips` left out, no clip in the open timeline or nest has it on.
813

2	---
3	title: "Cut false starts"
4	description: "Ask the Assistant to find a phrase the speaker abandoned or said again, and cut it in one undo step."
5	---
6	
7	import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
8	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
9	
10	A false start is a phrase the speaker abandoned or said again. Deciding what counts is a judgement about meaning, so there's no menu command for it. You ask the [Assistant](/assistant/what-it-can-do/), and it finds the words and cuts them. To pick the words yourself, [delete them in the Transcript tab](/captions/delete-words/).
11	
12	<AtAGlance
13	  menu="View ▸ Assistant"
14	  keys="⌃⌘A"
15	  where="Inspector ▸ Assistant tab"
16	  tools={['get_timeline_transcript', 'get_transcript', 'ripple_delete_ranges']}
17	  needs="Your own Anthropic API key, set in Frame Job ▸ Settings… ▸ Assistant."
18	/>
19	
20	## Cut a false start with the Assistant
21	
22	<Steps>
23	
24	1. Select the clip if you're going to say "this clip". Each message tells the Assistant what's selected and where the playhead is.
25	
26	2. Open the Assistant tab with **View ▸ Assistant** (<kbd>⌃⌘A</kbd>).
27	
28	3. Ask for it, for example "cut the false start at the beginning of this clip."
29	
30	4. The Assistant reads the words and their times, tells you which words it will cut, and cuts them in one step.
31	
32	</Steps>
33	
34	It doesn't wait for a go-ahead between telling you and cutting. If it took the wrong words, press <kbd>⌘Z</kbd>. The **Edit** menu names the step **Undo Ripple Delete**.
35	
36	The Assistant cuts a false start only when you ask.
37	
38	## What gets cut
39	
40	The cut runs from the start of the first word to the start of the next word you keep, taking at most 1 second of the pause after the last cut word. That's the range the [Transcript tab](/captions/delete-words/) cuts when you delete the same words by hand.
41	
42	If that range would cut into a word on another unlocked track, it widens to take that whole word.
43	
44	The timeline closes over the cut, as it does for every clean-up cut. See [How a clean-up cut works](/cleanup/how-cleanup-cuts-work/).
45	
46	## Where the words come from
47	
48	The Assistant reads a file's saved AssemblyAI transcript when it has a current one. Otherwise it uses this Mac's own speech recogniser, which reads the whole file once and keeps the words in the project, so later reads are immediate.
49	
50	Neither way uploads audio or needs an AssemblyAI key. The words the Assistant reads do go to Anthropic as part of the conversation. See [Assistant privacy](/assistant/privacy/).
51	
52	## Remove fillers and silences by asking
53	
54	The Assistant can also do what the two clean-up sheets do.
55	
56	| Ask it to | What it does |
57	| --- | --- |
58	| Take out the silences | Finds the ranges [Remove Silences](/cleanup/remove-silences/) would cut, then cuts them all at once. |
59	| Remove the filler words | Finds the ranges [Remove Filler Words](/cleanup/remove-filler-words/) would cut, then cuts them all at once. |
60	
61	Each cut is one undo step, labelled **Undo Ripple Delete** rather than the sheet's name.
62	
63	The Assistant can find filler words this way only in files that already have a [cloud transcript made with filler words](/cleanup/filler-transcripts/). In any other file it finds none, and its search reports which files have no such transcript.
64	
65	## The Assistant won't start a paid transcription
66	
67	The Assistant can't start a paid filler transcription, so you press **Transcribe** in the sheet yourself. Choose **Clip ▸ Remove Filler Words…**, check the price on the file's row, and choose [Transcribe](/cleanup/filler-transcripts/#transcribe-a-file). Then ask the Assistant again, or choose **Remove** in the sheet.
68	
69	Audio leaves your Mac only when you choose it, with the price in front of you. The same goes for transcribing captions with AssemblyAI: use **File ▸ Generate Captions…**. See [What it won't do and what it asks first](/assistant/what-it-will-not-do/).
70	
71	## Good to know
72	
73	- A clip that's muted, soloed out or at volume 0 isn't heard, so it's left out of the timeline's words the Assistant reads.
74	- The cut goes across every unlocked track. A locked track is neither cut nor moved.
75	- With a [nest](/editing/nests/) open, the Assistant reads and cuts inside that nest, as you would.
76	- If a file has no cloud transcript and its language isn't installed on this Mac, the Assistant can't read it, and it can't download the language. Open **File ▸ Generate Captions…**, choose the language under **Language**, and press **Download**.
77

86	---
87	title: "Transcripts for filler words"
88	description: "Get the AssemblyAI transcript that Remove Filler Words reads, see what it costs, and know what happens to your audio and your captions."
89	---
90	
91	import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
92	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
93	
94	[Remove Filler Words](/cleanup/remove-filler-words/) reads filler words from an AssemblyAI transcript made with filler words, a filler transcript for short, because transcription on your Mac doesn't report them. This page explains which files already have one, how to get one for a file that doesn't, and what that means for your captions.
95	
96	<AtAGlance
97	  menu="Clip ▸ Remove Filler Words…"
98	  where="Frame Job ▸ Settings… ▸ Transcription, for the key"
99	  tools={['detect_fillers', 'transcribe_for_fillers']}
100	  needs="Your own AssemblyAI API key, unless every file you want to clean up already has a filler transcript."
101	/>
102	
103	## Filler words need a cloud transcript
104	
105	Filler removal is a cloud feature. You need [your own AssemblyAI API key](/captions/assemblyai-key/), set in **Frame Job ▸ Settings…** (<kbd>⌘,</kbd>) under **Transcription**. A transcript this Mac made is never used here, so without a key Frame Job can't find fillers in a file that has no filler transcript yet.
106	
107	### Every AssemblyAI transcription asks for fillers
108	
109	Any file you've captioned with AssemblyAI (**File ▸ Generate Captions…**, AssemblyAI engine) is already ready for Remove Filler Words, with no second upload.
110	
111	A file needs a new transcript only when:
112	
113	- it has never been transcribed in the cloud
114	- it was transcribed before Frame Job started asking for filler words
115	- the file itself has changed since it was transcribed
116	
117	## Transcribe a file
118	
119	<Steps>
120	
121	1. Choose **Clip ▸ Remove Filler Words…**. Files with no filler transcript are listed in the sheet.
122	
123	2. Read what the row would upload and what it would cost.
124	
125	3. Choose **Transcribe** on the row. One press sends one file, and only one file can run at a time.
126	
127	4. When the run finishes, the file drops off the list and its fillers join the count above the list.
128	
129	5. Repeat for any other file, then choose **Remove**.
130	
131	</Steps>
132	
133	Pressing **Transcribe** only updates that file's saved transcript. It places no captions and adds no undo step.
134	
135	The run keeps the choices the file was last transcribed with, its language, speaker labels and vocabulary, and adds filler words. A file that's never been transcribed uses language detection, no speakers and no vocabulary.
136	
137	:::caution
138	A listed file that already has a caption transcript is uploaded again. That older transcript was made without filler words, so this is a second paid transcription.
139	:::
140	
141	### The list of files with no transcript
142	
143	Each file the sheet reads that has no filler transcript gets a row, under the heading "Filler words are found only in an AssemblyAI transcript made with filler words — transcription on this Mac does not report them. These files have none yet:". The whole section is hidden when every file the sheet reads has a filler transcript.
144	
145	A row has the file's name, an estimate and a **Transcribe** button. The estimate reads, for example:
146	
147	`1 file to upload · 00:00:05.249 of audio · under $0.01 at AssemblyAI's published rate`
148	
149	The upload is the whole file's audio, not only the part your clips play. Rest the pointer on the estimate to see the rate. It's $0.21 an hour, or $0.23 an hour when the file's earlier transcript used speaker labels.
150	
151	The list covers [the same clips as the rest of the sheet](/cleanup/remove-filler-words/#which-clips-are-read): the selected clips when the selection holds a clip Frame Job can read, otherwise every clip. A file is listed only if one of those clips plays its sound. Clips that play in reverse, clips with their sound switched off, clips on a locked track and clips whose file is missing don't count. A clip inside a [nest](/editing/nests/) counts only while that nest is open.
152	
153	### Where the audio goes
154	
155	Above the rows, the sheet says where the audio goes before anything is sent:
156	
157	> The audio of these files is uploaded to AssemblyAI (United States), transcribed with Universal-3.5 Pro, and deleted from AssemblyAI once the words have been read back. Nothing is uploaded until Transcribe is pressed.
158	
159	It names European Union instead when that's the **Region:** set in Settings, and it follows a change you make with the sheet open. See [What goes to AssemblyAI](/captions/assemblyai-privacy/).
160	
161	### Progress and Stop
162	
163	While a run goes, its row shows where it has got to, starting with **Starting…** and then a phase with a percentage:
164	
165	| The row reads | What's happening |
166	| --- | --- |
167	| Extracting *file* | Frame Job is pulling the audio out of the file. |
168	| Uploading *file* · 12 MB of 40 | The audio is on its way to AssemblyAI. |
169	| Submitting *file* | Frame Job is asking AssemblyAI to transcribe it. |
170	| Waiting for AssemblyAI · 8 s | AssemblyAI is working on it. |
171	| Saving *file* | The words are back and being saved. |
172	
173	The row's button reads **Stop**. The other rows' buttons are disabled, and so is **Remove**, so <kbd>Return</kbd> can't make a cut in the middle of a paid upload.
174	
175	Press **Stop** to end the run. Closing the sheet stops it too.
176	
177	### When a run ends
178	
179	When a run finishes, the file drops off the list and its fillers join the count.
180	
181	If it doesn't finish, the file stays on the list and the reason appears in the small note under the count, where it stays until the next run. After **Stop** the note reads "The transcription was cancelled."
182	
183	## When Transcribe is disabled
184	
185	A row's **Transcribe** button can be dimmed for two reasons.
186	
187	| What you see | Why | What to do |
188	| --- | --- | --- |
189	| The note and the button's tooltip read "No AssemblyAI API key is set. Set one in Frame Job ▸ Settings… ▸ Transcription." | There's no API key. | Save a key in Settings. The buttons turn on with the sheet still open. |
190	| The other rows' **Transcribe** buttons are disabled, and one row reads **Stop** | Another file's run is going. | Wait for it, or stop it. |
191	
192	## With no key
193	
194	You can only cut fillers without a key in a file that already has a filler transcript. With no key and no such file, the command stays off.
195	
196	### The menu item with no key
197	
198	With no key, the menu item is greyed and reads **Remove Filler Words… (needs your AssemblyAI key)**. Resting the pointer on it says "No AssemblyAI API key is set. Set one in Frame Job ▸ Settings… ▸ Transcription." Saving a key turns the command on at once. See [AI features and your own keys](/getting-started/ai-and-your-keys/).
199	
200	If nothing in the project plays sound from a file, the item is greyed with its plain title, key or no key.
201	
202	### Use a transcript you already have
203	
204	If a file the command would read already has a filler transcript, the command stays on and cuts that file's fillers with no key, because that transcript is already paid for. The transcript only counts if the file hasn't changed since it was made.
205	
206	Any other files stay on the list, with **Transcribe** disabled.
207	
208	Your selection matters here too. If you've selected a clip of a file with no filler transcript, the greyed item doesn't mean the project has none. Deselect the clip so the command reads every clip.
209	
210	## Captions stay clean
211	
212	Filler words never reach captions made from an AssemblyAI transcript. **File ▸ Generate Captions…** removes them first, and the sheet's preview leaves them out too, so a transcript made with filler words produces the same captions as one made without them.
213	
214	The words it removes are um, uh, hmm, mhm, uh-huh, ah, huh, hm, m, er and erm, with capitals and punctuation ignored. Any word on that list goes, even one said on purpose, such as a surprised "Huh?".
215	
216	The saved transcript keeps every word as it was heard. Only captions filter them, which is how Remove Filler Words can still find them.
217	
218	Captions made on this Mac aren't filtered. They hold what the Mac's recogniser wrote.
219	
220	### The transcript also serves captions
221	
222	A transcript made for Remove Filler Words also serves Generate Captions, so that file isn't uploaded or billed again. This holds as long as you ask for the same language, speaker labels and vocabulary it was transcribed with. Change one and the file goes up again. See [Transcribe with AssemblyAI](/captions/assemblyai-transcription/).
223	
224	## Good to know
225	
226	- You can transcribe a project you haven't saved yet. Its transcript is kept with the project when you save.
227	- AssemblyAI takes up to 10 hours in one file. Frame Job says so in the note before it uploads anything.
228	- If AssemblyAI hasn't confirmed deleting an earlier transcript of a file, the row reads "Nothing to upload · 1 file waiting on an earlier delete". **Transcribe** tries that delete again first. If it goes through, the file uploads as normal. If it doesn't, nothing is uploaded and the note says why.
229	- If AssemblyAI rejects your key, the note reads "AssemblyAI refused the API key — check it in Frame Job ▸ Settings".
230	
231	## With an agent
232	
233	`transcribe_for_fillers` is the **Transcribe** button for an agent connected over MCP, and it's the same paid upload of one file, keeping the file's earlier choices. It writes only the transcript, with no captions and no undo step. `detect_fillers` lists the files that need it under `needs_transcript`, and needs no key to do that.
234	
235	The agent gets `ready: true` once `detect_fillers` can read the file. The tool stops with a message if no clip on the timeline plays the file, or if it would upload and no key is set.
236	
237	It differs from the button in two ways. A file that already has a filler transcript uploads nothing and needs no key, and an agent's run has no **Stop**.
238	
239	The built-in [Assistant](/cleanup/false-starts/#the-assistant-wont-start-a-paid-transcription) can't use this tool. See [Tools: clean-up](/mcp/tools-clean-up/) for its arguments.
240	
241	## Related

244	- [Your AssemblyAI key](/captions/assemblyai-key/)
245	- [What goes to AssemblyAI](/captions/assemblyai-privacy/)
246	- [Transcribe with AssemblyAI](/captions/assemblyai-transcription/)

249	=== how-cleanup-cuts-work.mdx
250	---
251	title: "How a clean-up cut works"
252	description: "What Remove Silences and Remove Filler Words share: the preview, the single undo step, how far a cut reaches, and what it won't touch."
253	---
254	
255	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
256	
257	Frame Job's two clean-up commands cut the same way. Each shows you what it would take out, makes the whole cut as one edit, closes the timeline over it, and stays out of nests and transitions. This page covers what they share.
258	
259	<AtAGlance
260	  menu={['Clip ▸ Remove Silences…', 'Clip ▸ Remove Filler Words…']}
261	  tools={['detect_silence', 'detect_fillers', 'ripple_delete_ranges']}
262	/>
263	
264	## Two commands for a spoken recording
265	
266	Both commands are for a screencast, a tutorial or a talking-head take.
267	
268	- [Remove Silences](/cleanup/remove-silences/) cuts the dead air.
269	- [Remove Filler Words](/cleanup/remove-filler-words/) cuts the ums and uhs, using the timing of each word in a transcript.
270	
271	They're in the **Clip** menu, below **Close Gap** and **Retime Range…**, with **Remove Silences…** first. Neither has a keyboard shortcut.
272	
273	Remove Silences measures the mix as you hear it, so [volume](/audio/volume/), [fades](/audio/fades/), [ducking](/audio/ducking/), [mute and solo](/audio/mute-and-solo/) all change what it finds. See [What counts as silent](/cleanup/voice-or-level/).
274	
275	An agent can use both, and can also read a clip's transcript to [cut false starts](/cleanup/false-starts/).
276	
277	## See the cut before you make it
278	
279	Nothing changes until you choose **Remove**. While a sheet is open, it and the timeline show you exactly what would go.
280	
281	### Preview shading on the timeline
282	
283	Every span the command would remove is shaded on the timeline ruler and lanes.
284	
285	The shading is coral, about twice as strong as the wash of the [in/out range](/timeline/in-out-range/), so you can tell the two apart where they overlap. In the lanes it sits under the clips. On the ruler it sits under the ticks and marker flags, which stay readable.
286	
287	The shading goes away when the sheet closes, however it closes: **Remove**, **Cancel**, <kbd>Esc</kbd> or the window closing.
288	
289	### The cut count
290	
291	The sheet reads how many cuts it would make and how much time they remove, for example "23 cuts · removes 00:00:04:12". A single cut reads "1 cut". With nothing to cut it reads "No cuts", and **Remove** is dimmed.
292	
293	**Remove** makes exactly the cuts the count describes.
294	
295	### The rest of the editor waits
296	
297	Playback pauses when a sheet opens, because a moving playhead would repaint over the shading. Other editing commands in that window are off until you close the sheet.
298	
299	## One undo step
300	
301	**Remove** cuts every span and closes the timeline over each one as a single undo step, however many spans there are. One <kbd>⌘Z</kbd> restores everything. The step is named **Undo Remove Silences** or **Undo Remove Filler Words**.
302	
303	Spans that touch or overlap become one cut.
304	
305	[Deleting selected words](/captions/delete-words/) in the Transcript tab with <kbd>⌫</kbd> makes the same kind of cut, as its own step named Delete Words.
306	
307	## A ripple across every unlocked track
308	
309	A clean-up cut is a [ripple delete](/editing/delete-clips/#how-a-ripple-closes-holes) across every unlocked track, not only the clips that were analysed. The picture above a voice-over is cut with it, so the two stay in step.
310	
311	- **Working on selected clips doesn't limit the cut.** It changes what's listened to or read. The cut still reaches every unlocked track.
312	- **Locked tracks are neither cut nor moved.** Everything else closes up, so a [locked track](/timeline/hide-and-lock-tracks/) falls out of step with the rest.
313	- **Linked clips move together.** If a clip that moves has a linked partner, the partner moves too. When that would take a clip before the start of the timeline, Frame Job makes no cut at all. It beeps, and the foot of the inspector names both clips.
314	
315	### Markers keep their place
316	
317	[Markers](/timeline/markers/) stay at their times when the timeline closes, as they do under every ripple delete. The footnote of both sheets says so: "markers keep their place". A marker after a cut therefore sits over later material than it did, so check any you placed on a particular moment.
318	
319	## Frame-accurate edges
320	
321	Each cut's start rounds up to the next frame and its end rounds down. Both edges move inward, so each edge of a cut can leave up to a frame of room tone, or of a filler, behind. Rounding outward would clip the start of the next word, so a cut never does.
322	
323	## Nests are protected
324	
325	A clean-up cut never reaches into a nest clip. A [nest](/editing/nests/) always plays from its first frame, so cutting into one would strand the rest of it. The whole nest can still slide left with everything else when the timeline closes up.
326	
327	In Remove Silences a nest's sound still counts when **In:** is **All audible clips**. A loud nest keeps a moment from being quiet, even though no cut may touch the nest.
328	
329	To clean up the audio inside a nest, do one of these:
330	
331	- Open it with **Clip ▸ Open Nest** (<kbd>⌘↓</kbd>) and run the command there. With a nest open, both commands work on the nest's own timeline, and a nest inside that nest is still protected. See [Work inside a nest](/editing/inside-a-nest/).
332	- Un-nest it with **Clip ▸ Un-nest** (<kbd>⇧⌘G</kbd>).
333	
334	Each sheet tells you when a nest got in the way. [Remove Silences](/cleanup/remove-silences/#what-the-sheet-tells-you) adds a note telling you to open it, and Remove Filler Words counts the filler as left in.
335	
336	A nest on a locked track needs no protection, because the cut neither splits nor moves it.
337	
338	## Transitions are protected
339	
340	A clean-up cut never reaches into a [transition](/motion/transitions/)'s overlap or the area around it, so quiet or fillers there stay. The protected area is the overlap widened by its own length on each side: a 1 s overlap protects 3 s.
341	
342	This holds on every unlocked track, whichever clips you chose to work on, and for [any two clips that overlap](/motion/transitions/#an-overlap-with-no-stored-transition) on a track.
343	
344	Remove Silences says nothing about a transition it stayed out of. Remove Filler Words leaves the filler in whole and counts it as left in.
345	
346	## Good to know
347	
348	- Remove Silences measures a reversed clip as it plays. In **Voice** mode a cut edge in one can be off by up to 32 ms, because speech is measured in 32 ms steps along the file as it runs forwards.
349	- Remove Filler Words doesn't read reversed clips at all.
350	- Remove Silences still listens to locked tracks, so sound on one can keep a moment from being quiet. Remove Filler Words doesn't read clips on locked tracks, and its sheet says how many there are.
351	
352	## Make the cut from an agent
353	
354	`detect_silence` and `detect_fillers` report the ranges a sheet would cut, and change nothing. Passing them to `ripple_delete_ranges` makes the same cut as **Remove**, under the same rules. It takes a list of `[from, to]` pairs in ticks, at least one, and a pair written backwards is the same range.
355	
356	There's one difference you'll see. Any cut an agent makes this way, whether silences, fillers or [false starts](/cleanup/false-starts/), is one undo step named **Undo Ripple Delete**, not the sheet's name.
357	
358	To reach inside a nest, an agent opens it with `set_scope` first, and the ranges are then in the nest's own time. See [Tools: clean-up](/mcp/tools-clean-up/) and [Editing inside a nest](/mcp/nests/).
359
