368	=== remove-filler-words.mdx
369	---
370	title: "Remove Filler Words"
371	description: "Find the ums and uhs in your speech, see what would go, and cut them all as one edit."
372	---
373	
374	import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
375	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
376	
377	Remove Filler Words finds the ums and uhs in your speech, shows you what it would cut, and cuts them at the words' own timings, all as one undo step. There's nothing to tune.
378	
379	<AtAGlance
380	  menu="Clip ▸ Remove Filler Words…"
381	  tools={['detect_fillers', 'transcribe_for_fillers', 'ripple_delete_ranges', 'get_transcript', 'get_timeline_transcript']}
382	  needs="An AssemblyAI key, unless a file it would read already has a transcript made with filler words."
383	/>
384	
385	## Remove the filler words
386	
387	<Steps>
388	
389	1. If you only want some clips read, select them. See [Which clips are read](#which-clips-are-read).
390	
391	2. Choose **Clip ▸ Remove Filler Words…**. It's after **Remove Silences…** and has no keyboard shortcut.
392	
393	3. If the sheet lists files with no filler transcript yet, press **Transcribe** beside each one you want read. This uploads the file's audio to AssemblyAI and costs money, so the sheet shows the estimate first. See [Transcripts for filler words](/cleanup/filler-transcripts/).
394	
395	4. Check what's shaded on the timeline, and read the count in the sheet, such as "3 cuts · removes 00:00:01:12".
396	
397	5. Choose **Remove**, or **Cancel** to leave the timeline as it was. Closing the sheet also stops a transcription that's still running.
398	
399	</Steps>
400	
401	**Remove** is off while the sheet reads "No cuts" and while a transcription is running. One <kbd>⌘Z</kbd> puts everything back, because the whole cut is a single **Remove Filler Words** undo step.
402	
403	The command is available when the timeline has a clip that plays sound from a media file, forwards, with its sound on, and you've either set an AssemblyAI key or a file it would read already has a transcript made with filler words. With neither, it's greyed and reads **Remove Filler Words… (needs your AssemblyAI key)**. See [Your AssemblyAI key](/captions/assemblyai-key/).
404	
405	## Which words are fillers
406	
407	A word counts as a filler when it's on this fixed list, ignoring capitals and any punctuation at its ends:
408	
409	um · uh · hmm · mhm · uh-huh · ah · huh · hm · m · er · erm
410	
411	"Uh huh" written as two words matches as two fillers, and "uh-huh" matches as one.
412	
413	:::caution
414	The list can't be changed, and the sheet can't keep a single filler. A real "ah" or "er", or the letter "M" said aloud, is treated as a filler too, so check the shading before you choose **Remove**.
415	:::
416	
417	## Which clips are read
418	
419	Remove Filler Words reads the selected clips when the selection includes speech from a media file, and the sheet then says "Only the selected clips are read." Otherwise it reads every clip. The sheet has no menu for this, so make the selection first.
420	
421	Some clips can't be read:
422	
423	| Clip | What happens |
424	| --- | --- |
425	| It's on a locked track | Its fillers aren't read, because the cut can neither cut nor move it. The sheet counts them: "1 clip is on a locked track, which the cut neither cuts nor moves, so its fillers were not read." |
426	| It plays in reverse, its sound is switched off, its file is missing, or its file has no audio track | It has no words to read, and it's passed over without a note. |
427	| It's a [nest](/editing/nests/) | The words inside a nest aren't read from outside it. Open the nest with <kbd>⌘↓</kbd> and run the command there, where it works on the nest's own timeline. |
428	
429	When none of those clips has words to read, the sheet says "Nothing in scope plays speech from a media file, so nothing was read."
430	
431	## What gets cut
432	
433	Each run of consecutive fillers becomes one cut. A run ends at the next real word, so two fillers with a pause between them and no word go together, pause included. The pauses before and after a run stay. [Remove Silences](/cleanup/remove-silences/) takes those out.
434	
435	The cut is placed to take the whole filler and nothing else:
436	
437	- It widens outward to the speech grid, the 32 ms steps Frame Job measures speech in, so all of the filler goes. It never reaches into the words on either side.
438	- Its edges then snap inward to whole frames, as Remove Silences' do. Up to a frame of the filler can remain at each end.
439	
440	Cuts that touch or overlap join into one, and the count in the sheet is of the joined cuts.
441	
442	After that it's a normal clean-up cut. It runs across every unlocked track, closes the timeline over each cut, and markers keep their place. See [How a clean-up cut works](/cleanup/how-cleanup-cuts-work/).
443	
444	## Fillers left in whole
445	
446	A filler is never trimmed. Frame Job leaves the whole run in when:
447	
448	- It's too short to cut. A tiny filler can end up with nothing left once it's on both grids.
449	- Cutting it would reach a word spoken in another clip on any unlocked track, whether or not that clip is being read. The cut runs across every unlocked track, so it would take that word with it.
450	- Cutting it would reach a nest clip on an unlocked track.
451	- Cutting it would reach a transition on an unlocked track, or the area around one.
452	
453	The sheet counts these, one for each run: "2 fillers are left in: too short to cut, or cutting would reach another clip's word, a nest or a transition."
454	
455	## Good to know
456	
457	- **Protection needs a transcript.** A cut is kept away from speech in another clip only when that clip's file has a saved AssemblyAI transcript, made with or without filler words. Speech on another unlocked track with no such transcript isn't protected, so check the shading there.
458	- **The service can miss a filler.** A filler AssemblyAI doesn't return isn't cut. One it returns that isn't on the list stays in, both in the cut and in your captions.
459	- **A filler belongs to the clip it starts in.** It's read when it starts inside the part of the file the clip plays.
460	
461	## With an agent
462	
463	`detect_fillers` reads the same ranges the sheet would cut and changes nothing. Pass them to `ripple_delete_ranges` to make the cut. Any cut made this way is one undo step called **Ripple Delete**, not **Remove Filler Words**.
464	
465	- An agent can name the clips to read. Left to itself, it follows the same selection rule as the sheet.
466	- `detect_fillers` only reads transcripts that are already saved, so it needs no key and never uses the network. It names the files that have none.
467	- `transcribe_for_fillers` makes a transcript for one of those files. It's a paid upload, and the built-in assistant can't use it, so press **Transcribe** in the sheet yourself.
468	- Where the sheet counts, an agent gets detail: every run that's left in with its own reason, every clip on a locked track, and every named clip it couldn't read.
469	- `get_transcript` and `get_timeline_transcript` mark each word that's on the [filler list](#which-words-are-fillers).
470	
471	See [Tools: clean-up](/mcp/tools-clean-up/).
472	
473	## Related
474	
475	- [Transcripts for filler words](/cleanup/filler-transcripts/)
476	- [Your AssemblyAI key](/captions/assemblyai-key/)
477	- [How a clean-up cut works](/cleanup/how-cleanup-cuts-work/)
478	- [Remove Silences](/cleanup/remove-silences/)
479	- [Cut false starts](/cleanup/false-starts/)
480	- [Cut by deleting words](/captions/delete-words/)
481	=== remove-silences.mdx
482	---
483	title: Remove Silences
484	description: Find the dead air in a spoken recording, see it on the timeline, and cut it all as one edit.
485	---
486	
487	import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
488	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
489	import Shot from '@components/Shot.astro';
490	
491	Remove Silences finds the dead air in a spoken recording, shows you what it would cut, and takes it all out as one undo step, closing the timeline over each cut. Use it on a screencast, a tutorial or a talking-head take.
492	
493	<AtAGlance
494	  menu="Clip ▸ Remove Silences…"
495	  tools={['detect_silence', 'ripple_delete_ranges']}
496	  needs="Nothing. Voice detection runs on your Mac, with no key and no upload."
497	/>
498	
499	## Remove the silences
500	
501	<Steps>
502	
503	1. To measure only some clips, select them first. The sheet then opens on **Selected clips**.
504	
505	2. Choose **Clip ▸ Remove Silences…**. It's available when the timeline has a clip with its sound on. If there turns out to be nothing to measure, Frame Job beeps instead of opening the sheet.
506	
507	3. Check what's shaded on the timeline, and read the count in the sheet, for example "23 cuts · removes 00:00:04:12". Both update as you change a control. With nothing to cut the count reads "No cuts" and **Remove** is dimmed.
508	
509	4. Adjust the [controls](#the-controls) until the cuts look right.
510	
511	5. Choose **Remove**. Everything shaded is cut and the timeline closes up. <kbd>⌘Z</kbd> puts it all back. Choose **Cancel** to leave the timeline as it was.
512	
513	</Steps>
514	
515	<Shot
516	  name="14-remove-silences-sheet.sheet"
517	  alt="The Remove Silences sheet, with Judge by set to Voice, a Level if no voice slider at −40 dBFS, Longer than 0.5 seconds, Keep at ends 0.1 seconds, and In set to All audible clips."
518	/>
519	
520	The sheet opens on its defaults every time. It doesn't remember your last settings.
521	
522	## The controls
523	
524	| Control | What it does | Default | Range |
525	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
526	| **Judge by:** | How a moment is tested. See [What counts as silent](/cleanup/voice-or-level/). | Voice, or Level if the voice model can't be used | Voice, Level |
527	| **Quieter than:** or **Level if no voice:** | The level that counts as quiet. The row reads **Quieter than:** in Level mode and **Level if no voice:** in Voice mode. | −40 dBFS | −80 to −10 dBFS |
528	| **Longer than:** | The shortest quiet stretch worth cutting. Shorter pauses, such as the gap between two words, stay. | 0.5 s | 0.05 to 10 s |
529	| **Keep at ends:** | How much of each quiet stretch to keep at each end, so speech doesn't start or stop abruptly. | 0.1 s | 0 to 2 s |
530	| **In:** | Whether to look at **Selected clips** or **All audible clips**. | Selected clips when the selection has something audible, otherwise All audible clips | |
531	
532	The level row is a slider in whole decibels, with its value beside it. In Level mode, sound at or below it is quiet. In Voice mode, it judges clips that hold no voice, and a clip the mix turns down to it or lower is quiet whatever it contains.
533	
534	**Selected clips** is greyed out when nothing selected makes a sound, and a selection of muted clips counts as nothing audible, as does a selected nest. Choose it to stop a music bed under a voice-over from holding the cuts up.
535	
536	**Longer than:** measures the stretch as you hear it, before **Keep at ends:** takes its share. A stretch no longer than twice **Keep at ends:** isn't cut. Cuts then [round to whole frames](/cleanup/how-cleanup-cuts-work/#frame-accurate-edges), so up to a frame more of room tone can remain at each end. Raise **Keep at ends:** if a word gets clipped.
537	
538	The two number fields take up to two decimal places. A number outside the range stays in the field and **Remove** beeps until you fix it. The count and the shading follow the slider as it moves, and a number field when you leave it.
539	
540	## What the sheet tells you
541	
542	The sheet explains itself under the count. It can show more than one of these at once.
543	
544	| The sheet says | What it means |
545	| --- | --- |
546	| "Nothing in this timeline is audible, so nothing was analysed." | Nothing the sheet is measuring makes a sound. With **Selected clips** it reads "Nothing the selected clips play is audible in the mix, so nothing was analysed." |
547	| "The waveform is still being analysed for …" or "Speech is still being analysed for …" | Frame Job hasn't finished with the files it names, which often happens straight after an import. Leave the sheet open and it updates as each one finishes. |
548	| "Nothing inside is proposed for removal yet." | Follows the line above: nothing in those files can be cut until their analysis is ready. |
549	| "Anything inside it that holds no voice is left alone until it lands…" | Follows the waveform line in Voice mode: speech can already be judged, but a clip with no voice has to wait for the waveform. It may add that the mix already turns a clip down far enough to be quiet. |
550	| "What is proposed inside … is quiet in the MIX…" | The named clips are still waiting for analysis, but they've been turned down, faded or ducked far enough to be quiet, so those cuts stand whatever the analysis finds. |
551	| "Quiet inside a nest is left alone…" | A quiet stretch at least as long as **Longer than:** ran across a nest. There may be dead air inside it, so a low count doesn't mean there's none. Open the nest with <kbd>⌘↓</kbd> and remove its silences there. With several nests it reads "Quiet inside 2 nests…". |
552	
553	Relinking a file starts its analysis again. If an agent relinks one while the sheet is open, the sheet clears the old results at once and updates when the new ones are ready.
554	
555	## Good to know
556	
557	- A gap with nothing audible in it is left alone, and so is a stretch where only a muted clip plays. Remove Silences takes dead air out of a recording, not the gaps you placed between clips. [Close Gap](/editing/close-gaps/) does that.
558	- With **Selected clips**, a moment none of those clips covers is never cut.
559	- The cut reaches every unlocked track, not only the clips you measured, and markers stay where they are. See [A ripple across every unlocked track](/cleanup/how-cleanup-cuts-work/#a-ripple-across-every-unlocked-track).
560	- Nothing inside a [nest](/editing/nests/) is cut, because a nest plays from its first frame and a cut into one would strand the rest of it. [Transitions are protected](/cleanup/how-cleanup-cuts-work/#transitions-are-protected) too.
561	- A quiet stretch broken up by a nest or a transition is measured in its pieces.
562	
563	## With an agent
564	
565	`detect_silence` reads the same ranges the sheet would cut and changes nothing. Pass them to `ripple_delete_ranges` to make the cut. See [Tools: clean-up](/mcp/tools-clean-up/).
566	
567	An agent isn't held to the limits of the sheet's controls, and it can also set how sure the voice model must be, which the sheet doesn't offer. To look inside a nest, it opens the nest with `set_scope` and reads again.
568	
569	## Related
570	
571	- [What counts as silent](/cleanup/voice-or-level/)
572	- [How a clean-up cut works](/cleanup/how-cleanup-cuts-work/)
573	- [Remove Filler Words](/cleanup/remove-filler-words/)
574	- [Close gaps and insert time](/editing/close-gaps/)

576	=== voice-or-level.mdx
577	---
578	title: "What counts as silent"
579	description: "How Remove Silences decides a moment is quiet: Voice or Level, what the mix changes, and why a stretch isn't offered for cutting."
580	---
581	
582	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
583	
584	Remove Silences cuts a stretch only when it's quiet as you hear it, in the mix, and only where every clip it's measuring is quiet at once. The **In:** menu sets which clips those are. **Judge by:** in the sheet picks how each moment is tested.
585	
586	<AtAGlance
587	  menu="Clip ▸ Remove Silences…"
588	  where="Judge by: in the Remove Silences sheet"
589	  tools="detect_silence"
590	  needs="Nothing. Voice detection runs on your Mac, with no key and no upload."
591	/>
592	
593	## Judge by Voice or Level
594	
595	| **Judge by:** | A moment is quiet when |
596	| --- | --- |
597	| **Voice** | Nobody is talking. |
598	| **Level** | The sound in the mix is at or below the threshold. |
599	
600	The sheet opens on **Voice** every time, unless [the voice model can't be used](#when-the-voice-model-cant-be-used).
601	
602	Voice listens for speech, not for loudness. A low recording level doesn't make speech quiet, and in a clip that holds a voice, a loud sound that isn't speech, such as a hum, still counts as quiet. If a recording has sounds you want to keep, such as the audio of a demo, choose **Level**.
603	
604	## Voice mode
605	
606	A voice-activity model that comes with Frame Job (Silero VAD) scores every 32 ms of a file for how likely it is to be speech. A moment counts as speech when its score reaches the voice confidence, a value from 0 to 1 that the sheet always holds at 0.5.
607	
608	You don't start the analysis. It runs by itself after you import a file or open a project, listens to each file once and keeps the answer with the project. It runs on your Mac, and nothing is uploaded.
609	
610	In Voice mode the threshold row reads **Level if no voice:**, and it does two jobs:
611	
612	- It's the level for [clips with no voice in them](#clips-with-no-voice-are-judged-by-level).
613	- A clip the mix turns down to that level or lower is quiet whatever it holds. At the default −40 dBFS, that's a clip turned down by 40 dB or more.
614	
615	The same voice analysis also serves [Duck by Speech](/audio/duck-by-speech/), [Enhance Voice](/audio/enhance-voice/), [Synchronize Audio](/audio/synchronize-audio/), [Speed Up Typing](/recording/speed-up-typing/), [Switch by Speaker](/multicam/switch-by-speaker/) and the [transcript's word timing](/captions/transcript-words/).
616	
617	## Clips with no voice are judged by level
618	
619	In Voice mode, a clip with no voice in it at all, such as music or a tone, would read as quiet from start to end. So Frame Job judges that clip by level instead, against **Level if no voice:**, and the sheet names it:
620	
621	- One clip: "Intro music at 00:00:12:00 holds no voice and is judged by level."
622	- Several: "3 clips hold no voice and are judged by level: …", followed by each clip's name and time.
623	
624	The test covers only the part of the file the clip plays. That's why the sheet names clips and not files: two clips of one file can be judged differently.
625	
626	## Level mode
627	
628	In Level mode a moment is quiet when the sound in the mix is at or below **Quieter than:**. That's the file's waveform with the [mix](#silence-is-measured-in-the-mix) applied, measured in 10 ms steps. When a step holds more than one reading, as it does in a clip playing at ×2, the louder reading counts, so a step is quiet only if all of it is.
629	
630	**Quieter than:** runs from −80 to −10 dBFS and starts at −40 dBFS. See [The controls](/cleanup/remove-silences/#the-controls).
631	
632	## Silence is measured in the mix
633	
634	Remove Silences measures what you hear, not the raw file. The mix is the file's sound after everything that changes its volume in the project. These all count:
635	
636	- The clip's volume, its fades and any volume change in an action
637	- Ducking from another clip
638	- Muting a clip or a track, and soloing another track
639	- The track's volume
640	
641	In Level mode, a clip you've turned down reads quieter by exactly as much. In Voice mode, turning a clip down makes it quiet only once it reaches the level in **Level if no voice:**. Above that, speech is still speech.
642	
643	Effects on the clip don't count. Remove Silences hears the file without its [voice effect](/audio/voice-effects/) or [Voice Isolation](/audio/voice-isolation/).
644	
645	## Every clip being measured has to be quiet
646	
647	A stretch is silent only where every clip being measured is quiet. A music bed under a voice-over therefore keeps the pauses in the speech from being cut, because the music is still playing through them.
648	
649	To cut those pauses, select the voice clip and set **In:** to **Selected clips**, so only the voice is measured.
650	
651	:::caution
652	**In:** changes what's measured, not what's cut. The cut still runs across every unlocked track, so the music is cut at the same places. [Lock its track](/timeline/hide-and-lock-tracks/#lock-track) to leave the music where it is. See [How a clean-up cut works](/cleanup/how-cleanup-cuts-work/).
653	:::
654	
655	## Muted clips are left out
656	
657	A clip the mix silences all the way through is left out of the analysis entirely. That covers a muted clip, a clip silenced by a solo, and a clip turned down or faded to nothing. This holds whichever **In:** choice you make, even for a selected clip.
658	
659	So a muted music bed is never read as one long silence covering the whole song. It doesn't hold a cut up either. Where it's the only thing playing, there's nothing to measure, and the stretch is left alone like a gap.
660	
661	## While a file is still being analysed
662	
663	Nothing inside a file is offered for cutting until its analysis is ready, so a clip can't be cut as silence only because its waveform hasn't arrived yet. This often shows straight after an import.
664	
665	| Mode | What it waits for | The sheet says |
666	| --- | --- | --- |
667	| Level | The waveform | "The waveform is still being analysed for …" |
668	| Voice | The voice analysis | "Speech is still being analysed for …" |
669	| Voice, for a clip with no voice | The voice analysis, then the waveform | "The waveform is still being analysed for …. Anything inside it that holds no voice is left alone until it lands." |
670	
671	There's one exception in every mode. A part the mix has already turned down far enough to be quiet can still be cut, because no analysis can change that answer, and the sheet names the clip.
672	
673	You can leave the sheet open. It updates as each file finishes.
674	
675	If a file's sound can't be read to its end, Frame Job doesn't keep the analysis, and it tries again the next time you open the project. Until then, nothing inside that file is offered for cutting.
676	
677	## When the voice model can't be used
678	
679	If the voice model can't be used on this Mac, the sheet opens in **Level** mode with **Voice** greyed out, and it says "The voice model could not be used, so quiet is judged by level." This lasts until you relaunch Frame Job.
680	
681	## Limits of Voice mode
682	
683	- A soft word that scores under the voice confidence reads as quiet. Raise **Keep at ends:** if a word gets clipped.
684	- A clip that holds any voice is judged by voice for its whole length. So a long music clip with a little speech in it isn't judged by level, and the music around that speech reads as quiet. Use **In:** **Selected clips** to keep it out of the measurement.
685	- The model hears each file mixed down to mono, whatever the clip's pan or channel settings. A voice on only one side of a stereo file reaches it quieter.
686	
687	## With an agent
688	
689	`detect_silence` takes the same choices as the sheet, and one the sheet doesn't have: the voice confidence, which is how sure the model must be for a moment to count as speech. It runs from 0.1 to 0.9, with a default of 0.5, and it also decides which clips count as holding no voice. It works in Voice mode only, and asking for it in Level mode or outside that range gets an error that says why. The answer lists the clips judged by level, and the files they play.
690	
691	While the voice model can't be used, an agent that asks for Voice by name gets an error telling it to use Level. One that doesn't name a mode gets Level, with the same note the sheet shows. See [Tools: clean-up](/mcp/tools-clean-up/).
692	
693	## Related
694

2	---
3	title: "Your AssemblyAI key"
4	description: Save, check and remove the AssemblyAI key that turns on cloud captions and Remove Filler Words, choose your region, and see where the key is kept.
5	---
6	
7	import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
8	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
9	import Shot from '@components/Shot.astro';
10	
11	Your AssemblyAI key turns on cloud transcription, and AssemblyAI bills your account directly. It lives in Settings, so it's the same for every project, and you can set it with no project open. For how keys work across Frame Job, see [AI features and your own keys](/getting-started/ai-and-your-keys/).
12	
13	<AtAGlance
14	  menu="Frame Job ▸ Settings…"
15	  keys="⌘,"
16	  where="Settings ▸ Transcription"
17	  needs="An AssemblyAI account."
18	/>
19	
20	<Shot
21	  name="02-settings.window"
22	  alt="The Settings window. Under the Transcription heading, with its info button, are an AssemblyAI API key field reading Paste your key, a Region pop-up set to United States, the line No API key is set, and the buttons Save, Remove, Verify and Account Page. Remove and Verify are greyed."
23	/>
24	
25	## Save your AssemblyAI key
26	
27	<Steps>
28	
29	1. Choose **Frame Job ▸ Settings…** (<kbd>⌘,</kbd>) and find **Transcription**.
30	
31	2. Choose **Account Page** to get a key from your AssemblyAI dashboard.
32	
33	3. Paste the key into **AssemblyAI API key:**.
34	
35	4. Choose **Save**, or press <kbd>Return</kbd>.
36	
37	5. Choose [**Verify**](#check-the-key) to check that it works.
38	
39	</Steps>
40	
41	The line under **Region:** says "Key saved.", and the field empties. From then on the field shows a fixed row of dots, the same length whatever your key is. The key itself never goes back in the field, so it can't be read or copied out of the window.
42	
43	With no key anywhere, the line reads "No API key is set." in ordinary grey. That isn't an error. **Save** with an empty field beeps and does nothing.
44	
45	If the key file can't be written, the line reads "The API key could not be saved:" and gives the reason. The field is emptied anyway, so paste the key again once it's fixed.
46	
47	## Check the key
48	
49	**Verify** makes AssemblyAI's cheapest signed-in request, with your key and region, to see if the key works. It doesn't transcribe or bill anything.
50	
51	It checks the key typed in the field, even if you haven't saved it, then the saved key, then [the environment's](#use-a-key-from-the-environment). A typed key is only checked, so choose **Save** as well to keep it. A run never uses a key that's only typed.
52	
53	| The line says | What it means |
54	| --- | --- |
55	| "Checking…" | The request is on its way. |
56	| "Key accepted" | AssemblyAI accepted the key in this region. |
57	| "No API key is set." | There was no key to check. |
58	| "Settings changed since this check began. Verify again." | You changed the key or the region during the check, so its answer no longer applies. |
59	| AssemblyAI's message, such as "AssemblyAI refused the API key — check it in Frame Job ▸ Settings" | The check failed, and the message says why. "No network connection" is another. |
60	
61	**Verify** is greyed when there's no key at all, and while a check of the same key and region is running.
62	
63	## Choose a region
64	
65	**Region:** chooses the AssemblyAI data centre your audio goes to: **United States**, the default, or **European Union**. It's saved as soon as you pick it, and an open sheet updates straight away. The Generate Captions and Remove Filler Words sheets name the region before you upload.
66	
67	A transcript made in one region can't be seen from the other, so pick the region your account uses. [A pending delete](/captions/assemblyai-privacy/#unconfirmed-deletes-are-retried) only succeeds in the region it was made in.
68	
69	Changing the region doesn't upload anything again. Transcripts already kept in a project stay usable.
70	
71	## Open your AssemblyAI account
72	
73	**Account Page** opens your AssemblyAI dashboard in your browser, at `https://www.assemblyai.com/dashboard`. That's where you get a key and see what you've spent.
74	
75	## Remove the key
76	
77	**Remove** deletes the saved key and says "Key removed." It's greyed unless a key is saved.
78	
79	If the removal fails, the key stays saved and the line says why.
80	
81	## Where the key is kept
82	
83	The key is saved in a file only your account can read, not in the Keychain:
84	
85	`~/Library/Application Support/Frame Job/assemblyai-key`
86	
87	The file's mode is `0600`, and it sits beside `anthropic-key`, the [Assistant](/assistant/set-up/)'s key. Any program running as you can read it, so treat that file like a password. The key is never passed on the command line.
88	
89	## Use a key from the environment
90	
91	If no key is saved, Frame Job also accepts one from the `RC_ASSEMBLYAI_KEY` environment variable, which is useful when you launch it from a terminal.
92	
93	- A saved key always wins over the variable.
94	- An empty variable counts as no key.
95	- **Verify** checks the variable's key when nothing is typed or saved.
96	- **Remove** stays greyed, because nothing is saved.
97	
98	See [Where Frame Job keeps its files](/reference/file-locations/).
99	
100	## What the key turns on
101	
102	| Feature | Without a key |
103	| --- | --- |
104	| The **AssemblyAI** engine of [Generate Captions](/captions/assemblyai-transcription/) | **Generate** is greyed, [unless every file is already transcribed](/captions/assemblyai-transcription/#generate-with-no-key). |
105	| [Remove Filler Words](/cleanup/remove-filler-words/), which finds fillers only through AssemblyAI | The menu item is greyed and reads **Remove Filler Words… (needs your AssemblyAI key)**, unless a file under the selected clips, or with no clip selected any file on the timeline, already has a transcript with filler words. See [Transcripts for filler words](/cleanup/filler-transcripts/) for what works without one. |
106	
107	Captions made [on this Mac](/captions/on-device-transcription/) need no key.
108	
109	Saving or removing a key, or changing the region, reaches an open Generate Captions sheet straight away, so **Generate** can come on without reopening it.
110	
111	## What the info button says
112	
113	The ⓘ beside the **Transcription** heading explains three things:
114	
115	- **What leaves your Mac.** The audio of the files you're captioning is uploaded, transcribed, read back and then deleted from AssemblyAI. A delete that didn't land is retried at the start of the next run. Nothing is uploaded until you press **Generate**, and captions made on this Mac never leave it.
116	- **The rate.** AssemblyAI's published rate as Frame Job last read it: $0.21 an hour of audio, and $0.02 more with **Speakers:** on, read on 2026-09-17.
117	- **The key.** It's kept in a file only you can read and is never shown again once it's saved.
118	
119	[What goes to AssemblyAI](/captions/assemblyai-privacy/) has the full story.
120	
121	## Only a person sets the key
122	
123	No agent tool can read or change the key or the region, and an agent can't pass a key of its own. Only you set them, here. An agent's `transcribe` call uses your saved key, or the environment's. With neither, it stops with the same "No AssemblyAI API key is set." sentence, unless every file is already transcribed.
124

131	=== assemblyai-privacy
132	---
133	title: "What goes to AssemblyAI"
134	description: What leaves your Mac when you transcribe with AssemblyAI, what you're billed for, how the transcript is deleted afterwards, and what happens when a delete doesn't land.
135	---
136	
137	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
138	
139	When you transcribe with AssemblyAI, the sound of your files leaves your Mac, and only after you press **Generate**. Frame Job then asks AssemblyAI to delete its transcript as soon as it has the words. Captions made [on this Mac](/captions/on-device-transcription/) never leave it.
140	
141	<AtAGlance
142	  menu={['File ▸ Generate Captions…', 'Clip ▸ Remove Filler Words…']}
143	  where="Frame Job ▸ Settings… ▸ Transcription ▸ ⓘ"
144	  tools="transcribe"
145	  needs="Your own AssemblyAI key."
146	/>
147	
148	## What is uploaded and billed
149	
150	| Goes to AssemblyAI | Stays on your Mac |
151	| --- | --- |
152	| The whole audio of each media file behind the chosen clips | The video |
153	| Your **Vocabulary:** terms, and the language and **Speakers:** settings | The project and the rest of its media |
154	
155	The audio goes up as 16 kHz mono FLAC, about half the size of a WAV with the same samples. If the FLAC can't be written, a WAV goes up instead. Frame Job removes its temporary copy from your Mac when the upload ends, whether or not it worked.
156	
157	It's the whole file, not only the parts your clips use, and AssemblyAI bills for the whole file. A two-hour recording you use 30 seconds of costs two hours, about $0.42 at the rate [Frame Job shows](/captions/assemblyai-transcription/#the-price-before-you-press-generate). A file over 10 hours is turned down before anything is sent.
158	
159	The audio goes to the [region](/captions/assemblyai-key/#choose-a-region) set in Settings, and the sheet names that region before you press **Generate**. **Transcribe** in [Remove Filler Words](/cleanup/filler-transcripts/) sends audio in the same way.
160	
161	:::caution
162	A recording of someone else goes to a third party here. Get their say-so first, or use **On this Mac**. The `transcribe` tool gives an agent the same warning.
163	:::
164	
165	## The transcript is deleted after reading
166	
167	Each file's round trip runs in this order: upload, transcribe, read the words back, save them in the project package, then ask AssemblyAI to delete its transcript. You don't have to do anything. Each delete request has 5 seconds to answer.
168	
169	Frame Job also asks for the delete when a transcript fails, runs out of time or can't be used, and when you choose **Cancel** while AssemblyAI is working.
170	
171	A copy of the words stays in your [project package](/captions/assemblyai-transcription/#reuse-a-transcript). That copy is what makes later runs free.
172	
173	If AssemblyAI doesn't confirm the delete, [the result says so](#what-the-result-warns-about).
174	
175	## Unconfirmed deletes are retried
176	
177	An unconfirmed delete is retried at the start of the next AssemblyAI run in the same project that has a key. Every delete still waiting in the project is retried then, whichever files the run is about.
178	
179	The retry uses the key and region set at that later run, so it can only work with a key for the account and region that made the upload. The two regions don't share transcripts. If you've changed either since, set it back for a run.
180	
181	With no key set when that next run starts, nothing is sent, and the delete waits for a run that has one.
182	
183	## A pending delete holds a file back
184	
185	While a delete is pending, Frame Job won't upload that file again, because the kept transcript is its only record of the delete still to be made. If that file's kept transcript still matches the run, it's used as normal. If the file needs a new upload, or you ticked [Transcribe again](/captions/assemblyai-transcription/#transcribe-again), it waits:
186	
187	- The summary line counts it apart, as "1 file waiting on an earlier delete", and leaves it out of the price.
188	- Resting the pointer on the summary gives its price: "It is waiting on an earlier delete and will not be uploaded in this run — about $0.42 more if it does."
189	
190	The hover line says "if it does" because the retry happens first. If the delete goes through at the start of the run, the file uploads in that same run. If it doesn't, the file isn't uploaded, and its clips are listed with the reason "AssemblyAI has not confirmed deleting its earlier transcript, so it was not uploaded again; the next run with an API key retries the delete".
191	
192	## What the result warns about
193	
194	These lines appear on the sheet's result card, with the file's name in place of "name".
195	
196	| The card says | What to do |
197	| --- | --- |
198	| "AssemblyAI has not confirmed deleting the transcript of “name”; it will be retried at the next run with an API key." | Nothing. Run AssemblyAI again in this project when you next need it, with the same account and region. |
199	| "…It was not uploaded again in this run." | Added to the line above when the delete held the file back. |
200	| "AssemblyAI has not confirmed deleting the transcript of “name”; cleanup was deferred because no API key is set. Its deletion ID is retained in the project; a later run with a key for the originating account and region will retry deletion only if that ID is safe to send." | Set the key for that account and region, then run again in this project. |
201	| "AssemblyAI has not confirmed deleting the transcript of “name”. Its transcript could not be saved in the project, so Frame Job cannot retry deleting it automatically. Delete it in your AssemblyAI dashboard." | Frame Job has no record to retry from. Choose [Account Page](/captions/assemblyai-key/#open-your-assemblyai-account) in Settings and delete it there. |
202	
203	:::caution
204	In an [untitled project](/captions/assemblyai-transcription/#transcribe-an-untitled-project), the record of a pending delete lives in a temporary folder. If you never save the project, that record is lost and Frame Job can't retry. Save the project, or delete the transcript in your AssemblyAI dashboard.
205	:::

214	=== assemblyai-transcription
215	---
216	title: "Transcribe with AssemblyAI"
217	description: Send the audio of your files to AssemblyAI on your own key for captions with speakers, a vocabulary and language detection, see the price first, and reuse each transcript for free.
218	---
219	
220	import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
221	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
222	
223	**AssemblyAI** is the cloud engine for captions. It adds speaker labels, a vocabulary of names and jargon, and language detection, and its word timing shows real pauses. You pay AssemblyAI directly on your own key, and each file's transcript is kept so you only pay for it once.
224	
225	<AtAGlance
226	  menu="File ▸ Generate Captions…"
227	  where="Generate Captions sheet ▸ Engine: ▸ AssemblyAI"
228	  tools="transcribe"
229	  needs="Your own AssemblyAI key, unless every file is already transcribed, and a network connection for anything new."
230	/>
231	
232	## Transcribe with AssemblyAI
233	
234	<Steps>
235	
236	1. [Save your AssemblyAI key](/captions/assemblyai-key/) in Settings, if you haven't.
237	
238	2. Choose **File ▸ Generate Captions…**.
239	
240	3. Set **Engine:** to **AssemblyAI**. The **Speakers:**, **Vocabulary:** and **Transcribe again:** rows appear.
241	
242	4. Set [**Language:**](#choose-a-language), and turn on [**Speakers:**](#split-the-words-by-speaker) or fill in [**Vocabulary:**](#add-names-and-jargon) if you want them.
243	
244	5. Read the [price](#the-price-before-you-press-generate) in the summary line.
245	
246	6. Choose **Generate**. Nothing is uploaded until you do.
247	
248	</Steps>
249	
250	The paragraph at the top of the sheet reads "The audio of these files is uploaded to AssemblyAI (United States), transcribed with Universal-3.5 Pro, and deleted from AssemblyAI once the words have been read back. Nothing is uploaded until Generate is pressed." It names your [region](/captions/assemblyai-key/#choose-a-region), which is United States or European Union.
251	
252	Each media file goes up once, and every clip on it takes its words from that one transcript. Frame Job asks for Universal-3.5 Pro and allows Universal-2 as a fallback. This engine doesn't use your Mac's speech models, so it works on a Mac that has none.
253	
254	[What goes to AssemblyAI](/captions/assemblyai-privacy/) says exactly what leaves your Mac and how it's deleted. [Generate Captions](/captions/generate-captions/) covers the rest of the sheet.
255	
256	## Split the words by speaker
257	
258	Tick **Speakers:** ("split by speaker, coloured in Subtitles") to have AssemblyAI label who says what. It's off by default and adds $0.02 an hour to the price.
259	
260	A change of speaker then always starts a new caption: a new cue in [Subtitles](/captions/subtitles/), or a new page in a [word style](/captions/word-caption-styles/). In the Subtitles style, each speaker's cues also take their own colour.
261	
262	Speakers are counted separately for each media file. A speaker is a label within one file, so the same person in two files can come back as two different speakers.
263	
264	## Add names and jargon
265	
266	Type the words you expect into **Vocabulary:**, separated by commas: product names, people, identifiers. They go to AssemblyAI with the request. The field starts empty, and its placeholder reads "names and jargon, separated by commas".
267	
268	Blank entries and exact repeats are dropped. The list stops at 1,000 terms, which is AssemblyAI's limit, and it's cut from the end, so put the terms that matter most first. When the limit cuts your list, the note reads "Vocabulary was capped at 1000 terms (AssemblyAI's limit); N were given."
269	
270	## Choose a language
271	
272	**Language:** opens on **Detect automatically**, which leaves the language to AssemblyAI. The [result](#what-the-result-says) then tells you what it found.
273	
274	You can also name one: English, English (Australia), English (United Kingdom), English (United States), Spanish, French, German, Italian, Portuguese, Arabic, Danish, Dutch, Finnish, Hebrew, Hindi, Japanese, Chinese, Norwegian, Swedish, Turkish or Vietnamese. That list is what AssemblyAI published on 2026-09-17, so it can fall behind.
275	
276	## The price before you press Generate
277	
278	The summary line prices the run at AssemblyAI's published rate, and updates as you change a control:
279	
280	`2 files to upload · 01:12:30.000 of audio · about $0.25 at AssemblyAI's published rate · 1 file already transcribed`
281	
282	The rate is $0.21 an hour of audio, plus $0.02 an hour with **Speakers:** on. Those are the figures AssemblyAI published on 2026-09-17. They're built into Frame Job and aren't fetched, so AssemblyAI's own bill is the real figure. Each file is priced at its whole length, because AssemblyAI [bills for the whole file](/captions/assemblyai-privacy/#what-is-uploaded-and-billed).
283	
284	A very short run reads "under $0.01". When every file is already transcribed the line starts "Nothing to upload", as in `Nothing to upload · 2 files already transcribed`.
285	
286	Two more counts can appear, and neither is in the price:
287	
288	| The line says | What it means |
289	| --- | --- |
290	| "1 file waiting on an earlier delete" | The file [isn't uploaded](/captions/assemblyai-privacy/#a-pending-delete-holds-a-file-back) until AssemblyAI confirms an earlier delete. |
291	| "1 file could not be read" | Frame Job couldn't read the media file, so it can't be transcribed. With nothing else to do, **Generate** is greyed. |
292	
293	## Why each file uploads
294	
295	Rest the pointer on the summary line. You get one line for each file that isn't already transcribed, saying why, and then the rate as a dated sentence.
296	
297	| The line says | What changed |
298	| --- | --- |
299	| "has not been transcribed yet" | This file has no transcript in the project. |
300	| "has changed since it was transcribed" | The file on disk isn't the one that was transcribed. |
301	| "was transcribed with a different language" | The named setting differs from the transcript's. It can also name **model**, **speakers** or **vocabulary**, or several of them. |
302	| "was transcribed for a different request" | Something else about the request differs. |
303	| "is already transcribed, and Transcribe again was asked for" | You ticked [Transcribe again](#transcribe-again). |
304	| "could not be read, so it cannot be transcribed" | The media file couldn't be read. |
305	
306	## Reuse a transcript
307	
308	Each media file's transcript is kept in the project package, every word as AssemblyAI sent it. A later run that wants the same transcript uses it, with no upload, no request and no cost.
309	
310	A transcript is reused when all of these match:
311	
312	- **The file:** its size, modified time and duration, and whether it has audio. Change the file, or relink to a different one, and it's transcribed again.
313	- **The model** Frame Job asks for.
314	- **The language:** **Detect automatically** and a named language count as different, as do two named languages.
315	- **Speakers:** on or off.
316	- **Vocabulary:** the same terms in the same order.
317	
318	The caption style and the looks don't count, so [restyling](/captions/restyle-captions/) never uploads. Your region doesn't count either, so changing it uploads nothing again.
319	
320	A transcript made for [Remove Filler Words](/cleanup/filler-transcripts/) serves captions too, as long as those settings match.
321	
322	The transcript belongs to the media entry, not the file on disk. Two media entries over the same file are uploaded and billed separately.
323	
324	## Transcribe again
325	
326	Tick **Transcribe again:** ("ignore any cached transcript") to ignore what's kept and ask AssemblyAI again. It's off by default. Each file goes up in full and is billed again, and the summary line shows that price.
327	
328	Frame Job won't do this for a file with a [pending delete](/captions/assemblyai-privacy/#a-pending-delete-holds-a-file-back) until the delete goes through.
329	
330	## Generate with no key
331	
332	With no key set, the note reads "No AssemblyAI API key is set. Set one in Frame Job ▸ Settings… ▸ Transcription.", **Generate** is greyed, and resting the pointer on it shows the same sentence. Saving a key in Settings turns **Generate** on with the sheet still open.
333	
334	The exception is work you've already paid for. When every file in the run has a current transcript, **Generate** works with no key, and the paragraph at the top changes to "Current cached transcripts will be used without an API key or network request." Ticking **Transcribe again:** ends that, because it needs a new upload.
335	
336	With a key set the paragraph stays as it is, and the summary line says there's nothing to upload.
337	
338	## Transcribe an untitled project
339	
340	You don't have to save first. An untitled project's transcripts stay in a temporary folder and move into the project package on its first save. Close the project without saving and they're gone, so the same files would be paid for again in a new project. The record of any [delete still pending](/captions/assemblyai-privacy/#what-the-result-warns-about) goes with them.
341	
342	In the rare case that a project has no folder to keep transcripts in at all, the note reads "This project has nowhere to keep its transcript cache, so it cannot be transcribed with AssemblyAI. Save it first." Save the project and carry on.
343	
344	## What the result says
345	
346	While a run goes, the detail line on the sheet's progress card shows the stage for each file: "Extracting", "Uploading" with the megabytes sent, "Submitting", "Waiting for AssemblyAI" with the seconds so far, and "Saving".
347	
348	A run with nothing to report closes the sheet by itself. If there is something, the card stays open with **Close**, and these lines can join the usual count of captions added:
349	
350	| The card says | What it means |
351	| --- | --- |
352	| "“interview.mov”: detected Spanish (97% confidence)." | With **Detect automatically**, the language AssemblyAI found in each file it just transcribed, and how sure it was. The figure is left out if AssemblyAI gave none. |
353	| "“interview.mov” was transcribed with universal-2, not universal-3-5-pro." | AssemblyAI used the fallback model. |
354	| "The transcript of “interview.mov” could not be kept in the project for reuse." | The captions are fine, but a later run may upload and bill this file again. |
355	| "AssemblyAI has not confirmed deleting the transcript of…" | See [What goes to AssemblyAI](/captions/assemblyai-privacy/#what-the-result-warns-about). |
356	
357	## When a file fails
358	
359	One file's failure doesn't end a run. Its clips are listed with the reason, and captions from the other files are still placed. If every file fails, nothing is placed and the card shows why.
360	
361	Two things end a run early, and neither places anything: choosing **Cancel**, and a key AssemblyAI turns down, because every later upload would fail the same way. Files that had already finished stay in the project, so a later run doesn't pay for them again.
362	
363	| The reason reads | What happened |
364	| --- | --- |
365	| "No network connection" | Frame Job couldn't reach AssemblyAI. |
366	| "AssemblyAI refused the API key — check it in Frame Job ▸ Settings" | AssemblyAI turned the key down, and the run stops there. Try **Verify** in [Settings](/captions/assemblyai-key/#check-the-key). |
367	| "AssemblyAI answered 500" | AssemblyAI had a problem of its own. The number varies. |
368	| "AssemblyAI did not finish the transcript in the time allowed." | Frame Job waits at least 5 minutes for a transcript, and longer for audio over about 4 hours. |
369	| "“name” is longer than AssemblyAI's 10-hour limit for one file." | Nothing was sent for this file. |
370	| "AssemblyAI may have created a transcript, but Frame Job could not recover its ID…" | AssemblyAI's reply never reached Frame Job. Check your AssemblyAI dashboard before you try again, because the transcript may still be there. |
371	| AssemblyAI's own sentence | AssemblyAI turned the request down or couldn't transcribe the file, perhaps over a problem with your account, and Frame Job passes on its words. |
372	
373	A failed upload is tried once more, unless AssemblyAI turned it down outright. While waiting, Frame Job checks on the transcript every 3 seconds and rides out up to 3 failed checks in a row. It never follows a redirect, so your key can't reach another host, and the run reports that instead.
374	
375	## Filler words stay out of captions
376	
377	AssemblyAI's words include fillers, and captions leave them out, so a caption reads the same whether or not its transcript has them. The sheet's preview leaves them out too.
378	
379	The words left out are um, uh, hmm, mhm, uh-huh, ah, huh, hm, m, er and erm, in any case and with any punctuation at their edges. The kept transcript still has them, which is what lets [Remove Filler Words](/cleanup/remove-filler-words/) find them later.
380	
381	## With an agent
382	
383	`transcribe` never picks this engine by itself: an agent has to pass `engine: "assemblyai"` on each call, whatever the sheet last chose. It can pass any language code, and one AssemblyAI doesn't support comes back as AssemblyAI's own sentence after the upload.
384	
385	`speakers`, `vocabulary` and `refresh` are the sheet's **Speakers:**, **Vocabulary:** and **Transcribe again:**. They work only with this engine, and the call stops if an agent passes one with `engine: "apple"`.
386	
387	Beside the usual result, a run reports `uploaded`, `cached`, `audio_seconds`, `speech_model_used`, `language_detected`, `endpoint` and, when there's something to say, `note`. A second run over the same files lists them under `cached`.
388	
389	The built-in [Assistant](/assistant/privacy/) can't use this engine at all. Use **File ▸ Generate Captions…**, which shows what's uploaded and what it costs.
390	
391	See [Tools: captions and transcripts](/mcp/tools-captions/).

401	=== delete-words
402	---
403	title: "Cut by deleting words"
404	description: Select words in the Transcript tab and delete them, taking the picture and sound under them out of the timeline and closing the gap.
405	---
406	
407	import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
408	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
409	
410	Editing a spoken video can work like editing text. Select words in the Transcript tab, press <kbd>⌫</kbd>, and the words and everything under them come out of the timeline, with the gap closed.
411	
412	<AtAGlance
413	  menu={['Edit ▸ Delete', 'Edit ▸ Ripple Delete']}
414	  keys={['⌫', '⌦', '⌘⌫']}
415	  where="Inspector ▸ Transcript"
416	  tools={['get_timeline_transcript', 'get_transcript', 'ripple_delete_ranges', 'set_range']}
417	  needs="Words in the Transcript tab, read on this Mac or from an AssemblyAI transcript. Cutting them uploads nothing."
418	/>
419	
420	## Delete words
421	
422	<Steps>
423	
424	1. Choose **View ▸ Transcript** (<kbd>⌃⌘T</kbd>). The Transcript tab opens and its text takes the keyboard. The first time you look, the tab has to [read the file](/captions/transcript-words/), so the words can take a moment to appear.
425	
426	2. [Select the words](#select-words) you want gone.
427	
428	3. Look at what's shaded on the timeline. That's exactly what will go. To hear it first, turn on [Loop](/timeline/loop/), which plays the shaded range.
429	
430	4. Press <kbd>⌫</kbd>.
431	
432	</Steps>
433	
434	The words and the sound under them come out of every unlocked track and the gap closes, as one undo step named **Delete Words**. The range clears and the playhead lands where the cut was.
435	
436	<kbd>⌦</kbd>, <kbd>⌘⌫</kbd>, **Edit ▸ Delete** and **Edit ▸ Ripple Delete** all do the same thing here. On the timeline, <kbd>⌫</kbd> [leaves a gap](/editing/delete-clips/). In the transcript it closes the gap, the way deleting text does.
437	
438	Deleting words one at a time gives the same result as deleting them together, unless a pause of more than a second lies between them. See [where a word cut falls](#where-a-word-cut-falls).
439	
440	:::caution
441	These keys cut words only while the transcript text has the keyboard. If it doesn't, <kbd>⌫</kbd> does what it does on the timeline: with no clip selected, it lifts the shaded range and leaves a gap. Choose **View ▸ Transcript** first to give the text the keyboard. A click on a word would replace your selection.
442	:::
443	
444	## Select words
445	
446	| To | Do this |
447	| --- | --- |
448	| Select one word | Click it. The playhead moves to it too. |
449	| Select a run of words | Drag across them. The text scrolls as you go, and a drag selects words only, never a pause. |
450	| Extend the selection | <kbd>⇧</kbd>-click a word, or press <kbd>⇧</kbd> with an arrow. Neither moves the playhead. |
451	| Select every word | Press <kbd>⌘A</kbd>. |
452	| Clear the selection | Press <kbd>⎋</kbd>. |
453	
454	[Transcript keys](/captions/transcript-keys/) has every key the text takes.
455	
456	## The selection becomes the range
457	
458	Whatever you select becomes the timeline's [in/out range](/timeline/in-out-range/), replacing any range you had, so the timeline shades exactly what will go. With the range set you can [loop](/timeline/loop/) or [export](/export/range/) only those words.
459	
460	The selection can grow as it does this. It widens over any word the cut would cut into, so what's highlighted is what the cut takes. The range lands on the nearest whole frames.
461	
462	<kbd>⎋</kbd> clears the selection and the range with it. It clears only a range the selection set: if you've changed the range since, with <kbd>I</kbd>, <kbd>O</kbd> or an agent, the transcript leaves it alone.
463	
464	## Where a word cut falls
465	
466	A cut runs from where the first word starts to where the next word you keep starts. The pause before the cut stays, and the pause after it goes.
467	
468	- **A long pause after the words.** The cut goes no more than one second past the end of the last deleted word, and the rest of the pause stays.
469	- **Frames.** Both ends land on whole frames, and the end never passes the start of a word that stays.
470	- **The last word on the timeline.** With no word after it, the cut ends where the word ends.
471	- **A clip not read yet.** The cut stops at the start of a clip whose words haven't been read.
472	
473	## Where a word starts
474	
475	When words are [read on this Mac](/captions/transcript-words/), the recogniser puts each word's start early, often well inside the pause before it. So the tab moves each start to where its sound begins. There's nothing for you to do, and this is how it works:
476	
477	1. It finds where the voice model, the one [Remove Silences](/cleanup/remove-silences/) uses, first hears speech after the recogniser's start.
478	2. It then looks for the first hundredth of a second loud enough to be the word: at least −40 dBFS, and 12 dB above the pause's own background noise. The search starts no more than about 0.1 s before the speech, so a click earlier in the pause isn't taken for the word. If nothing is that loud, the start stays where the voice model heard speech.
479	
480	A word after a pause therefore starts on its sound, so a cut that ends at that word neither keeps a slice of the pause nor takes the start of the word you keep.
481	
482	Both steps use what the project measures when it opens a file. Until the voice model has heard a file, the starts are the recogniser's own. The tab moves them as soon as it has, and keeps your selection.
483	
484	Words from an [AssemblyAI transcript](/captions/assemblyai-transcription/), and where any word ends, are left as transcribed.
485	
486	## How exact a word cut is
487	
488	Word edges come from the transcript itself, so in fast speech a cut can take the very end of the word before it, or leave a sliver of the word you deleted. Play the shaded range with [Loop](/timeline/loop/) before you delete, and undo if the cut sounds wrong.
489	
490	## Overlapping words on other tracks
491	
492	If a word on another track starts before your selection and runs into it, say two people talking at once, the tab adds that word to the selection first, along with any words between. You see everything the cut takes before you press <kbd>⌫</kbd>.
493	
494	A word on another track that starts inside your last selected word isn't added. It's the next word you keep, so the cut ends at its start, and the rest of the deleted word after that point can stay in.
495	
496	Only the words the tab shows are added. With **Words from** set to one track, the cut still goes through the other unlocked tracks, and any words it takes there are ones you can't see.
497	
498	## Words that can't be cut
499	
500	Some words are shown faint, because a cut at them would break something. Hold the pointer over one to read why.
501	
502	| Where the word is | What the tab says |
503	| --- | --- |
504	| Inside a [nest](/editing/nests/) | "Inside nest *name*: open it (⌘↓) to cut its words." |
505	| Under a [transition](/motion/transitions/) | "Under a transition: a cut here would leave one clip's tail under its neighbour." |
506	| On a locked track | "Track *name* is locked: a cut would leave these words in place and move everything after them." |
507	
508	A nest or track with no name is given by its number. With a nest open, the tab shows only what's inside it, and a word there is no longer faint for being in that nest.
509	
510	You can still click a faint word to move the playhead there, but a selection that holds one can't be deleted. A clip with a [speed ramp](/speed/make-a-ramp/) isn't faint: its words can be cut.
511	
512	## When the tab won't cut
513	
514	In these cases the tab beeps, keeps your selection and shows the reason at the foot of the inspector, after the word "Refused:". The message stays until the project changes or you click it.
515	
516	| Why | What it says |
517	| --- | --- |
518	| A selected word is [faint](#words-that-cant-be-cut). | That word's own reason. |
519	| A locked track has words inside the cut, even a track **Words from** is hiding. A locked track never moves, so its words would fall out of step. | "Track Music is locked and has words in this cut: unlock it to cut here." |
520	| The cut would pass the project's limit of 4,096 clips while it's being made. Every clip the cut crosses is split first, so a project near the limit can pass it for a moment even if the cut ends with fewer. | "This cut would make 4097 clips; a project holds at most 4096. Lock a track that needs no cut, such as a music bed, or cut less." |
521	
522	Closing the gap can also fail for a reason of its own, such as a linked clip that would have to start before the start of the timeline. That reason shows in the same place.
523	
524	## Good to know
525	
526	- The cut goes through everything on every unlocked track, including music, captions and tracks you've muted or hidden. A locked track with no words in the cut stays whole and doesn't move, which is the way to keep a music bed in one piece.
527	- Markers don't move, as with every [ripple delete](/editing/delete-clips/).
528	
529	## With an agent
530	
531	`get_timeline_transcript` reads the same words, up to 2,000 at a time, and says which can't be cut and why. Each word carries `cut_start` and `cut_end`, the range the tab would cut it by. One `ripple_delete_ranges` call from the first word's `cut_start` to the last word's `cut_end` cuts a run, and `set_range` can shade it first. `get_transcript` reads one clip's words. Neither reading tool uploads anything. If the voice model hasn't heard a file yet, the answer has a note saying its starts are still early, so ask again once it has. See [Tools: captions and transcripts](/mcp/tools-captions/).
532

541	=== edit-captions
542	---
543	title: "Edit captions"
544	description: "Change a caption's words, case, look, position and timing, and see which edits keep a word caption's word-by-word timing."
545	---
546	
547	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
548	
549	A caption is an ordinary text clip, so you edit it the way you edit any text clip. The one thing to watch is word captions. Each of their clips is a **page** of words, with every word timed to the speech. Most edits keep that timing, and a few drop it.
550	
551	<AtAGlance
552	  where={['Clip tab ▸ Text sections', 'Double-click a page on the canvas', 'The timeline']}
553	  tools="set_text"
554	/>
555	
556	## Edit captions in the Text sections
557	
558	Select a caption and open the **Clip** tab. The **Text** sections are **Content**, **Font**, **Style**, **Outline**, **Backdrop**, **Box**, **Reveal** and **Presets**, and they work as they do for any [text clip](/text-and-shapes/text-clips/).
559	
560	Select several captions to change them together. That's the quick way to set a font or a colour across a whole run. Take care with **Content**, though: what you type there replaces the text of every selected caption.
561	
562	To move a caption on the screen, drag it on the canvas or use the **Transform** section. To change when it shows, use the timeline, as [below](#trimming-splitting-and-moving-a-page). The **Presets** buttons set position as well as look.
563	
564	## Change the words on a page
565	
566	Type in the **Content** box, or double-click the page on the canvas and [type there](/text-and-shapes/edit-text-on-canvas/). The same rule holds in both places:
567	
568	| You change | What happens to the timing |
569	| --- | --- |
570	| The text, keeping the same number of words | Every word keeps its timing. Fixing a misheard word is safe. |
571	| The number of words | The page loses its timing and shows plainly, with no word-by-word effect. |
572	
573	Words are counted by the spaces between them, so turning "gonna" into "going to" changes the count.
574	
575	A page that has lost its timing says **Not timed — regenerate to time it again** in the **Content** section. To time it again, [generate the captions again](/captions/restyle-captions/#restyle-by-generating-again). The new pages come from the speech, not from the old track, so your corrections, splits, trims and hand styling on that track go too.
576	
577	## Case on a word page
578	
579	The capitals on a word caption come from its style, through the **UPPERCASE** box in the **Style** section. Untick it to show a page as written.
580	
581	Case is applied when the page is drawn, so the **Content** box always shows the words as written, however the page looks. Changing case never drops the word timing.
582	
583	## Trimming, splitting and moving a page
584	
585	Trim, split and drag a page on the timeline with the usual tools. All three are safe for word timing:
586	
587	- **Trim** changes when the page is on screen. Each word stays on the speech it times, and the page's text doesn't change.
588	- **Split** gives you two clips that play as the one page did. Both keep the page's words, each word still on its speech.
589	- **Dragging** a page moves its words with it, so they stay in step with the page, not with the speech under it.
590	
591	## Reveals do not apply to a timed page
592	
593	The text reveals (**Typewriter**, **Word Fade** and **Line Rise**) don't work on a word caption page. The rows in the **Reveal** section are greyed, and the section says **Word style wins; the reveal does not apply.**
594	
595	That's true of any page with a word style, including one that has lost its timing.
596	
597	## Change a page's word style
598	
599	No inspector section sets a word style's highlight colour, pop scale or pill colour. To change them, [generate the captions again](/captions/restyle-captions/#restyle-by-generating-again) with a different style, or ask an agent.
600	
601	## Newly revealed speech stays uncaptioned
602	
603	When a speed-up or a ramp makes a clip play further into its file, the new part gets no captions until you choose **File ▸ Generate Captions…** again. [Captions follow a speed change](/speed/captions-and-speed/) explains how the captions you already have move.
604	
605	## Word timings for agents
606	
607	An agent can do two things here that the inspector can't: rewrite a page's word timings, and change its word style, both with `set_text`. Frame Job won't take a set of timings that doesn't have exactly one timing for each word of the page, so a change to the number of words has to clear the timings in the same call. Word timings can't be animated with an action. See [Word timings and word style](/mcp/tools-clip-properties/#word-timings-and-word-style).
608	
609	## Good to know
610	
611	- With an [action](/motion/actions/) selected on a page, a **Content** edit goes to that action and the page keeps its timing. Where the action's text has a different number of words from the page, the page shows plainly.
612	- A split page is two text clips, so an [exported caption file](/captions/export-captions/) has two cues with the same words.
613	- Frame Job won't run [Retime Range](/speed/retime-range/) over a caption page with timed words. Move the range off the page first.
614

623	=== export-captions
624	---
625	title: "Export captions"
626	description: "Write a track of captions out as a SubRip or WebVTT file to ship beside your movie, without changing the project."
627	---
628	
629	import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
630	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
631	
632	Export Captions writes one track of captions out as a separate subtitle file, for a platform or player that takes one. Burned-in captions need none of this: they're part of the picture in any [movie you export](/export/export-sheet/).
633	
634	<AtAGlance menu="File ▸ Export Captions…" tools="export_captions" />
635	
636	## Export captions
637	
638	<Steps>
639	
640	1. Choose **File ▸ Export Captions…**. It has no keyboard shortcut, and it's greyed out until some track holds only text clips, with caption text on at least one of them.
641	
642	2. In the save panel, choose the [**Track**](#track) and the [**Format**](#format-subrip-or-webvtt). The name starts as your project's name with `.srt` on the end.
643	
644	3. Choose **Save**.
645	
646	</Steps>
647	
648	Exporting changes nothing in the project, so there's no undo step. If the file can't be written, an alert says why.
649	
650	## Track
651	
652	The **Track** pop-up lists the tracks you can write, front-most first, with the front-most chosen. Each row reads like "Captions — 12 cues (track 4)". The pop-up is greyed when there's only one to choose.
653	
654	Nothing marks a track as a caption track, so any track made only of text clips is listed, a titles track included. A track with any other kind of clip on it isn't listed, and neither is one whose text clips are all empty.
655	
656	With a [nest](/editing/nests/) open, the list shows that nest's tracks.
657	
658	## Format: SubRip or WebVTT
659	
660	The **Format** pop-up offers **SubRip (.srt)**, the default, and **WebVTT (.vtt)**. Choose whichever your player or platform asks for. Changing it changes the extension in the name field and keeps the name you've typed.
661	
662	The words and times are the same in both. The files differ like this:
663	
664	| | SubRip | WebVTT |
665	| --- | --- | --- |
666	| First line of the file | The first cue | `WEBVTT` |
667	| A number above each cue | Yes | No |
668	| Timestamps | `00:00:04,133` | `00:00:04.133` |
669	| `&`, `<` and `>` in the text | Written as they are | Escaped |
670	
671	Both use Unix (LF) line endings and end with one newline.
672	
673	## One cue per text clip
674	
675	Each text clip on the track becomes one cue, at the time and with the words it has now. A caption you dragged exports where you dragged it. Styling plays no part, so restyling a caption doesn't change the file.
676	
677	- A caption with no text is left out.
678	- Line endings become LF. Blank lines inside a caption are removed, and so are spaces at the ends of its lines.
679	- A word caption track is written one cue per page, with the page's words as written. The style's **UPPERCASE**, the word timings and the styling don't go in the file.
680	
681	## Frame-exact round trips
682	
683	Export a track and [import it again](/captions/import-captions/), and every cue goes back on the frame it came from, at every ordinary frame rate.
684	
685	The file itself may not match the one you first imported, because import moves each time onto a whole frame. At 30 fps, `00:00:04,120` comes back as `00:00:04,133`. A file only comes back byte for byte when its cue times are already on whole frames and a frame lasts a whole number of milliseconds, as it does at 25 or 50 fps.
686	
687	## With an agent
688	
689	`export_captions` takes a `path`, and can be given a `track` and a `format`. With no `format` it follows the path's `.srt` or `.vtt`, and a `format` you name wins over the extension.
690	
691	It never guesses the track. With no track to write, it writes nothing and says so. With more than one and none named, it writes nothing and lists the candidates. A track it writes comes back through `import_captions` with every cue where it was. See [`export_captions`](/mcp/tools-captions/#export_captions).
692

701	---
702	title: "Follow along and jump"
703	description: "Watch the spoken word light up as the video plays, and use the transcript to move around the timeline."
704	---
705	
706	import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
707	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
708	
709	The [Transcript tab](/captions/transcript-tab/) stays in step with the playhead, and works the other way too: click the text and the playhead goes there. Use it to find a moment by what was said, instead of scrubbing for it.
710	
711	<AtAGlance
712	  menu="View ▸ Transcript"
713	  keys="⌃⌘T"
714	  where="Inspector ▸ Transcript"
715	  tools="set_playhead"
716	/>
717	
718	## The word being spoken
719	
720	While the video plays, the word being spoken is highlighted. It stays lit through the pause after it, until the next word starts. Before the first word, nothing is lit.
721	
722	The highlight follows the playhead when you're paused too, so moving the playhead by hand lights the word there.
723	
724	## The text scrolls with playback
725	
726	During playback the text scrolls to keep the spoken word in view.
727	
728	If you scroll the text yourself, it stays where you put it for three seconds before it follows again. With playback paused, the text doesn't scroll on its own.
729	
730	## Click a word to jump
731	
732	Click a word to move the playhead to it and select it. The playhead lands on a whole frame. If the video is playing, it keeps playing from there.
733	
734	The selected word becomes the timeline's in/out range, so clicking a word replaces any range you've set. See [Cut by deleting words](/captions/delete-words/).
735	
736	## Click a timecode to jump
737	
738	Click a paragraph's timecode to move the playhead to the start of that paragraph. Unlike a click on a word, this doesn't change the selection.
739	
740	## A selected clip scrolls to its words
741	
742	Click a clip that's already selected, on the timeline or the canvas, while the Transcript shows. The tab stays, and the clip's first word scrolls to the top. The playhead doesn't move.
743	
744	The click that selects a clip doesn't bring its words up, so click it a second time. Leave a moment between the clicks: a double-click on the timeline renames the clip, or opens a nest.
745	
746	For a nest clip, that's the first word inside the nest. A clip with no words in the tab scrolls nothing.
747	
748	## Loop plays the selected words
749	
750	Whatever you select in the text becomes the in/out range, so [Loop](/timeline/loop/) can play it. Use it to hear a cut before you make it.
751	
752	<Steps>
753	
754	1. Select the words: drag across them, or click the first and <kbd>⇧</kbd>-click the last.
755	
756	2. Turn on **Loop**, the repeat button in the toolbar.
757	
758	3. Press <kbd>Space</kbd>.
759	
760	</Steps>
761	
762	Change the selection and the next pass plays the new range. <kbd>Esc</kbd> clears the selection and the range with it, and Loop then goes round the whole timeline.
763	
764	## With an agent
765	
766	`get_timeline_transcript` gives each word's time on the timeline, and `set_playhead` moves the playhead there. See [Tools: playhead, range and selection](/mcp/tools-view-state/).
767
