811	=== word-caption-looks
812	---
813	title: Looks for word captions
814	description: Add a sliding pill, a left-to-right word fill or a dim in pauses to word captions, and find out what you can change about their colours.
815	---
816	
817	import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
818	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
819	
820	Looks add movement to a [word style](/captions/word-caption-styles/)'s pages: a pill that slides between words, a word that fills as it's said, and a page that dims when nobody's talking.
821	
822	<AtAGlance
823	  menu="File ▸ Generate Captions…"
824	  where="The Generate Captions sheet, under Style:"
825	  tools={['transcribe', 'set_text']}
826	/>
827	
828	## Three looks for word captions
829	
830	<Steps>
831	
832	1. Choose **File ▸ Generate Captions…**, and set **Language:**, **Engine:** and **From:** as [Generate Captions](/captions/generate-captions/) explains.
833	
834	2. Set **Style:** to a [word style](/captions/word-caption-styles/).
835	
836	3. Tick the looks you want under the **Style:** pop-up.
837	
838	4. Choose **Generate**.
839	
840	</Steps>
841	
842	Each look works with some styles and not others:
843	
844	| Look | Highlight | Pill | Karaoke | Build | One Word |
845	| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
846	| **Slide the pill** | | Yes | | | |
847	| **Fill words as spoken** | Yes | | Yes | Yes | |
848	| **Dim in pauses** | Yes | Yes | Yes | Yes | Yes |
849	
850	A box that doesn't apply to the chosen style is greyed out and does nothing, but it keeps its tick for when you switch back. With **Subtitles** chosen, all three are greyed out.
851	
852	Each box is off until you tick it, and the sheet remembers each one between runs.
853	
854	A look changes how a word is drawn, never a letter or the size of the page. Ticking one doesn't change where pages break.
855	
856	Looks are set when the captions are generated, like the style. To change them on a placed track, [generate again with Replace](/captions/restyle-captions/#restyle-by-generating-again).
857	
858	## Slide the pill
859	
860	The pill slides from the previous word to the one being said, instead of jumping. The slide takes 0.2 s, or less when the next word starts sooner, so the pill has always arrived before it has to leave. The first word on a page has nothing to slide from, so the pill starts there.
861	
862	This works with **Pill**, the only style that has one.
863	
864	## Fill words as spoken
865	
866	The word being said fills from left to right as it's spoken. The fill runs from the word's start to its end, and takes 0.6 s at most, so a long word finishes filling before it's finished being said.
867	
868	| Style | The part already said | The rest of the word |
869	| --- | --- | --- |
870	| **Highlight** | Yellow | White |
871	| **Karaoke** | Yellow | White at 55% opacity |
872	| **Build** | Yellow | Not drawn yet |
873	
874	**Pill** and **One Word** can't use this look, because their spoken word is the same colour on both sides of the fill.
875	
876	## Dim in pauses
877	
878	The page fades to half opacity during a pause of 0.25 s or more, then comes back before the next word. Each fade takes 0.1 s, and the words and the pill fade together. It works with all five word styles.
879	
880	The page also dims at either end of a caption, when the wait there is 0.25 s or more:
881	
882	- before the first word. The page opens dim, with no fade.
883	- after the last word, until the caption ends.
884	
885	A pause of 0.25 s also [ends a page](/captions/word-caption-styles/#where-a-page-breaks), so on a generated track you'll mostly see the dim at the end of a page, after its last word.
886	
887	With **On this Mac** chosen and a word style selected, a note under the boxes reads "On-device words rarely carry a pause; this shows mostly with AssemblyAI."
888	
889	The sheet's [preview](/captions/word-caption-styles/#the-sheets-two-frame-preview) doesn't show this look.
890	
891	## Word colours
892	
893	The inspector has no section for a page's word colours, pop size or pill. Nothing in the Clip tab changes the yellow, the violet or how far the word pops.
894	
895	To change them, generate again with a [different style](/captions/restyle-captions/#restyle-by-generating-again), or [have an agent do it](#with-an-agent).
896	
897	The **Color** row under **Text ▸ Style** still works on the words drawn in the text's own colour. That's the white words in **Highlight** and **Build**, and every word in **Pill** and **One Word**. It leaves the yellow alone, and it changes nothing in **Karaoke**, which sets all its own colours.
898	
899	## With an agent
900	
901	An agent can do two things here that the sheet can't.
902	
903	It can change a placed page's word style with `set_text`. That covers highlighting or building word by word, the colours of the spoken word and of the words before and after it, a pop from 100% to 150%, the pill's colour, padding and corners, whether the pill slides, whether the word fills, and how far the page dims, from none to fully invisible. The sheet's dim is always half. A page changed this way is no longer one of the styles Frame Job makes, so [Re-lay Captions](/captions/re-lay-captions/#tracks-kept-as-placed) keeps its track as placed. See [Tools: text, shapes and clip names](/mcp/tools-clip-properties/).
904	
905	It can also ask for looks with `transcribe`, through `slide`, `fill` and `dim`, but each one is off unless it asks, never what the sheet last chose. Frame Job won't add a look to a style it wouldn't show on, or to captions it isn't placing. When it gives any of the three and the captions are placed, the result lists the looks that were on. See [Tools: captions and transcripts](/mcp/tools-captions/).
906	
907	## Related
908	
909	- [Generate Captions](/captions/generate-captions/)
910	- [Word caption styles](/captions/word-caption-styles/)
911	- [Restyle a caption track](/captions/restyle-captions/)
912	- [Edit captions](/captions/edit-captions/)
913	=== word-caption-styles
914	---
915	title: Word caption styles
916	description: Make the large word-by-word captions used in shorts and reels, choose how the spoken word is marked, and see how pages are filled for your canvas.
917	---
918	
919	import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
920	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
921	
922	The five word styles make the large captions used in shorts and reels, where each word is marked as it's said. For classic two-line cues, use [Subtitles](/captions/subtitles/) instead.
923	
924	<AtAGlance
925	  menu="File ▸ Generate Captions…"
926	  where="The Generate Captions sheet ▸ Style:"
927	  tools="transcribe"
928	/>
929	
930	## Make word captions
931	
932	<Steps>
933	
934	1. Choose **File ▸ Generate Captions…**.
935	
936	2. Set **Language:**, **Engine:** and **From:**. [Generate Captions](/captions/generate-captions/) explains each one.
937	
938	3. Set **Style:** to **Highlight**, **Pill**, **Karaoke**, **Build** or **One Word**. The sheet remembers your choice for next time.
939	
940	4. Tick any [looks](/captions/word-caption-looks/) you want, and check the [preview](#the-sheets-two-frame-preview).
941	
942	5. Choose **Generate**.
943	
944	</Steps>
945	
946	## Word caption pages
947	
948	A word style doesn't make cues. Each clip holds a **page** of words, with each word's timing, and the word being spoken is drawn the way the style says. A page is still an ordinary [text clip](/captions/how-captions-work/), so you can drag, trim and split it.
949	
950	All five styles are white with the spoken word marked. Words are marked by their timing only, so there's no keyword emphasis and no emoji.
951	
952	The text is 7.5% of the canvas's shorter side, or 12% for One Word. That means a vertical and a horizontal canvas get the same text height: on both 1080 × 1920 and 1920 × 1080 it's 81 px, or 130 px for One Word. Where a style pops the spoken word, the pop takes 0.12 s.
953	
954	## The five styles
955	
956	### Highlight
957	
958	The spoken word turns yellow and pops to 112%, and the other words stay white.
959	
960	Montserrat Black with a black outline, in capitals. The box is centred a quarter of the frame height below the middle.
961	
962	### Pill
963	
964	The spoken word sits on a violet pill, and doesn't change size. [Slide the pill](/captions/word-caption-looks/#slide-the-pill) makes the pill travel between words instead of jumping.
965	
966	Montserrat ExtraBold, in capitals. The box is centred a quarter of the frame height below the middle.
967	
968	### Karaoke
969	
970	Words turn yellow as they're said and stay yellow. Words still to come are white at 55% opacity.
971	
972	Montserrat ExtraBold, as written. Karaoke can use up to two lines, and it's the only style that wraps a page of several words. The box is centred 28% of the frame height below the middle.
973	
974	### Build
975	
976	Words appear one by one. The newest is yellow and pops to 115%, and the ones before it are white.
977	
978	Anton with a black outline, in capitals. The box is centred a quarter of the frame height below the middle.
979	
980	### One Word
981	
982	One large word at a time, white, popping to 120%. Every page holds one word.
983	
984	Bebas Neue with a black outline, in capitals. The box is centred 18% of the frame height below the middle.
985	
986	## Bundled typefaces
987	
988	Montserrat Black, Montserrat ExtraBold, Anton and Bebas Neue ship inside the app under the SIL Open Font License, so there's nothing to install.
989	
990	## Pages are filled to their measured width
991	
992	A page holds as many words as fit, not a set number. Frame Job measures each page in its style's typeface, size, case and outline on your canvas, and fills it up to 86% of the canvas width, on one line. Karaoke can use two lines, and One Word always holds one word.
993	
994	So the same speech makes shorter pages on a 9:16 canvas than on a 16:9 one. On a 1080 × 1920 canvas a page can be about 929 px wide. If you change the canvas size later, [Re-lay Captions for This Canvas](/captions/re-lay-captions/) pages them again.
995	
996	When a page ends because the width ran out, Frame Job can move its last word onto the next page if the two then come closer in width. That stops a sentence ending on one word alone.
997	
998	## Where a page breaks
999	
1000	A page ends early at any of these:
1001	
1002	- a pause of 0.25 s or more between two words
1003	- a word ending in `.` `?` `!` or `…`
1004	- 3 seconds on screen, up to the end of the page's last word
1005	- a change of speaker, when [**Speakers:**](/captions/assemblyai-transcription/) is ticked
1006	
1007	When the width runs out within two words of a comma, semicolon or colon, the break moves back to that mark. It only does this when the page is already at least half full and the words that move still fit on the next page.
1008	
1009	On-device words rarely carry a pause, so pages from **On this Mac** break at pauses less often than pages from AssemblyAI.
1010	
1011	## A word too wide for the frame
1012	
1013	A word too wide for a page gets a page of its own and shrinks in 5% steps, down to 80% of the style's size, until it fits. If it's still too wide at 80%, it stays at that size and wraps.
1014	
1015	## How long a page stays up
1016	
1017	A page stays up 0.5 s after its last word, and the row is empty until the next page. If the next page starts sooner than that, the page runs right up to it, so the row doesn't blink between pages.
1018	
1019	Pages never run past the end of the clip they came from.
1020	
1021	## The sheet's two-frame preview
1022	
1023	The preview under the looks shows a sample page, drawn the way the canvas draws it and paged for this canvas's proportions. It shows you how the style looks, not how big it will be, because each frame is scaled to fit the strip.
1024	
1025	| What you see | What it means |
1026	| --- | --- |
1027	| Two frames | A word style, with the first word active in the top frame and the second word in the bottom one. A page of one word shows that word in both. |
1028	| One frame | Subtitles. |
1029	| The sample words | The first words of the first clip's cached AssemblyAI transcript when there is one, otherwise "This is how it looks". |
1030	| A half-filled word | **Fill words as spoken** is ticked. |
1031	| A pill between two words | **Slide the pill** is ticked. It shows in the second frame. |
1032	
1033	**Dim in pauses** isn't previewed.
1034	
1035	## Good to know
1036	
1037	- A style is set when the captions are generated, and you can't switch it on a placed track. To change it, see [Restyle a caption track](/captions/restyle-captions/).
1038	- The capitals are applied when a page is drawn, so the words stay as written in the **Content** box and in an [exported caption file](/captions/export-captions/). To show a page as written, untick **UPPERCASE**. See [Edit captions](/captions/edit-captions/).
1039	- [Text reveals](/text-and-shapes/text-reveal/) don't apply to a timed page.
1040	- The [Subtitles](/captions/subtitles/) style is the first choice in the **Style:** pop-up, and it works differently: two-line cues with no word timing.
1041	
1042	## With an agent
1043	
1044	`transcribe` makes word captions when it asks for a word style: `highlight`, `pill`, `karaoke`, `build` or `one_word`. It never uses the style the sheet last chose. See [Tools: captions and transcripts](/mcp/tools-captions/).
1045	
1046	## Related
1047	
1048	- [Generate Captions](/captions/generate-captions/)
1049	- [Looks for word captions](/captions/word-caption-looks/)
1050	- [Restyle a caption track](/captions/restyle-captions/)
1051	- [Re-lay captions for a canvas](/captions/re-lay-captions/)
1052	- [Edit captions](/captions/edit-captions/)

144:## `ripple_delete_ranges`
145-
146-Cuts several stretches of time out of the timeline as one edit and one undo step, named Ripple Delete, however many ranges there are.
147-
148-[Remove Silences](/cleanup/remove-silences/) and [Remove Filler Words](/cleanup/remove-filler-words/) make this cut from their sheets. See [Ripple delete several ranges](/editing/delete-clips/#ripple-delete-several-ranges).
149-
150-| Argument | Type | Required | What it does |
151-| --- | --- | --- | --- |
152-| `ranges` | array of `[from, to]` pairs of ticks | Yes | The stretches to cut, at least one. A single pair may be written flat, as `[from, to]`. |
153-| `project` | string | No | The open project to act on, by the path `get_project` reports. Left out, the frontmost. |
154-| `scope` | integer | No | A nest's id, to edit inside it. Left out, whatever is open. See [Editing inside a nest](/mcp/nests/). |
155-
156-`detect_silence` and `detect_fillers` return ranges in this shape. A `cut_start` and `cut_end` from `get_timeline_transcript` make a pair too, so a run of words is one range from its first word's `cut_start` to its last word's `cut_end`. See [Tools: clean-up](/mcp/tools-clean-up/).
157-
158-Each pair is rounded to the frame grid and put in order, so a reversed pair is the same range. Pairs that touch or overlap then merge, and what's left is cut from right to left, each cut as `ripple_delete_range` makes it. So every time you send is a time in the project as you read it, and this isn't the same as calling `ripple_delete_range` once per pair: two ranges that meet make one shift, not two.
159-
160-**Answers** `new_clips`, the pieces left after each range of any clip cut at a range's end.
161-
162-**Won't run** when `ranges` is empty, which is an error, or when a shift would push a linked clip before the start of the timeline. A list whose pairs are all empty changes nothing. Each cut can add a clip, so a list that would pass 4,096 clips is an error and nothing is cut.
163-
164-## `lift_range`
165-
166-Cuts a stretch of time out and leaves the hole. Every clip on an unlocked track is cut at both ends of the range and what's between is removed, and nothing moves. Use it when a mix or a caption track is already timed.

---
title: "On-device media analysis"
description: "What Frame Job works out about your files on this Mac, when it runs, how to stop it, and where the results are kept."
---

import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
import Shot from '@components/Shot.astro';

Frame Job studies your files so its commands know where the cuts fall, who's in frame and when someone is talking. All of it happens on this Mac, with no upload, no network request and no key.

<AtAGlance
  menu={['Clip ▸ Split at Shot Changes', 'Clip ▸ Follow Subject…', 'Clip ▸ Remove Background', 'Clip ▸ Switch by Speaker…', 'File ▸ Make Vertical Version…']}
  where={['The Analyzing sheet', 'Clip tab ▸ Picture ▸ Background']}
  tools={['get_media_analysis', 'analyze_cutout', 'split_at_shots', 'reframe_clip', 'detect_silence', 'set_media_speech', 'set_video', 'new_project_from_range', 'make_vertical_version']}
  needs="Nothing. Every analysis runs on your Mac, with no key and no upload."
/>

This page explains the analysis itself. How to use a result is on the page of the feature that uses it.

## What Frame Job works out

| Result | When it's made | What uses it |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [Filmstrips, waveforms and loudness](#whats-built-when-a-file-arrives) | When a file arrives | The timeline and the audio tools |
| [Voice detection](#voice-detection) | When a file arrives | Remove Silences, Enhance Voice, Duck by Speech and others |
| [Shots](#shots) | When something asks | Split at Shot Changes, Follow Subject, Make Vertical Version |
| [Faces](#faces) | When something asks | Follow Subject, Make Vertical Version, Switch by Speaker, Show Subjects |
| [People and salient regions](#people-and-salient-regions) | When something asks | Follow Subject, Make Vertical Version, Show Subjects |
| [Person masks](#person-masks) | When a clip needs them | Remove Background, Text Behind Subject |
| [Foreground masks](#foreground-masks-on-pictures) | When a picture needs one | Remove Background, Text Behind Subject |
| [Sound events](#sound-events) | When an agent asks | Agents only |

## Analysis happens on demand

Importing a file doesn't analyse its picture. Frame Job does that when something asks for it: Split at Shot Changes, Follow Subject, Make Vertical Version, Switch by Speaker, Remove Background, Text Behind Subject or an agent.

Only the part that's needed is read:

- Follow Subject, Make Vertical Version and an agent reframing a clip ask for the part of the file each clip plays, plus a second either side.
- Split at Shot Changes reads the parts its clips play, and skips any stretch of the file between them that no clip uses.
- A part that's already been analysed isn't read again, so a second request over the same footage starts at once.

If two analyses of one file run at different times, what they find is added together. Neither replaces the other.

## The Analyzing sheet

When a menu command needs an analysis that isn't in the project yet, the **Analyzing** sheet comes up while it's made. When everything is already there, the sheet doesn't appear and the command goes straight ahead.

<Shot
  name="15f-analyzing-sheet.sheet"
  alt="The Analyzing sheet for Split at Shot Changes. A sentence explains that nothing changes until the analysis is found and that Stop leaves everything as it is. Below it, the file speech.mov has an empty progress bar and the word Waiting, and a Stop button sits at the bottom right."
/>

The sheet has one row for each file that needs work, with its name, a bar and a status:

| Status | What it means |
| --- | --- |
| Waiting | Frame Job hasn't read the file's first frame yet. |
| A percentage | The share of the work done so far. |
| Done | This file has finished. |

For [Follow Subject](/framing/follow-subject/) and [Make Vertical Version](/framing/make-vertical-version/), a file can have a row for each thing being found, such as "speech.mov — Faces", "speech.mov — Shot changes" and "speech.mov — People and salient regions".

These commands use the sheet:

- **Clip ▸ Split at Shot Changes**
- **Clip ▸ Follow Subject…**, after you press **Follow** in its own sheet
- **File ▸ Make Vertical Version…**, after you press **Make** in its own sheet
- **Clip ▸ Switch by Speaker…**, before its own sheet, when it needs to find faces because it's working from one microphone

When every row is done, the sheet closes by itself and the command carries on. Every editor action is off while the sheet is up.

If the project changes while the sheet is up, which an agent can do, the command makes no edit. The inspector says so and asks you to choose the command again.

[Remove Background](/effects/remove-background/) doesn't use this sheet. It makes its masks while you go on working, and shows its progress in **Status** in the Clip tab's **Background** section.

### Stop an analysis

Choose **Stop**, or press <kbd>Esc</kbd>. The sheet closes, the command is cancelled and no edit is made. What was already saved stays in the project, so choosing the command again carries on from there.

Minimising the window also stops the work. When you bring the window back, the sheet starts again on whatever hadn't finished.

### When an analysis fails

If an analysis can't finish, the command stops instead of editing with half an answer. Frame Job beeps, and the foot of the inspector names the file and the reason, for example: "The shots analysis of “interview.mov” failed: …"

If a file is missing or can't be read, Split at Shot Changes and Switch by Speaker stop before the sheet opens, and Follow Subject says so in its own sheet. Make Vertical Version keeps a clip whose file is missing as it's placed and goes on with the rest. See [Relink missing media](/projects/relink-media/).

## Analysis runs in the background

You can keep working while an analysis runs, except while the Analyzing sheet is up.

- Picture analysis runs at low priority, one job at a time across all your open projects.
- Sound analysis has its own queue, so one sound job can run beside one picture job.
- Frame Job saves what it has found every 30 seconds, and at the end of each stretch of the file it reads. If a job stops part-way, everything saved so far is kept and the next request continues from there.
- A job that nothing wants any more is dropped if it hasn't started, and cancelled if it has. Closing a project does this to its jobs.

## What each analysis finds

### Shots

Frame Job finds the hard cuts in a video by comparing each frame's colours with the frames before it. This is plain arithmetic, with no machine learning.

- A gradual dissolve isn't reported as a cut.
- A single flash frame isn't a cut.
- A dissolve between flat-coloured pictures, such as slides or title cards, can show as one cut.

[Split at Shot Changes](/editing/split-at-shot-changes/) cuts your clips at these moments.

### Faces

Frame Job looks for faces ten times a second of the file's own time, using Apple's Vision framework. For each face it keeps its box, how far it's turned and tilted, and how open the mouth is.

Faces are listed from left to right. They carry no identity, so Frame Job doesn't know that a face in one sample is the same person in the next, and it never puts names to faces.

### People and salient regions

At the same ten samples a second, Frame Job finds:

- **People**, as a box around each person's head and shoulders.
- **Salient regions**, as boxes around the parts of the picture the eye goes to first. In a talking-head shot that's usually the speaker, and on a slide it's often the text.

Each sample is judged on its own, so no person is followed from one moment to the next. See [Subjects in the picture](/framing/what-is-found/) for how Frame Job uses them, and [Show Subjects](/framing/show-subjects/) to see faces, people and salient regions over the preview.

### Person masks

A person mask is an outline of a person, made for every frame of the video that a clip plays. [Remove Background](/effects/remove-background/) and [Text Behind Subject](/effects/text-behind-subject/) draw with these masks, and they're made when a clip has one of those on.

A frame counts as holding a person when at least 0.5 % of its mask is above half strength. The masks are kept at the size Vision makes them, one for every frame, so a long clip's masks take up room in the package: about 62 MB for a minute of 1080p video.

### Foreground masks on pictures

On a still picture, Frame Job can mask the foreground subject, whether or not it's a person. Turn on Remove Background, then choose **Foreground** in the **Subject** row of the Clip tab's **Background** section. The row appears when every selected clip is a picture, and **Person** is the default.

Either way a picture gets one mask, made from the picture as it's drawn, the right way up.

### Sound events

Frame Job can listen to a file's first sound track and score how likely six kinds of sound are: laughter, applause, cheering, crowd, music and speech. It uses Apple's Sound Analysis, in overlapping windows 1.5 seconds long that start every 0.75 seconds. Each score runs from 0 to 1, and there's no score where a window runs past the end of the sound.

Only an agent can ask for these, and no menu or pane uses them. Treat the scores as hints, never as a finding on their own.

The file needs sound, and an audio file works. Frame Job won't read sound events for a clip that plays in reverse, because its sound runs backwards.

## What's built when a file arrives

After you open a project, import a file or relink one, Frame Job builds these in the background, and the timeline fills in as they finish:

- **Filmstrip thumbnails** for every file with a picture, which its clips show on the timeline. See [Reading a clip on the timeline](/timeline/reading-a-clip/).
- **The waveform**, at 100 peaks a second.
- **The loudness record**, in 10 ms steps, which Normalize, Enhance Voice and the loudness read-outs use.
- **Sound-matching features**, which [Synchronize Audio](/audio/synchronize-audio/) uses.
- **[Voice detection](#voice-detection)**.

At most two files' sound is read at a time, so a big import doesn't hold up playback or a speed ramp's sound. Anything already built for an unchanged file is never built again. A file with no sound has no waveform, loudness or voice detection, and a `.cube` LUT file gets none of these.

Until one of these is ready, the controls that need it wait or read "measuring…". A command that needs it says the file is still being analysed and asks you to try again in a moment.

If a waveform or loudness pass fails, Frame Job tries again after 2 seconds and again after 10. After that it tries the next time you open the project.

### Voice detection

Frame Job scores every 32 ms of a file's sound for speech, using the Silero voice model bundled with the app. That's how later commands tell a voice from noise. These use it:

- [Remove Silences](/cleanup/voice-or-level/), in its **Voice** mode
- [Enhance Voice](/audio/enhance-voice/) and [Match Audio](/audio/match-audio/)
- The [Leveller](/audio/leveller/)
- [Duck by Speech](/audio/duck-by-speech/)
- [Synchronize Audio](/audio/synchronize-audio/)
- [Switch by Speaker](/multicam/switch-by-speaker/)
- [Speed Up Typing](/recording/speed-up-typing/)
- [Cut by deleting words](/captions/delete-words/) and [Shorten a pause](/captions/shorten-pauses/)
- The [Transcript tab](/captions/transcript-tab/), to place where a word on this Mac's reading really starts and to find the pauses between paragraphs

If the voice model can't be used, Remove Silences says so and judges quiet by level instead.

## Results are kept per file

Anything Frame Job finds is kept for the file, not for a clip, in the project's cache, a folder of things it can make again. Every clip of a file shares it, and a second request over the same part is ready at once. Picture analysis and sound events live in the `.framejob` package under `cache/analysis/`.

A result counts only for the file it was made from, which Frame Job checks by the file's size, modification time and length. Relink to a different file, or change the file on disk, and it's analysed again. An unchanged file isn't.

Picture analysis and sound events also record the macOS build they were made on. After a macOS update, or on a Mac running a different build, they're made again the next time something asks. The same goes when a Frame Job update changes what one of them stores.

## Results travel with the project

The caches live inside the `.framejob` package, so they go wherever it goes. Moving, copying or consolidating a package keeps them. See [The .framejob package](/reference/framejob-package/) for what's inside.

A new project made from this one starts with them too, so nothing is analysed twice. [New Project from Range](/projects/new-project-from-range/) and the **Make a copy** option of [Make Vertical Version](/framing/make-vertical-version/) carry these, for each file the new project keeps:

- Filmstrips, waveforms and loudness
- Voice detection and sound-matching features
- On-device transcripts
- Everything on this page that's found in the picture or sound
- The reversed render of any clip that plays backwards

Your media files are never copied. Neither is speed-ramp audio, or a voice-isolated or voice-effect render, and those are made again when they're needed. A cloud transcript stays behind unless its copy on AssemblyAI has already been deleted.

## Good to know

- **Show Subjects** never starts an analysis. Where nothing has been found it reads "Not analyzed — Clip ▸ Follow Subject… analyzes it".
- A package with a missing or damaged cache still opens, and what's built when a file arrives is built again. Picture analysis is made again when something next asks, but a lost cloud transcript costs money to make again.
- Until an untitled project is first saved, its caches sit in a temporary folder. The first save copies them into the package.

## With an agent

An agent can read the results themselves with `get_media_analysis`, for a whole file or for the part one clip plays, and it's the only way to reach [sound events](#sound-events). It shows no sheet. It waits at most 60 seconds, then stops and says how much it covered. What it covered is kept, so asking again carries on. A long file is read in windows, because one reply has a size limit. Each reply says whether it came from the cache alone, and what the result was made with.

`analyze_cutout` makes a clip's masks and says where they stand. See [Tools: reading analysis](/mcp/tools-analysis/).

## Related

- [Split at Shot Changes](/editing/split-at-shot-changes/)
- [Subjects in the picture](/framing/what-is-found/)
- [Follow Subject](/framing/follow-subject/)
- [Remove Background](/effects/remove-background/)
- [Relink missing media](/projects/relink-media/)
- [The .framejob package](/reference/framejob-package/)
- [Tools: reading analysis](/mcp/tools-analysis/)
The **Remove background** checkbox, **Subject** and the section's **Reset** always change the clip itself, even with an action selected, and the checkbox and **Subject** rows show ⊘. You can't turn a cut-out off at the end of an action.

## How the masks are made

A mask is the outline of the subject in one frame. You never start this yourself. When you turn Remove Background on, or change what a cut-out clip plays, Frame Job makes masks for the frames that clip plays, in the background, while you go on working.

Masks are made on this Mac with person segmentation from Apple's Vision framework, at its balanced setting. Nothing is uploaded, and no key is needed. They're kept per media in the project's cache, so a frame that's been analysed is never analysed again. See [On-device media analysis](/projects/media-analysis/#person-masks).

Until a frame has its mask, the clip draws whole in the preview, as if Remove Background were off. A paused frame redraws by itself once its mask is ready, and a playing preview picks new masks up on its next frame.

### Status

**Status** says where the clip's masks stand, and why a clip is drawing whole.

| Status | What it means |
| --- | --- |
| **Analyzing N %** | The masks are being made. The figure stops at 99 until they're done. |
| **Ready** | Every frame the clip plays has its mask. |
| **No person found** | Every frame was looked at and no person is in the clip, so it draws whole. A frame counts as holding a person when at least 0.5 % of its mask is above half. |
| **No subject found** | A picture with **Subject** set to **Foreground** was looked at and no subject was found, so it draws whole. |
| **Failed:** and the reason | The masks couldn't be made. The media file may be missing or unreadable, or the masks couldn't be written. Fix the cause and choose **Analyze Now**. |
| **No picture to analyze** | The clip plays no frame of its file. |
| **Off** | Remove Background is off. |
| **—** | Several clips are selected. |

### Analyze Now

Masks start on their own, so you'll mostly want this after a failure. **Analyze Now** asks again for the masks the clip needs, then retries a run that failed. It's enabled only while a clip is analysing or has failed.

## Pictures

<Shot
  name="05k-clip-background-picture.inspector"
  alt="The Background section for an image clip. Remove background is ticked, a Subject row reads Foreground above Background, which reads Remove, then Edge, Feather and a Status of Analyzing 0 %."
/>

A picture gets one mask, made once on this Mac from the picture as the preview draws it, the right way up. When it's done, **Status** goes from Analyzing to **Ready**, or to **No person found** or **No subject found**.

**Person** uses the same person segmentation as a video. **Foreground** uses the Vision framework's foreground instance mask, which keeps every foreground subject it finds. If it finds none, **Status** reads **No subject found** and the picture draws whole.

## Exports

With **Background** on **Remove**, an export draws the subject alone in every frame, GIF and APNG included. It waits until every mask its range needs is made, with no time limit, and the Exporting sheet reads "Preparing" and the file's name until then. You can cancel it while it waits.

If a mask can't be made, the export fails with "Clip n's person masks could not be made: …" and writes no file. For a picture with **Subject** set to **Foreground**, the message says "foreground masks".

A single frame doesn't wait as long. **File ▸ Save Frame…** (<kbd>⌥⌘E</kbd>) waits up to 30 seconds for the masks it needs. If they aren't ready by then, it saves the frame with the clip whole, and a sheet titled "Saved without Remove Background" names the files drawn whole. An agent's [`render_frame`](/mcp/render-frame/) waits the same 30 seconds, and its reply names any clip it drew whole.

## Good to know

- Once its masks are made, a clip draws whole only when no frame it plays has a person. If the person leaves the picture for part of a clip, those frames have little or nothing to keep, so what's behind shows through.
- The recorder panel can do this for you. See [Polish when a recording lands](/recording/when-it-lands/).

## With an agent

An agent turns this on with `set_video`, as the checkbox does, and sets the same options there. See [Tools: picture and grade](/mcp/tools-set-video/#cutout).

`analyze_cutout` can wait up to 60 seconds for a clip's masks to settle, and it reports the subject's mean centre in the picture, which the app doesn't show. For a video, `get_media_analysis` says which stretches of the file hold a person. See [Tools: reading analysis](/mcp/tools-analysis/).

import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';

Frame Job can find who and what is in a clip's picture: faces, people and the parts the eye goes to first. Its framing tools use this to keep a subject in shot on a canvas of a different shape.

<AtAGlance
  menu={['Clip ▸ Follow Subject…', 'File ▸ Make Vertical Version…', 'View ▸ Show Subjects']}
  tools={['get_media_analysis', 'reframe_clip', 'make_vertical_version']}
  needs="Nothing. Apple's Vision framework does this on your Mac, with no key and no upload."
/>

## What is found

Frame Job samples the picture ten times a second of the file's own time, so a clip you've slowed down or sped up doesn't change what's found. It keeps three things from each sample.

### Faces

Each face's box, how it's turned, and how open the mouth is. Faces in a sample are listed from left to right. An agent reads them with `get_media_analysis`, kind `faces`. See [Faces](/projects/media-analysis/#faces) under media analysis.

### People

Each person's head and shoulders, as a box. A person's box can stand in for their face while the face can't be found. An agent reads people with `get_media_analysis`, kind `subjects`.

### Salient regions

The parts of the picture the eye goes to first, as boxes. In a talking-head shot that's usually the speaker, and on a slide it's often the text. An agent reads them with kind `subjects`, beside the people. See [People and salient regions](/projects/media-analysis/#people-and-salient-regions) under media analysis.

[Show Subjects](/framing/show-subjects/) draws all three over the preview, so you can see what Frame Job has to work with.

## Boxes, not people

Each sample stands alone. A box has no name, and nothing records that a box in one sample is the same person as a box in the next. Frame Job never puts a name to a face, and it doesn't recognise anyone.

[Follow Subject](/framing/follow-subject/#which-subject-it-follows) works out who's who for itself each time, from how the boxes overlap from one sample to the next. That reasoning isn't kept, and it stops at a shot change. Someone who leaves the shot for more than a second and comes back counts as someone new.

## When a file is analysed

Importing a file doesn't look for any of this. It's found when something asks for it:

- **Clip ▸ Follow Subject…**
- **File ▸ Make Vertical Version…**
- [**Clip ▸ Switch by Speaker…**](/multicam/one-microphone/), when it cuts from faces
- An agent, with `get_media_analysis`, `reframe_clip`, `make_vertical_version` or `switch_by_speaker`

Follow Subject, Make Vertical Version and `reframe_clip` ask only for the part of the file each clip plays, plus a second either side. **View ▸ Show Subjects** never asks, so turning it on costs nothing.

Analysis runs in the background and saves what it has found every 30 seconds, so stopping it keeps what's been saved. Asking again continues from there, and a part that's already been analysed isn't read again. What's found is kept in the project's cache. A change to the file, or a macOS update, means it's analysed again.

[On-device media analysis](/projects/media-analysis/#analysis-happens-on-demand) covers this in full, along with everything else Frame Job analyses on your Mac, including [the Analyzing sheet](/projects/media-analysis/#the-analyzing-sheet) and [how background jobs run](/projects/media-analysis/#analysis-runs-in-the-background).

## What uses it

| Feature | What it uses |
| --- | --- |
| [Follow Subject](/framing/follow-subject/) | Faces, people and salient regions, to frame the selected clips |
| [Make Vertical Version](/framing/make-vertical-version/) | The same, to frame a whole timeline on a tall or square canvas |
| [Follow the speaker in a vertical](/framing/follow-speaker/) | Faces and how open each mouth is, to match each microphone to a face |
| [Cut from faces with one microphone](/multicam/one-microphone/) | Faces and how open each mouth is, to tell who's talking |
| [Show Subjects](/framing/show-subjects/) | All three, drawn over the preview |

An agent can frame a clip with the same analysis. See [Reframe a clip (agents)](/framing/reframe-clip/).

## Word timings and word style

A caption page is a text clip with a time on each word. `set_text` edits these like any other text key. See [Edit captions](/captions/edit-captions/) and [Word caption styles](/captions/word-caption-styles/).

### Word timings

`words` is one `{start, end}` per whitespace-separated word of `content`, in ticks from the clip's start, or `[]` for an untimed page.

- When the list isn't empty, it must hold exactly one timing for each word. If not, the call answers "this text is timed word by word: 5 timings for 6 words".
- A change to `content` that alters the word count must send `words: []` in the same patch.
- A word's `end` can't come before its `start`, and each `start` can't come before the one before it. Two words can start together.
- A negative `start` is allowed. It means the word was already being said when the clip began.
- The times snap to the frame grid, so two words can land on one frame.

`words` can't be animated: `set_action_end` refuses it.

### Word style

`word_style` is `null` or an object. It replaces `animation` on the page.

| Key | What it does | Values | Default |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `mode` | `highlight` draws the whole page and picks out the active word. `build` makes words appear as they're said. | `highlight`, `build` | `highlight` |
| `active_color` | The active word's colour. | Four numbers | The text's colour |
| `active_scale` | Where the active word's pop settles. 1 is no pop. | 1 to 1.5 | 1 |
| `active_pill` | A rounded plate behind the active word. | `null`, or `{color, padding, radius, glide}` | No plate |
| `spoken_color` | The colour of words already said. | Four numbers | The text's colour |
| `upcoming_color` | The colour of words not yet said, in `highlight` mode. | Four numbers | The text's colour |
| `active_fill` | Fills the active word left to right as it's said. | `true`, `false` | `false` |
| `pause_dim` | How far the words and pill fade in a pause. | 0 to 1 | 0 |

**The pill.** Its `padding` and `radius` are fractions of the text's `size`, starting from 0.2 and 0.25, and its `color` starts as purple. `glide` set to `true` slides the pill from the word before to the active one over 0.2 s, or sooner when the next word starts sooner, instead of jumping.

**The fill.** `active_fill` runs from the word's start to its end, taking 0.6 s at most. The part already said draws in `active_color` and the rest in `upcoming_color`, or isn't drawn yet in `build` mode. In `highlight` mode it shows only where those two colours differ.

**The pause dim.** `pause_dim` fades the words and the pill to 1 minus `pause_dim` of their opacity, over 0.1 s each way, in a pause of 0.25 s or more. A pause runs from one word's end to the next one's start, before a late first word, and after the last word until the clip ends.

```json
{ "word_style": { "active_pill": { "glide": true }, "pause_dim": 0.5 } }
```

captions/assemblyai-privacy.mdx:54:While a delete is pending, Frame Job won't upload that file again, because the kept transcript is its only record of the delete still to be made. If that file's kept transcript still matches the run, it's used as normal. If the file needs a new upload, or you ticked [Transcribe again](/captions/assemblyai-transcription/#transcribe-again), it waits:
captions/assemblyai-transcription.mdx:112:Tick **Transcribe again:** ("ignore any cached transcript") to ignore what's kept and ask AssemblyAI again. It's off by default. Each file goes up in full and is billed again, and the summary line shows that price.
captions/assemblyai-transcription.mdx:120:The exception is work you've already paid for. When every file in the run has a current transcript, **Generate** works with no key, and the paragraph at the top changes to "Current cached transcripts will be used without an API key or network request." Ticking **Transcribe again:** ends that, because it needs a new upload.
captions/assemblyai-transcription.mdx:165:The words left out are um, uh, hmm, mhm, uh-huh, ah, huh, hm, m, er and erm, in any case and with any punctuation at their edges. The kept transcript still has them, which is what lets [Remove Filler Words](/cleanup/remove-filler-words/) find them later.
captions/generate-captions.mdx:57:| **Transcribe again:** | AssemblyAI only. "ignore any cached transcript". | Off |
captions/restyle-captions.mdx:35:- **AssemblyAI:** the cached transcript is reused whatever style you ask for, so nothing is uploaded and nothing is billed. That holds while the language, **Speakers:** and **Vocabulary:** match the transcript and **Transcribe again:** stays unticked. See [Transcribe with AssemblyAI](/captions/assemblyai-transcription/).
captions/word-caption-styles.mdx:116:| The sample words | The first words of the first clip's cached AssemblyAI transcript when there is one, otherwise "This is how it looks". |
cleanup/false-starts.mdx:47:The Assistant reads a file's saved AssemblyAI transcript when it has a current one. Otherwise it uses this Mac's own speech recogniser, which reads the whole file once and keeps the words in the project, so later reads are immediate.
cleanup/filler-transcripts.mdx:48:Pressing **Transcribe** only updates that file's saved transcript. It places no captions and adds no undo step.
cleanup/filler-transcripts.mdx:131:The saved transcript keeps every word as it was heard. Only captions filter them, which is how Remove Filler Words can still find them.
cleanup/remove-filler-words.mdx:89:- **Protection needs a transcript.** A cut is kept away from speech in another clip only when that clip's file has a saved AssemblyAI transcript, made with or without filler words. Speech on another unlocked track with no such transcript isn't protected, so check the shading there.
mcp/tools-captions.mdx:50:| `refresh` | boolean | No | AssemblyAI only. Ignore the kept transcript and upload again. Default false. |
mcp/tools-captions.mdx:136:You can't combine it with `replace` or with a look set to true, because nothing is placed. To place the captions, call again without `place`. With AssemblyAI the second call reuses the kept transcript and uploads nothing.
mcp/tools-captions.mdx:182:It needs a word style and `place` true. A style is only a display choice, so with AssemblyAI a kept transcript is reused whatever style you ask for, and restyling uploads nothing. Engine `apple` recognises the audio again.
mcp/tools-captions.mdx:280:| `language` | string | No | A language tag, such as `en-US`, for this Mac's recogniser only. By default this Mac's own language. A kept AssemblyAI transcript answers in its own language. |
mcp/tools-captions.mdx:291:| `engine` | `assemblyai` for a kept transcript, or `apple` for this Mac's recogniser. |
mcp/tools-captions.mdx:305:- There's no kept transcript and the language's speech model isn't installed. The tool never downloads one. A person installs it from **File ▸ Generate Captions…**.
mcp/tools-captions.mdx:322:`fillers_reported` says whether the transcript was made with filler words at all. It's false for every on-device read, and for a kept transcript made without them. A filler can then be in the audio and missing from `words`, and `note` says so. See [Transcripts for filler words](/cleanup/filler-transcripts/).
mcp/tools-captions.mdx:343:| `language` | string | No | A language tag, such as `en-US`, for this Mac's recogniser only. By default this Mac's own language. Each language is kept apart, and a kept AssemblyAI transcript answers in its own language. |
mcp/tools-clean-up.mdx:81:It reads only a saved AssemblyAI transcript that asked for filler words, and never uses the network, so it needs no key. Making that transcript does, see [`transcribe_for_fillers`](#transcribe_for_fillers).

captions/on-device-transcription.mdx:3:description: Turn the speech in your clips into captions with your Mac's own speech engine, with no key, no upload and no length limit, and install the languages you need.
captions/on-device-transcription.mdx:46:**Language:** lists every language this Mac's speech engine supports, by name, so the list differs from Mac to Mac. It opens on your Mac's own language, or the nearest one on the list.
captions/on-device-transcription.mdx:50:If the engine names no language at all, the pop-up reads **No on-device language** and the note under the summary says "This Mac's speech engine named no language with an on-device speech model. Reopen this sheet to ask it again." Setting **Engine:** to **AssemblyAI** still works in that state.
captions/generate-captions.mdx:87:- **On this Mac:** every language this Mac's recogniser supports. One with no model reads "— not installed", and choosing it puts a **Download** row under **Language:**. [Transcribe on this Mac](/captions/on-device-transcription/) covers installing one.
--- assistant lower
cleanup/remove-filler-words.mdx:99:- `transcribe_for_fillers` makes a transcript for one of those files. It's a paid upload, and the built-in assistant can't use it, so press **Transcribe** in the sheet yourself.
--- See Tools links
captions/assemblyai-transcription.mdx:177:See [Tools: captions and transcripts](/mcp/tools-captions/).
captions/delete-words.mdx:130:`get_timeline_transcript` reads the same words, up to 2,000 at a time, and says which can't be cut and why. Each word carries `cut_start` and `cut_end`, the range the tab would cut it by. One `ripple_delete_ranges` call from the first word's `cut_start` to the last word's `cut_end` cuts a run, and `set_range` can shade it first. `get_transcript` reads one clip's words. Neither reading tool uploads anything. If the voice model hasn't heard a file yet, the answer has a note saying its starts are still early, so ask again once it has. See [Tools: captions and transcripts](/mcp/tools-captions/).
captions/edit-captions.mdx:66:An agent can do two things here that the inspector can't: rewrite a page's word timings, and change its word style, both with `set_text`. Frame Job won't take a set of timings that doesn't have exactly one timing for each word of the page, so a change to the number of words has to clear the timings in the same call. Word timings can't be animated with an action. See [Word timings and word style](/mcp/tools-clip-properties/#word-timings-and-word-style).
captions/export-captions.mdx:68:It never guesses the track. With no track to write, it writes nothing and says so. With more than one and none named, it writes nothing and lists the candidates. A track it writes comes back through `import_captions` with every cue where it was. See [`export_captions`](/mcp/tools-captions/#export_captions).
captions/follow-the-transcript.mdx:66:`get_timeline_transcript` gives each word's time on the timeline, and `set_playhead` moves the playhead there. See [Tools: playhead, range and selection](/mcp/tools-view-state/).
captions/generate-captions.mdx:185:See [Tools: captions and transcripts](/mcp/tools-captions/).
captions/import-captions.mdx:94:`import_captions` can put the captions on a track that already exists, which the menu can't. Captions that would overlap something on that track are dropped, so leaving it to make a new track is the safer choice. It reports what landed and each malformed entry by line. See [Tools: captions and transcripts](/mcp/tools-captions/).
captions/on-device-transcription.mdx:96:An agent can't install a language, and `transcribe` never downloads one. A language tag that speech recognition doesn't know stops the call with "check the tag's spelling" and the tags it does know. A tag it knows with no model on this Mac stops the call with "A person has to install it", the steps in this sheet, and the languages that are ready. Nothing changes in either case. `get_transcript` works to the same rules. See [Tools: captions and transcripts](/mcp/tools-captions/).
captions/re-lay-captions.mdx:84:`relay_captions` does the same in the timeline or nest that's open, usually after `set_canvas` changes the size. It takes no arguments, and its result lists the tracks it re-laid and each kept track with its reason. When nothing can be re-laid, the call fails with those reasons, so an agent can tell you why the menu item is greyed out. See [Tools: captions and transcripts](/mcp/tools-captions/).
captions/shorten-pauses.mdx:65:`get_timeline_transcript` reads the same pauses, each with the range the tab would cut it by, and one `ripple_delete_ranges` call shortens one. `set_range` can shade that range first. An agent can pass several in that call, which makes them one undo step. See [Tools: captions and transcripts](/mcp/tools-captions/).
captions/subtitles.mdx:107:`transcribe` makes Subtitles (`style: subtitles`) unless it asks for another style, whatever the sheet last chose. See [Tools: captions and transcripts](/mcp/tools-captions/).
captions/transcript-tab.mdx:113:Agents read the same words with `get_timeline_transcript`. It returns the same notes as `notes` and the clips with no words as `no_words`, and its `tracks` and `language` do what **Words from** and **Language** do. See [`get_timeline_transcript`](/mcp/tools-captions/#get_timeline_transcript).
captions/transcript-words.mdx:61:An agent reads these words with `get_timeline_transcript`, or one clip's with `get_transcript`. When it reads a file on this Mac, the tab's **Stop** leaves that reading running. The Assistant's own **Stop** ends it, unless the tab is reading that file too, and nothing is saved from a stopped reading. See [Tools: captions and transcripts](/mcp/tools-captions/).
captions/word-caption-looks.mdx:92:It can change a placed page's word style with `set_text`. That covers highlighting or building word by word, the colours of the spoken word and of the words before and after it, a pop from 100% to 150%, the pill's colour, padding and corners, whether the pill slides, whether the word fills, and how far the page dims, from none to fully invisible. The sheet's dim is always half. A page changed this way is no longer one of the styles Frame Job makes, so [Re-lay Captions](/captions/re-lay-captions/#tracks-kept-as-placed) keeps its track as placed. See [Tools: text, shapes and clip names](/mcp/tools-clip-properties/).
captions/word-caption-looks.mdx:94:It can also ask for looks with `transcribe`, through `slide`, `fill` and `dim`, but each one is off unless it asks, never what the sheet last chose. Frame Job won't add a look to a style it wouldn't show on, or to captions it isn't placing. When it gives any of the three and the captions are placed, the result lists the looks that were on. See [Tools: captions and transcripts](/mcp/tools-captions/).
captions/word-caption-styles.mdx:131:`transcribe` makes word captions when it asks for a word style: `highlight`, `pill`, `karaoke`, `build` or `one_word`. It never uses the style the sheet last chose. See [Tools: captions and transcripts](/mcp/tools-captions/).
cleanup/filler-transcripts.mdx:154:The built-in [Assistant](/cleanup/false-starts/#the-assistant-wont-start-a-paid-transcription) can't use this tool. See [Tools: clean-up](/mcp/tools-clean-up/) for its arguments.
cleanup/how-cleanup-cuts-work.mdx:109:To reach inside a nest, an agent opens it with `set_scope` first, and the ranges are then in the nest's own time. See [Tools: clean-up](/mcp/tools-clean-up/) and [Editing inside a nest](/mcp/nests/).
cleanup/remove-filler-words.mdx:103:See [Tools: clean-up](/mcp/tools-clean-up/).
cleanup/remove-silences.mdx:84:`detect_silence` reads the same ranges the sheet would cut and changes nothing. Pass them to `ripple_delete_ranges` to make the cut. See [Tools: clean-up](/mcp/tools-clean-up/).
cleanup/voice-or-level.mdx:115:While the voice model can't be used, an agent that asks for Voice by name gets an error telling it to use Level. One that doesn't name a mode gets Level, with the same note the sheet shows. See [Tools: clean-up](/mcp/tools-clean-up/).
--- cut-out
mcp/tools-analysis.mdx:8:These two tools hand an agent what Frame Job finds in your media, so it can locate a cut, a face or a burst of laughter without watching the footage. `get_media_analysis` reads shots, faces, people, sounds and person masks for a file or a clip. `analyze_cutout` makes a cut-out clip's masks and says where they stand.
mcp/tools-analysis.mdx:158:Reports where Remove Background stands for cut-out clips and makes their masks now. It's the agent's version of **Status** and [**Analyze Now**](/effects/remove-background/#analyze-now) in the Clip tab's **Picture ▸ Background** section.
mcp/tools-analysis.mdx:160:A cut-out clip is one with Remove Background on, through **Clip ▸ Remove Background**, the section's checkbox, or `cutout` in [`set_video`](/mcp/tools-set-video/). A clip's masks are made as soon as that's set, so an agent needs this tool only to wait for them or to read how they went. A still picture counts, and its one frame is made from the picture itself.
mcp/tools-analysis.mdx:168:| `clips` | array of integers | No | The cut-out clips to answer for. Left out, every cut-out clip in the timeline or nest that's open, in timeline order. |
--- US/UK

app_defects.title: transcribe's clips description says project, but the call reads the open timeline or nest

app_defects.title: detect_fillers' dropped reason says 'crosses a transition' for a filler that only reaches the area around one

fixes.pages: mcp/tools-captions (Caption styles and paging) vs captions/word-caption-styles

fixes.now: A page holds for 0.5 s after its last word, or runs up to the next page if that starts sooner.
fixes.evidence: app/Sources/CaptionPages.swift:229: end = next - last.end < breakGap ? next : min(next, last.end + hold). A gap of 0.25 to 0.5 s also runs up to the next page. word-caption-styles was already right.
